passages.name: 2026年考研英语一 Text 1
passages.title: 基因组揭示驴的驯化起源
passages.genre: 说明文 · 生物与考古
passages.summary: 研究人员利用200多头驴的基因组，把驴的驯化追溯到约7000年前发生在东非的唯一一次驯化事件，比人类驯服马早约3000年；约2500年后，驴扩散到非洲大陆其他地区，并传入欧洲和亚洲。驯化的原因仍不清楚，但这一事件与撒哈拉沙漠不断扩大、日益干燥同时发生；史前人类驯服驴，可能是为了借助它们穿越这片不断扩张的沙漠。论文作者写道，了解驴的基因构成有助于揭示它们对人类历史的贡献，或许还能改善今后对它们的管理。

paras.en: For thousands of years, donkeys have been critical for propelling human civilizations forward.
paras.zh: 几千年来，驴对推动人类文明向前发展一直至关重要。

w.m: adj. 至关重要的；关键的

paras.en: They’ve helped pull wheeled vehicles, carry travelers and move goods across the world.
paras.zh: 它们一直在世界各地帮人拉轮式车辆、驮运旅人、运送货物。

paras.en: But where and when these animals first became intertwined with humans has been a mystery.
paras.zh: 但这些动物最初在何时何地与人类紧密联系在一起，一直是个谜。

w.m: 与……紧密联系在一起；与……交织在一起

paras.en: Now, researchers have used genomes of over 200 donkeys to trace their domestication back to a single event around 7,000 years ago in East Africa—about 3,000 years before humans tamed horses.
paras.zh: 如今，研究人员利用200多头驴的基因组，把驴的驯化追溯到大约7000年前发生在东非的唯一一次驯化事件——比人类驯服马早了约3000年。

paras.en: The team published their findings in the journal Science this month.
paras.zh: 研究团队本月在《科学》杂志上发表了研究结果。

paras.en: “Through their DNA, the animals are telling their history themselves,” co-author Samantha Brooks, an equine researcher at the University of Florida, says in a statement.
paras.zh: 论文合著者、佛罗里达大学的马科动物研究员萨曼莎·布鲁克斯在一份声明中说：“这些动物正通过自身的DNA，亲自讲述自己的历史。

paras.en: “We usually only get the human’s side of history through written accounts, but of course written history does not always record exactly how something happened.
paras.zh: 我们通常只能通过文字记载了解人类一方眼中的历史，但成文的历史当然并不总是确切地记录事情的经过。

paras.en: Looking at these DNA sequences, we get a biological testimony to the environment these animals lived in and the experiences they survived.”
paras.zh: 研究这些DNA序列，我们就能得到一份生物学证词，见证这些动物当年生活的环境，以及它们挺过的种种经历。”

paras.en: The researchers examined 207 genomes from modern donkeys living in 31 countries across the globe.
paras.zh: 研究人员分析了现代驴的207个基因组，这些驴生活在全球31个国家。

paras.en: They also looked at genomes from 15 wild equids and 31 earlier donkeys that lived between about 4,000 and 100 years ago.
paras.zh: 他们还研究了15头野生马科动物和31头更早时期的驴的基因组，后者生活在约4000年前至100年前。

w.m: adj. 较早的；更早时期的

paras.en: The team reconstructed the animals’ evolutionary tree and used computer models to pinpoint the domestication event when herders in Kenya and the Horn of Africa tamed wild asses.
paras.zh: 研究团队重建了这些动物的进化树，并利用计算机模型，精确定位了肯尼亚和非洲之角的牧民驯服野驴的那次驯化事件。

w.m: v. 精确定位；准确找出

paras.en: They then traced how the animals spread across the rest of the continent into Europe and Asia about 2,500 years later.
paras.zh: 随后，他们追溯了这些动物如何在约2500年后扩散到非洲大陆其他地区，进而传入欧洲和亚洲。

paras.en: Though it’s still unclear why the original domestication happened, Science News’ Freda Kreier reports that the event coincided with the Sahara growing larger and drier.
paras.zh: 尽管最初的驯化因何发生仍不清楚，但据《科学新闻》的弗雷达·克赖尔报道，这一事件与撒哈拉沙漠不断扩大、日益干燥同时发生。

paras.en: “Donkeys are champions when it comes to carrying stuff and are good at going through deserts,” co-author Ludovic Orlando, an evolutionary biologist at Paul Sabatier University in France, tells the publication.
paras.zh: 论文合著者、法国保罗·萨巴蒂埃大学的进化生物学家卢多维克·奥兰多对该刊表示：“说到驮东西，驴是一等一的好手，而且它们很擅长穿越沙漠。”

paras.en: Prehistoric humans may have tamed donkeys to help navigate the expanding Sahara.
paras.zh: 史前人类驯服驴，可能是为了借助它们穿越不断扩大的撒哈拉沙漠。

w.m: v. 穿越；（在……中）找到路线
adj. 不断扩大的；日益扩张的

paras.en: Researchers say these findings could help put donkeys in the spotlight.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，这些研究结果或许有助于让驴成为关注的焦点。

paras.en: The animals could benefit from more research: Currently, there are no published genomes from donkeys located south of the Equator in Africa.
paras.zh: 驴或许能从更多研究中受益：目前，非洲赤道以南地区的驴还没有任何已发表的基因组。

w.m: adj. 已发表的；已出版的

paras.en: But understanding where the animals were first domesticated could guide archaeologists to a narrow region to search for insights about the original tamed donkeys.
paras.zh: 不过，弄清驴最初是在哪里被驯化的，或许能把考古学家引向一个范围较小的区域，在那里寻求对最早被驯服的那批驴的新认识。

paras.en: Not only does understanding the equines’ genetic makeup help reveal their contribution to human history, but it also might improve their management in the future, as climate change alters the planet’s environment, write the authors.
paras.zh: 论文作者写道，了解这些马科动物的基因构成，不仅有助于揭示它们对人类历史的贡献，而且随着气候变化改变地球环境，或许还能改善今后对它们的管理。

w.m: 不仅（置于句首时句子部分倒装，与后文 but…also 呼应）

passages.name: 2026年考研英语一 Text 2
passages.title: 好莱坞衰落，加州应加大激励力度
passages.genre: 议论文 · 影视产业与经济
passages.summary: 美术指导工会暂停了一项培训计划，并声明无法昧着良心鼓励人们从事这一行，这是对好莱坞衰落的反应。影视制作自20世纪50年代起就一直在从好莱坞流失，其他地区稳步加大激励力度；流媒体催生的“巅峰电视”一度让洛杉矶撑了下来，但2022年过后，流媒体平台的重心转向盈利，新剧集的数量随之下降。作者认为，如果南加州的影视制作量跌到临界水平以下且持续太久，人才和收入都会流失，因此呼吁加州电影委员会、FilmLA等政府机构趁早行动，大幅改善激励措施。

paras.en: There’s no business like show business—but in Los Angeles, it feels like there’s no business at all.
paras.zh: 没有哪一行比得上演艺业，可在洛杉矶，感觉根本就没有生意可做。

paras.en: If that sounds melodramatic, consider this: The Art Directors Guild, a labor union representing about 3,000 film workers, has suspended a training program and issued a statement explaining that “we cannot in good conscience encourage you to pursue our profession.”
paras.zh: 如果这听起来有些夸张，那不妨看看这件事：代表约3000名电影从业者的美术指导工会已经暂停了一项培训计划，并发表声明解释说：“我们无法昧着良心鼓励你们从事我们这一行。”

paras.en: This is a reaction to Hollywood’s decline, which is reaching a critical point for the industry and Southern California.
paras.zh: 这是对好莱坞衰落作出的反应，而对这个行业和南加州来说，这种衰落正走到一个临界点。

paras.en: Production has been slipping away from Hollywood since the 1950s, but the effects have never been more apparent than at present.
paras.zh: 自20世纪50年代以来，影视制作就一直在从好莱坞流失，但其影响从未像现在这样明显。

paras.en: Other regions in the United States, Canada and Europe have steadily increased incentives to attract TV shows and movies, leaving California in the dust.
paras.zh: 美国、加拿大和欧洲的其他地区一直在稳步加大激励力度，以吸引电视节目和电影，把加州远远甩在了后面。

w.m: n. 激励（措施）；优惠政策

paras.en: Georgia offers up to 30% in transferable tax credits on film and TV production costs, including an additional 10% increase on the base tax credit if the project includes a Georgia promotional logo.
paras.zh: 佐治亚州按影视制作成本提供最高达30%的可转让税收抵免，其中，如果项目带有佐治亚州的宣传标识，还可在基础税收抵免之上额外提高10%。

paras.en: Even as California lost a huge volume of production to other locations, there was still plenty of film production taking place in Los Angeles before this year.
paras.zh: 即便加州有大量影视制作流失到了其他地方，今年之前，洛杉矶仍有大量影视作品在拍摄。

paras.en: We were kept afloat by “peak TV”—the glut of content that was required by the explosion of streaming services.
paras.zh: 让我们撑下来的是“巅峰电视”，即流媒体服务爆炸式增长所需的、多到泛滥的内容。

w.m: 巅峰电视（剧集产量空前高涨的时期）

paras.en: But 2022 was the peak of peak TV.
paras.zh: 但2022年是“巅峰电视”的顶峰。

w.m: 巅峰电视（剧集产量空前高涨的时期）

paras.en: Back then platforms such as Netflix, Amazon and Apple TV hemorrhaged billions of dollars to generate content to attract new subscribers, resulting in 633 scripted series being released that year.
paras.zh: 当时，Netflix、亚马逊和Apple TV等平台为了产出内容以吸引新订户，烧掉了数十亿美元，结果那一年推出了633部有剧本的剧集。

w.m: v. 大量耗费（资金）；大出血
adj. 有剧本的；剧本类的

paras.en: As the streamers’ emphasis changed from subscriber growth to profitability, prices for the services went up and the number of new shows went down to 481 released in 2023, with the number expected to dip into the 300s within a few years.
paras.zh: 随着流媒体平台的重心从订户增长转向盈利，这些服务的价格上涨了，2023年推出的新剧集数量则降至481部，预计几年之内还会跌到300多部。

paras.en: If productions in Southern California dip below a critical level for too long, the industry’s essential talent will drift away along with enormous sums of revenue.
paras.zh: 如果南加州的影视制作量跌到临界水平以下，而且持续太久，这个行业不可或缺的人才就会逐渐流失，巨额收入也会随之流走。

w.m: adj. 不可或缺的；必要的

paras.en: Persuading studios to film here would become much more challenging if we couldn’t offer a deep bench of local film workers, on-screen talent and local businesses that support the entertainment industry.
paras.zh: 如果我们拿不出一大批本地电影从业者、幕前人才和为娱乐产业提供配套服务的本地企业，要说服制片公司来这里拍摄就会困难得多。

w.m: n. 制片公司；电影公司
adj. 困难的；有挑战性的
一大批（可随时调用的）……；雄厚的……储备

paras.en: That’s why the California Film Commission and its Los Angeles counterpart, FilmLA, now should act, before it’s too late.
paras.zh: 正因如此，加州电影委员会及其在洛杉矶的对应机构FilmLA现在就应该采取行动，以免为时已晚。

w.m: 这就是……的原因；正因如此
n. 对应的机构；对等方
以免为时已晚；趁还来得及

paras.en: These agencies and other government bodies should dramatically improve incentives to keep our current shows and attract new productions to Los Angeles.
paras.zh: 这些机构和其他政府部门应当大幅改善激励措施，以留住我们现有的剧集，并把新的影视项目吸引到洛杉矶来。

w.m: n. 激励措施；优惠政策

paras.en: Let’s go on with the show…and make sure the show doesn’t go on without us.
paras.zh: 让演出继续下去吧……同时要确保，这场演出不会撇下我们继续上演。

passages.name: 2026年考研英语一 Text 3
passages.title: 广播带来的意外之喜正在消退
passages.genre: 议论文 · 科技与社会
passages.summary: 无线电广播的先驱们把它视为送给全体民众的礼物；一本新书和一场展览记录了1922年至1939年间广播如何改变日常生活；总的来说，收音机当年是受人欢迎的。在数字时代到来之前的80多年里，线性播出的谈话类广播一直带来意外之喜，但作者认为，广播的这种意外之喜正在消退：如今智能手机用户自己选择听什么、什么时候听，而无限的选择会促使人们退缩到小众兴趣和合自己心意的观点里。作者指出，创新总会发生，但与技术相关的社会习惯确实发生变化时，值得留意，也值得问一问是否要对其稍加控制，或者保护好最年幼的孩子们。

paras.en: The pioneers of wireless saw it as a gift to all the people.
paras.zh: 无线电广播的先驱们把它视为送给全体民众的礼物。

w.m: n. 无线电广播；收音机

paras.en: Sir John Reith said that it would end “isolation of the spirit” and rejoiced: “It does not matter how many thousands may be listening; there is always enough for others…the genius and the fool, the wealthy and the poor listen simultaneously.”
paras.zh: 约翰·里斯爵士说，无线电广播将终结“精神上的孤立”，并欣喜地表示：“收听的人不管有几千还是几万，都无关紧要；总有足够的份留给其他人……天才和傻瓜、富人和穷人同时在听。”

w.m: adj. 富有的（the wealthy 指富人）

paras.en: Between two great wars this technological innovation built a new kind of national consciousness.
paras.zh: 在两次大战之间的那些年里，这项技术创新塑造了一种新型的国民意识。

paras.en: Opening this week, a book and exhibition curated by Beaty Rubens at the Bodleian in Oxford records how radio changed everyday life from 1922 to 1939.
paras.zh: 本周，由比蒂·鲁本斯策划的一本书和一场展览在牛津博德利图书馆推出，记录了1922年至1939年间广播如何改变日常生活。

paras.en: She draws on letters, diaries and fiction, and a 1939 field notebook of verbatim audience research by Winifred Gill.
paras.zh: 她取材于书信、日记和小说，以及威妮弗雷德·吉尔1939年的一本实地调查笔记，里面是逐字记下的听众调查。

w.m: 实地调查笔记；田野笔记
adj. 逐字的；一字不差的

paras.en: There’s fun in testimonies of people enjoying the sheer newness.
paras.zh: 人们说起自己如何享受这份十足的新鲜感，这些亲身讲述读来饶有趣味。

paras.en: A cartoon mocks a group failing to converse because they’re all in headphones.
paras.zh: 一幅漫画嘲讽一群人因为都戴着耳机而无法交谈。

paras.en: People report that broadcast music made workmen whistle new tunes.
paras.zh: 据人们讲述，广播播放的音乐让工人们用口哨吹起了新曲子。

paras.en: A woman says there have been fewer street fights since the arrival of the wireless but also less stopping and “talking on the brush handle”.
paras.zh: 一位女士说，自从收音机出现，街头斗殴少了，但人们停下脚步、“拄着扫帚把聊天”的时候也少了。

w.m: n. 收音机；无线电广播

paras.en: By and large the wireless was welcome.
paras.zh: 总的来说，收音机是受人欢迎的。

w.m: n. 收音机；无线电广播

paras.en: I loved the man from the Thirties research who found that wireless suddenly offered “a lot of variety…things I thought I’d never be interested in…ice hockey perhaps”.
paras.zh: 20世纪30年代那项调查里有一位男士，我很喜欢他：他发现收音机一下子提供了“种类繁多的东西……那些我原以为自己永远不会感兴趣的东西……也许是冰球吧”。

w.m: n. 收音机；无线电广播

paras.en: True: for more than 80 pre-digital years, linear speech broadcasting brought the gift of serendipity, random enlivening of a car journey or dull manual task.
paras.zh: 的确如此：在数字时代到来之前的80多年里，线性播出的谈话类广播带来了意外之喜这份礼物，让一次驾车出行或一件枯燥的体力活偶然间变得生动有趣。

w.m: adj. （用于句首表示承认）的确；诚然
adj. （广播）线性播出的（按节目表依次播出，非点播）
n. 意外之喜；机缘巧合
n. 使……生动有趣；增添生气

paras.en: In my own book about radio I recorded how, on one drive, “I caught up with the news, learnt some 17th-century history, and was startlingly educated by an unpretentious programme on the history of the stethoscope.”
paras.zh: 我在自己那本讲广播的书里，记录了有一次开车途中的经历：“我了解了最新新闻，学了些17世纪的历史，还从一档朴实无华、讲听诊器历史的节目里长了见识，收获大得惊人。”

w.m: adv. 惊人地；出人意料地
adj. 朴实无华的；不做作的

paras.en: But radio’s enriching serendipity is ebbing.
paras.zh: 但广播那种让生活更丰富的意外之喜正在消退。

w.m: adj. 使丰富的；使充实的
n. 意外之喜；机缘巧合

paras.en: With multiple networks and countless podcasts, a smartphone user selects what to hear and when.
paras.zh: 有了众多广播网和数不清的播客，智能手机用户自己选择听什么、什么时候听。

paras.en: And while it is wonderful to take a walk with anything in your headphones, infinite choice encourages us to shrink into niche interests and sympathetic beliefs.
paras.zh: 而且，散步时耳机里想听什么就听什么，虽然很美妙，但无限的选择会促使我们退缩到小众兴趣和合自己心意的观点里。

w.m: 促使某人做；鼓励某人做
adj. 小众的；针对特定群体的
adj. 合自己心意的；与自己观点一致的

paras.en: A hundred years on from Marconi and Reith, is the art of mere listening endangered?
paras.zh: 从马可尼和里斯那时算起，一百年过去了，单纯聆听这门艺术是否已经濒危？

w.m: adj. 濒危的；受到威胁的

paras.en: Some will say the audiobook boom revives it, though I suppose you can then worry about the decline of reading.
paras.zh: 有人会说，有声书的热潮让这门艺术重获新生，不过我想，这样一来，你又可以担心阅读的衰落了。

w.m: v. 使复兴；使重获生机

paras.en: But inventions shape all of us and it is worth noticing when techno-social habits do change, and asking whether to control them a bit or shield the youngest.
paras.zh: 但发明塑造着我们每一个人；当与技术相关的社会习惯确实发生变化时，值得加以留意，并问一问：是否要对这些习惯稍加控制，或者保护好最年幼的孩子们。

w.m: adj. 技术与社会的；与技术相关的社会（行为）的
v. （用于加强语气）确实；的确

paras.en: Whatever we do, innovation will happen.
paras.zh: 无论我们怎么做，创新总会发生。

w.m: pron. 无论什么；不管什么

paras.en: Today we fret about the isolating culture of smartphone-staring and selfie-vanity, but already in 1939 there was that lady regretting how, when all her street got wirelesses, it lost the neighbourly habit of “talking on the brush handle”.
paras.zh: 如今，我们为盯着智能手机、靠自拍满足虚荣心这种使人孤立的文化而发愁，但早在1939年，那位女士就已惋惜地说起，等到她那条街家家户户都有了收音机，整条街便失去了“拄着扫帚把聊天”这一邻里习惯。

w.m: n. 盯着智能手机看（的行为）
n. 靠自拍满足的虚荣心
adj. 邻里之间的；睦邻的

paras.en: It’s enough to make a person put down the smartphone and go out front with a yard broom.
paras.zh: 这简直让人想放下智能手机，拿上一把扫院子用的扫帚走到门前去。

passages.name: 2026年考研英语一 Text 4
passages.title: 让有益的火回归森林
passages.genre: 说明文 · 环境与生态
passages.summary: 汤姆·斯韦特南通过研究树木年轮发现，早在欧洲殖民者来到北美大陆之前几百年，那里就反复发生火灾；越来越多的研究表明，频繁发生的低烈度火灾让许多生态系统更加健康。上个月发表的一项研究以北美树木年轮火疤网络（NAFSN）为基础，发现各采样点经历的火灾次数还不到不灭火情况下预期次数的四分之一。专家凯莉·马丁认为，人们必须让有益的火回到需要它的地方；研究表明，计划烧除能让此后的野火没那么猛烈，但专家们表示，气候变化正使这一策略更具挑战性。

paras.en: When Tom Swetnam joined the U.S. Forest Service in the 1970s, his mandate was to “put everything out,” he recalled.
paras.zh: 汤姆·斯韦特南回忆说，20世纪70年代加入美国林务局时，他的任务是“全部扑灭”。

paras.en: But when Swetnam enrolled in graduate school at the University of Arizona’s Laboratory of Tree-Ring Research, he was surprised to find a record of repeated blazes dating back hundreds of years before European colonists arrived on the continent.
paras.zh: 但斯韦特南在亚利桑那大学树木年轮研究实验室读研究生时，惊讶地发现了反复发生火灾的记录，这些记录可以追溯到欧洲殖民者来到这片大陆之前几百年。

paras.en: Some of the trees he analyzed bore more than 20 fire scars among their rings.
paras.zh: 他分析过的树木中，有些在年轮之间留有超过20处火疤。

w.m: 火疤（树木被火烧后留下的伤疤）

paras.en: The fact that fires happened so often meant they couldn’t have been severe enough to kill most trees.
paras.zh: 火灾发生得如此频繁，这一事实意味着，这些火不可能猛烈到足以烧死大多数树木。

paras.en: Instead, a growing body of research showed that frequent, low-severity fires made many ecosystems healthier.
paras.zh: 相反，越来越多的研究表明，频繁发生的低烈度火灾让许多生态系统变得更健康。

paras.en: They rid the forest of dead and sick trees, reducing competition and curbing the spread of disease.
paras.zh: 这些火清除了森林中枯死和患病的树木，从而减少了竞争，遏制了疾病的传播。

paras.en: Because flammable material couldn’t build up on the landscape, blazes tended to move slowly and peter out when they reached the footprints of previous burns.
paras.zh: 由于易燃物无法在这片土地上积聚，火往往蔓延缓慢，烧到以往的过火区域时就会逐渐熄灭。

paras.en: In 2022, Swetnam and other scientists teamed up to compile a database of fire-scarred trees from across the continent.
paras.zh: 2022年，斯韦特南和其他科学家联手编制了一个数据库，收录了这片大陆各地留有火疤的树木。

paras.en: Their North American tree-ring fire-scar network (NAFSN) provided the basis for a study published last month.
paras.zh: 他们的北美树木年轮火疤网络（NAFSN）为上个月发表的一项研究提供了基础。

paras.en: In the study, the researchers compared the historical fire cadence with the wildfires recorded over the past few decades, and uncovered a striking shortfall.
paras.zh: 在这项研究中，研究人员将历史上的火灾节律与过去几十年记录的野火相比较，发现了一个惊人的缺口。

paras.en: The NAFSN sites experienced less than a quarter of the number of fires that would have been expected without fire suppression.
paras.zh: NAFSN各采样点经历的火灾次数，还不到不灭火情况下预期次数的四分之一。

paras.en: This deficit is a testament to the effectiveness of modern firefighting, said Kelly Martin, a past president of the International Association of Wildland Fire.
paras.zh: 曾任国际荒野火灾协会主席的凯莉·马丁说，这一缺口证明了现代灭火工作的成效。

paras.en: “Yet the combined consequences of suppression and climate change have eroded humanity’s ability to suppress fires, particularly those that ignite under the most dangerous weather conditions.”
paras.zh: “然而，灭火与气候变化共同造成的后果，已经削弱了人类扑灭火灾的能力，尤其是扑灭那些在最危险的天气条件下燃起的火灾。”

paras.en: To prevent entire ecosystems from going up in smoke, Martin said, people must bring healthy fire back to places that need it.
paras.zh: 马丁说，为了防止整个生态系统付之一炬，人们必须把有益的火带回需要它的地方。

paras.en: At Yosemite National Park, Martin oversaw the use of what is known as prescribed burns to make the landscape more resilient.
paras.zh: 在约塞米蒂国家公园，马丁曾负责实施一种名为计划烧除的做法，以使这片土地更有韧性。

w.m: 被称为……的（事物）；人们所说的
计划烧除（有计划的人为火烧）
adj. 有韧性的；恢复力强的

paras.en: These fires were carefully planned and intentionally ignited during periods when weather kept the blazes easy to control, and helped eliminate some of the fuel that had built up around the park’s important facilities.
paras.zh: 这些火经过精心规划，在天气让火势易于控制的时段有意点燃，并帮助清除了公园重要设施周围积聚起来的部分可燃物。

paras.en: Research shows that these prescribed burns make subsequent wildfires less severe, even if later fires happen under the most dangerous weather conditions.
paras.zh: 研究表明，这些计划烧除能让此后的野火没那么猛烈，即使后来的火灾发生在最危险的天气条件下也是如此。

paras.en: Yet even as scientists and public officials increasingly agree on the need for more fires in our forests, climate change is making this tactic more challenging, experts said.
paras.zh: 然而专家们表示，尽管科学家和政府官员越来越一致地认为森林需要更多的火，气候变化却正使这一策略更具挑战性。

w.m: adj. 有挑战性的；困难的

paras.en: “It’s a double-edged sword because wildfires are getting more severe and larger under climate change and we need this work even more, but then the work gets more challenging,” said Susan Prichard, a fire ecologist at the University of Washington.
paras.zh: 华盛顿大学的火生态学家苏珊·普里查德说：“这是一把双刃剑，因为在气候变化的影响下，野火正变得更猛烈、规模更大，我们就更需要这项工作，可是这项工作也变得更有挑战性了。”

w.m: adv. （修饰比较级）更加；甚至更
adj. 有挑战性的；困难的

paras.en: You don’t need to get out more.
If, like most business people, you spend your life dashing from office to plane, train to home, boardroom to washroom, what you really need to do is stay in more, sit down—and read a book.
But for the most part, this isn’t what the business community does.
I have yet to meet a chief executive who reads regularly.
Many skip newspapers, and magazines are a stretch.
They don’t have time, they say.
It’s inefficient; they can get the information they need from those around them.
At a pinch, they might pick up a business book before a long flight, in the hope that, like a cookbook, it will provide a foolproof recipe.
Some are drawn to what I think of as “business car crash” books—the stories of Theranos, Purdue, or WeWork.
But outside those narrow pools of interest, a vast ocean awaits, bountiful with simmering ideas, mental adventure and imaginative refreshment.
We are living through a golden age of science writing, so lucid and accessible that even lay readers can relish the unpredictability of discovery.
Daunted by uncertainty?
Stand in the shoes of scientists and witness the degree to which breakthroughs emerge from accidents, conflict and sheer mental stamina.
“We are never sure of anything,” says the physicist (and writer) Carlo Rovelli.
Read fiction.
Any fiction.
Free yourself from algorithms and choose—anything.
You don’t need technology for an immersive experience—just surrender to narratives across time and place.
Modern (Sebastian Barry or Olga Tokarczuk), classic (Virginia Woolf or James Baldwin) or genre (Stephen King, Margaret Atwood, Georges Simenon)—it doesn’t matter.
Fiction invites you to loiter unseen in the lives of others.
We are living through a golden age of translation too, so you can go anywhere in time or place.
And just read a single poem.
In his Oxford lectures, Seamus Heaney argued that a poem draws a picture of reality, a “glimpsed alternative” that sets up a contradiction with your own, in ways little and large.
The negotiation, between you and it, is the heart of the matter.
What does the poet see that you don’t?
What does the difference mean?
It could be one of the best conversations you ever have.
Forget self-help books; reading is self-help in action.
Neuroscientists have been at pains to demonstrate that the pleasure a book provides isn’t indulgence; it’s good for you.
Reading will keep you better informed about the world but it can also improve our tech-shattered ability to concentrate.
Standing in the shoes of others fine-tunes our social understanding, useful as we struggle to understand friends, neighbours, customers and co-workers.
Different parts of our brain engage as we simulate scenes, characters and mental states.
Our imagination—remember that?—is rekindled.
Reading has also been found to make us more helpful, to reduce bias, and even to increase longevity—something we will enjoy all the more if we have a good book in our hands.
(And yes, all these benefits are more closely associated with physical books than digital ones.)
It is undoubtedly true that all work and no play really does make Jack, or Jill, dull.
The cure is right at hand.
Reading is cheap, easy and, most important, it’s fun.
Liberate your imagination this year.

passages.name: 2026年考研英语二 Text 1
passages.title: 被忽视、被低估的公共图书馆
passages.genre: 议论文 · 社会与文化
passages.summary: 作者受文化部委托，对英格兰公共图书馆开展了独立评估，发现现实与人们印象中积满灰尘、老派过时的图书馆大不相同：图书馆的数量是麦当劳门店的两倍多，除书籍外还提供就业咨询、语言课程等众多服务，而且不收任何费用。然而，图书馆常常被忽视，没有得到应有的重视；到馆人次总体下降，随着地方政府持续承受财政压力，许多图书馆举步维艰。作者认为，要为子孙后代保护好图书馆，就必须提高人们对图书馆及其工作的认识。评估报告建议：开展全国性的品牌宣传活动；重新推行一项计划，让会员在全国任何一家图书馆都能使用自己的借书证；让儿童自动获得会员资格。如果不利用图书馆，我们最终就会失去它们。

paras.en: Ask people about public libraries and a certain image springs to mind: dusty, old-fashioned, the sort of place you enjoyed as a child but, rather like a British seaside town, would you go there now?
paras.zh: 向人们问起公共图书馆，他们脑海中就会浮现出某种印象：积满灰尘，老派过时，是你小时候喜欢去的那种地方，可如今你还会去吗？在这一点上，图书馆倒颇像英国的海滨小镇。

w.m: 浮现在脑海中；突然想到

paras.en: And anyway—aren’t they all closing?
paras.zh: 况且，图书馆不是都在关闭吗？

paras.en: The reality is startlingly different, as I discovered when the culture department commissioned me to conduct an independent review of English public libraries, published yesterday.
paras.zh: 现实情况与此大不相同，令人吃惊。文化部委托我对英格兰公共图书馆开展了一项独立评估，评估报告已于昨天发布，我正是在评估中发现了这一点。

w.m: adv. 令人吃惊地；惊人地

paras.en: As I visited libraries up and down the country, I was surprised to learn there are more than twice the number of libraries (2,892) as there are branches of McDonald’s.
paras.zh: 在全国各地走访图书馆时，我惊讶地得知，图书馆的数量（2892座）是麦当劳门店的两倍多。

paras.en: Enter any one of them and you will find a hive of activity.
paras.zh: 随便走进其中任何一家，你都会发现那里一派繁忙热闹的景象。

paras.en: While books are, and should always be, at the heart of any library, a multitude of other services are offered: employment advice, language classes or digital access and support.
paras.zh: 虽然书籍是任何一家图书馆的核心，也理应永远如此，但图书馆还提供众多其他服务：就业咨询、语言课程，或是数字接入与支持。

paras.en: There are libraries with business and intellectual property centres, which can help business owners and entrepreneurs.
paras.zh: 有的图书馆设有商业与知识产权中心，可以为企业主和创业者提供帮助。

paras.en: Many have nurses on site to carry out basic health checks, with a link to the GP’s surgery.
paras.zh: 许多图书馆有护士驻馆，负责进行基本的健康检查，并与全科医生诊所保持联系。

paras.en: There are libraries where young people can borrow a Fifa-standard football free.
paras.zh: 在有些图书馆，年轻人可以免费借到符合国际足联标准的足球。

w.m: adj. 符合国际足联标准的

paras.en: In return for all of this, you’ll be asked for precisely nothing.
paras.zh: 享受这一切，图书馆不会向你索取任何回报——一丁点儿都不要。

w.m: adv. （加强语气）完全；不折不扣地

paras.en: There will be no charge and you will never be asked to justify or explain yourself; you will simply be welcomed in, offered help if you need it, and left alone if you do not.
paras.zh: 这里不会收取任何费用，也绝不会有人要你为自己辩解或解释什么；这里只会欢迎你进门，你需要帮助就有人帮你，不需要也没人打扰你。

w.m: 不打扰某人；不理会某人

paras.en: There is no other institution, public or private, that can say the same.
paras.zh: 无论公立还是私营，再没有别的机构能这样说了。

w.m: 也能这么说；说同样的话

paras.en: Yet still our libraries are often overlooked and underappreciated.
paras.zh: 然而，我们的图书馆仍常常被忽视，没有得到应有的重视。

w.m: adj. 未得到充分重视的

paras.en: There is an overall decline in visits and many are struggling as local authorities come under continued financial pressure.
paras.zh: 到馆人次总体呈下降趋势；随着地方政府持续承受财政压力，许多图书馆举步维艰。

w.m: v. 艰难维持；苦苦挣扎

paras.en: The number of libraries that have closed since 2010 is disputed.
paras.zh: 自2010年以来关闭的图书馆有多少，存在争议。

paras.en: An annual survey by the Chartered Institute of Public Finance and Accountancy puts it at nearly 800 across the UK; official statistics held by the Arts Council record 230 in England.
paras.zh: 英国特许公共财务与会计协会的一项年度调查估计，全英国关闭的图书馆接近800座；而据艺术委员会掌握的官方统计数据记录，英格兰关闭了230座。

paras.en: It is, of course, 230 libraries too many.
paras.zh: 当然，即便是230座，也已经太多了。

paras.en: So if we are to protect our libraries for future generations, we must raise awareness of them and the work they do.
paras.zh: 因此，如果我们要为子孙后代保护好图书馆，就必须提高人们对图书馆及其所做工作的认识。

paras.en: The review recommends a national branding campaign to give libraries a stronger physical presence, the reintroduction of a scheme to enable members to use their card in any library in the country, and automatic memberships for children.
paras.zh: 评估报告建议：开展一场全国性的品牌宣传活动，增强图书馆在现实中的存在感；重新推行一项计划，让会员可以在全国任何一家图书馆使用自己的借书证；让儿童自动获得会员资格。

w.m: n. 品牌推广；品牌塑造
n. 重新推行；重新引入
n. 会员资格；会员身份

paras.en: If we don’t use them, we will end up losing them.
paras.zh: 如果我们不去利用图书馆，最终就会失去它们。

paras.en: And those who haven’t been to a library for some time may be surprised by what they find.
paras.zh: 而那些有一段时间没去过图书馆的人，去了可能会对眼前所见感到惊讶。

passages.name: 2026年考研英语二 Text 2
passages.title: 职场用AI，须防机密外泄
passages.genre: 议论文 · 科技与职场
passages.summary: 研究显示，英国约五分之一的员工像对待朋友一样与AI交谈，许多人会透露敏感、有时甚至高度机密的信息，而超过三分之一的人没有意识到AI平台未必善于保密，这对企业来说令人担忧。25%的雇主已决定彻底禁用AI或规范其使用，但仍有员工违反规定，其中约63%的人称使用AI能提高他们的工作效率。作者认为，雇主需要像对待其他任何形式的数据共享或存储一样谨慎管理AI工具；通过在企业内部建立数字责任文化，我们可以让AI在帮助我们的同时不泄露秘密。

paras.en: According to our research, around one in five workers in the UK talk to AI like a friend, looking for guidance on personal and professional problems.
paras.zh: 我们的研究显示，在英国，约五分之一的员工像对待朋友一样与AI交谈，就个人和工作上的问题向它寻求指点。

w.m: 五分之一；每五个中有一个

paras.en: Our data shows that engaging with AI like this can leave us feeling heard and less isolated.
paras.zh: 我们的数据显示，像这样与AI互动，能让我们感到有人在倾听自己，也没那么孤单了。

w.m: v. 使（处于某种状态）；让
感到有人倾听；觉得被理解

paras.en: But, with this newfound connection, many of us share sensitive, sometimes highly confidential information, and over a third of people don’t realise that AI platforms may not be very good at keeping our secrets…secret.
paras.zh: 但有了这种新建立起来的情感联系，我们中许多人会透露敏感信息，有时还包括高度机密的信息，而超过三分之一的人没有意识到，AI平台可能不太擅长让我们的秘密……始终是秘密。

w.m: adj. 新近建立的；新得到的
n. 联系；（情感上的）关联

paras.en: For businesses, the implications are worrying.
paras.zh: 对企业而言，由此带来的影响令人担忧。

paras.en: Consider Microsoft Copilot, for example.
paras.zh: 就拿微软的Copilot来说吧。

paras.en: It grants Microsoft broad rights to the data inputted or outputted by any user—rights to use this data in any way it sees fit; it can even share it with third parties.
paras.zh: 对于任何用户输入或输出的数据，它都赋予微软广泛的权利：微软有权按自认为合适的任何方式使用这些数据，甚至可以与第三方共享。

paras.en: This means that any sensitive business information could potentially be exposed to the world.
paras.zh: 这意味着，任何敏感的商业信息都有可能暴露在世人面前。

paras.en: Employers are taking note and taking action.
paras.zh: 雇主们正在留意这一问题，也在采取行动。

paras.en: According to our research, 25% have decided to either outright ban AI or regulate its use within their organisations.
paras.zh: 我们的研究显示，25%的雇主已决定在各自的机构内要么彻底禁用AI，要么规范其使用。

paras.en: But even with these policies in place, some employees choose to break the rules.
paras.zh: 但即便这些政策已经落实，还是有一些员工选择违反规定。

paras.en: They have their reasons—around 63% of them report that using AI increases their productivity, and some even feel AI offers more help than their human colleagues.
paras.zh: 他们有自己的理由：其中约63%的人称，使用AI能提高他们的工作效率；有些人甚至觉得，AI提供的帮助比人类同事还要多。

paras.en: The situation presents a delicate balance between leveraging AI for its productivity gains and risking confidential data exposure.
paras.zh: 这种局面带来了一个微妙的平衡问题：一边是利用AI来提升工作效率，一边是冒着机密数据外泄的风险。

w.m: adj. 微妙的；需小心处理的

paras.en: Employers need to manage AI tools with the same level of care as any other form of data sharing or storage.
paras.zh: 雇主在管理AI工具时，需要像对待其他任何形式的数据共享或存储一样谨慎。

paras.en: There’s also a knowledge gap that needs to be addressed—40% of individuals surveyed are unsure about who retains ownership over the content produced by AI.
paras.zh: 还有一个知识缺口需要弥补：40%的受访者不清楚AI生成内容的所有权归谁。

w.m: adj. 不确定的；不清楚的

paras.en: By instilling best practices in AI engagement and creating policies that evolve with the technology, businesses can positively shift the AI landscape.
paras.zh: 通过推广与AI互动的最佳做法、使之深入人心，并制定随技术发展而演进的政策，企业可以推动AI格局发生积极的转变。

paras.en: With AI’s potential to simplify our professional lives, do the admin and enhance the work experience, it’s up to us to navigate its usage cautiously so it supports us without compromising our privacy.
paras.zh: 既然AI有潜力简化我们的职业生活、处理行政杂务、提升工作体验，那就要靠我们自己谨慎把握使用AI的分寸，让它在为我们提供支持的同时，不损害我们的隐私。

w.m: n. 行政杂务；行政事务

w.h: it's up to sb to do
w.m: 由某人负责做；取决于某人
v. 把握；驾驭（复杂局面）
conj. 以便；为了（= so that）

paras.en: There’s no need to back away from progress, as long as we’re equipped with the knowledge and tools to make sure AI remains a friend.
paras.zh: 只要我们具备相应的知识和工具，能确保AI始终是朋友，就没有必要在进步面前退缩。

paras.en: And this is where the challenge lies.
paras.zh: 而挑战正在于此。

paras.en: There are so many products out there, being promoted with huge advertising and marketing budgets, that it’s easy to fall victim.
paras.zh: 市面上的产品实在太多，又借助巨额的广告和营销预算加以推广，以至于人们很容易上当受骗。

paras.en: But by building a culture of digital responsibility within our businesses, we can create a future where AI can help us without spilling the beans.
paras.zh: 但通过在企业内部建立数字责任文化，我们可以创造这样一个未来：AI既能帮助我们，又不会把秘密泄露出去。

passages.name: 2026年考研英语二 Text 3
passages.title: 意大利高铁为何频频延误
passages.genre: 说明文 · 交通与经济
passages.summary: 自2008年罗马至米兰的高铁网络开通以来，火车已成为本地人和游客在意大利各地出行的首选交通方式。然而，近来大量维修工程造成严重延误，又恰逢大多数人外出度假，令铁路行业陷入混乱。意大利国家铁路集团称，对陈旧基础设施的大规模改造是运行受阻的部分原因；运力不足则是另一个问题：在混合系统下，高速列车在某些线路上或途经大城市时必须在普通轨道上行驶。交通经济学家朱里钦认为，计划中的投资会带来改善，但在此期间运行受阻在所难免；RFI投资的高密度技术和卫星信号系统应能显著提升运力。

paras.en: Since the 2008 launch of the high-speed rail network between Rome and Milan, trains have become the preferred means of travel across Italy for locals and tourists alike.
paras.zh: 自2008年罗马至米兰的高铁网络开通以来，无论是本地人还是游客，都已把火车当作在意大利各地出行的首选交通方式。

w.m: adj. 首选的；更受青睐的

paras.en: Fast trains can cover the 500km between the two cities in three hours.
paras.zh: 高速列车可在3小时内跑完两座城市之间500公里的路程。

w.m: v. 走完（一段路程）；行过

paras.en: The network also connects Naples, Bologna, Florence and Turin.
paras.zh: 这一网络还连通那不勒斯、博洛尼亚、佛罗伦萨和都灵。

paras.en: In many cases, it is the best option—in terms of travel time and cost—for both leisure and business travellers.
paras.zh: 在很多情况下，从出行时间和费用来看，无论对休闲游客还是商务旅客而言，高铁都是最佳选择。

paras.en: This is why the recent severe delays caused by numerous maintenance works have thrown the rail industry into chaos at a time when most people head on holiday, which matters for business in a country where tourism accounts for 10 percent of GDP.
paras.zh: 正因如此，近来大量维修工程造成严重延误，又恰逢大多数人外出度假，令铁路行业陷入了混乱；在旅游业占GDP 10%的意大利，这对商业来说关系重大。

paras.en: Disruptions have become increasingly frequent, with train delays now a fixture in Italian media coverage.
paras.zh: 运行受阻的情况越来越频繁，列车延误如今已成为意大利媒体报道中的固定话题。

w.m: n. 固定存在的事物；常见内容

paras.en: Ferrovie dello Stato Italiane, the publicly controlled group that owns train operator Trenitalia and the national train network RFI, said 23 percent of all high-speed trains it operated were late in 2023.
paras.zh: 国有控股的意大利国家铁路集团旗下拥有列车运营商Trenitalia和国家铁路网RFI，该集团称，2023年，其运营的全部高速列车中有23%晚点。

w.m: 意大利国家铁路集团（意大利语名称）
国有控股的；由国家控制的

paras.en: The huge improvements in Italy’s obsolete infrastructure partly explained the disruption, said Ferrovie.
paras.zh: 意大利国家铁路集团表示，运行受阻的部分原因在于意大利正在对陈旧的基础设施进行大规模改造。

w.m: adv. 部分地；在一定程度上

paras.en: RFI, the network operator, is the single largest European recovery fund beneficiary with planned investments of €24bn by 2026.
paras.zh: 铁路网运营商RFI是欧洲复苏基金最大的单一受益方，计划到2026年投资240亿欧元。

w.m: 最大的单一（……）；单个最大的

paras.en: Ferrovie will invest a total of €124bn in infrastructure over the next 10 years.
paras.zh: 意大利国家铁路集团将在未来10年内向基础设施总共投资1240亿欧元。

w.m: 在接下来的……里；在未来……内

paras.en: But lack of capacity is another problem.
paras.zh: 但运力不足是另一个问题。

paras.en: Transport economist Andrea Giuricin said the planned investments would bring improvements but disruptions in the meantime were inevitable.
paras.zh: 交通经济学家安德烈亚·朱里钦说，计划中的投资会带来改善，但在此期间运行受阻在所难免。

w.m: adj. 不可避免的；必然的

paras.en: “We have a mixed system, there is no spare capacity and as soon as there’s a hiccup on the line, the situation becomes highly complex,” he said.
paras.zh: 他说：“我们用的是混合系统，没有多余的运力，线路上一出点小故障，情况就会变得非常复杂。”

paras.en: A mixed system means that high-speed trains must travel on the regular tracks on certain routes or when passing through large cities.
paras.zh: 混合系统意味着，在某些线路上或途经大城市时，高速列车必须在普通轨道上行驶。

paras.en: If there’s congestion or, for example, a local train breaks down, the entire high-speed network is affected.
paras.zh: 如果出现拥堵，或者比如一列慢车发生故障，整个高铁网络都会受到影响。

paras.en: One of the most important changes the upgrades will bring is the segregation of the high-speed line from the regular one in certain urban centres through the construction of underground rail links.
paras.zh: 升级工程将带来的最重要的变化之一，是通过修建地下铁路连接线，在某些城市中心区把高铁线路与普通线路分隔开。

paras.en: Improvements will also come from the high-density technology and satellite signalling that RFI has been investing in for years, say experts.
paras.zh: 专家们说，RFI多年来一直在投资的高密度技术和卫星信号系统也将带来改善。

paras.en: They will allow for a reduction of the distance between high-speed trains travelling on the same line at any given time, which should mean a significant increase in capacity and traffic fluidity, according to Giuricin.
paras.zh: 据朱里钦说，这些技术将能缩短同一时刻在同一线路上行驶的高速列车之间的间距，这应该意味着运力和交通流畅度会显著提升。

w.m: 在任一时刻；在任何特定时刻

passages.name: 2026年考研英语二 Text 4
passages.title: 芝加哥街头节庆的生存困境
passages.genre: 议论文 · 社会与文化
passages.summary: 芝加哥深受喜爱的银屋街区派对已经停办，举办者威廉斯指出，主要原因是筹办成本不断上升、参加者捐款日益减少，这也是所有街头节庆组织者眼下都面临的现实。作者认为，芝加哥的夏季节庆是直接惠及所在街区以及整个城市的经济引擎，而街区的街头节庆却得不到任何市政资金，要靠赞助、摊位费和入口捐款来支付成本。作者参与举办的威克公园节2024年参加人数创下纪录，入口捐款却跌到历史最低点，今年不得不缩减规模；作者希望人们记住，这类节庆因社区的支持而存在，需要大家都出一份力。

paras.en: In 2023, Chicago lost one of its most beloved street festivals.
paras.zh: 2023年，芝加哥失去了本市最受喜爱的街头节庆之一。

w.m: adj. 深受喜爱的；心爱的

paras.en: The Silver Room Block Party, staged by Hyde Park community leader Eric Williams, announced it would not return in 2024.
paras.zh: 由海德公园社区领袖埃里克·威廉斯操办的银屋街区派对宣布，2024年将不再举行。

paras.en: What began as a small neighborhood gathering blossomed into a massive cultural event, welcoming tens of thousands of people each year over nearly two decades before abruptly shutting down.
paras.zh: 这场活动起初是一次小型的邻里聚会，后来逐渐壮大，成为一项大型文化盛事，近二十年间每年迎来数万人，随后却突然停办。

paras.en: Williams pointed to rising production costs and declining attendee donations as primary reasons the Silver Room Block Party could not continue, highlighting a reality that all street festival organizers face right now.
paras.zh: 威廉斯指出，筹办成本不断上升、参加者捐款日益减少，是银屋街区派对无法继续举办的主要原因，这凸显了所有街头节庆组织者眼下都面临的现实。

paras.en: The cost of producing a street festival in Chicago has skyrocketed.
paras.zh: 在芝加哥筹办一场街头节庆，成本已经飙升。

paras.en: Security, entertainment, portable restrooms, insurance and even basics such as fencing and staffing have all become significantly more expensive.
paras.zh: 安保、娱乐表演、移动厕所、保险，甚至连围栏、人员配备这类基本项目，费用都已大幅上涨。

w.m: n. 基本项目；必需品（常用复数）

paras.en: At the same time, donations at festival gates have dropped dramatically.
paras.zh: 与此同时，节庆入口处收到的捐款已急剧减少。

paras.en: Chicago’s summer festivals are about more than just entertainment; they are economic engines that directly benefit the neighborhoods they’re in and the city of Chicago as a whole.
paras.zh: 芝加哥的夏季节庆不仅仅关乎娱乐；它们是经济引擎，直接惠及所在的街区以及整个芝加哥市。

paras.en: Street festivals drive foot traffic to local businesses and foster the kind of cultural vibrancy that makes our city special.
paras.zh: 街头节庆能为当地商家带来客流，并培育出让我们这座城市与众不同的那种文化活力。

w.m: adj. 特别的；与众不同的

paras.en: We often hear people ask why we solicit donations at our entry points, especially when the city’s largest festivals like the Chicago Jazz Festival do not request donations.
paras.zh: 我们常听到有人问，为什么要在入口处募集捐款，尤其是像芝加哥爵士音乐节这样的本市最大型节庆并不要求捐款。

paras.en: The fact is, unlike those large, city-produced music festivals, your neighborhood street festivals receive no city funding and rely on a combination of sponsorships, vendor fees and gate donations to cover their costs.
paras.zh: 事实上，与那些由市政府举办的大型音乐节不同，你们街区的街头节庆得不到任何市政资金，要同时依靠赞助、摊位费和入口捐款来支付成本。

paras.en: Wicker Park Fest has long been one of Chicago’s most anticipated summer festivals, drawing upward of 70,000 attendees for a full weekend of live indie music, local art, small business vendors and, most importantly, community connection.
paras.zh: 威克公园节长期以来一直是芝加哥最受期待的夏季节庆之一，吸引7万多名参加者前来共度整整一个周末，这里有现场独立音乐、本地艺术、小商户摊贩，最重要的是，还有社区的联结。

w.m: adj. 独立制作的（音乐等）

paras.en: In 2024, Wicker Park Fest saw record-breaking attendance.
paras.zh: 2024年，威克公园节的参加人数创下纪录。

w.m: v. 经历；出现（某种情况）
n. 参加人数；出席人数

paras.en: Despite the turnout, gate donations reached their lowest point in our history.
paras.zh: 尽管到场人数如此之多，入口捐款却跌到了我们有史以来的最低点。

w.m: n. 到场人数；出席人数

paras.en: This year, we’ve been forced to scale back the footprint of the fest.
paras.zh: 今年，我们不得不缩减节庆的规模。

paras.en: We are eliminating a stage, booking fewer performers and making additional cuts to reduce our costs, all while striving to keep the festival as vibrant as ever, as supportive of local artists and businesses, and as true to Wicker Park’s unique spirit and reputation as festgoers have come to expect.
paras.zh: 我们正在撤掉一个舞台，少邀请一些表演者，并采取更多削减措施来降低成本；与此同时，我们力求让节庆一如既往地充满活力，并像参加者们早已习惯的那样，继续支持本地艺术家和商家，继续忠于威克公园独特的精神，不负它的声誉。

paras.en: This summer, as you enjoy your favorite neighborhood street festival, I hope you’ll remember that such festivals exist because of community support.
paras.zh: 今年夏天，在你享受最喜欢的街区街头节庆时，我希望你能记住，这样的节庆之所以存在，是因为有社区的支持。

paras.en: A thriving summer festival season doesn’t happen by accident; it happens when we all chip in.
paras.zh: 红红火火的夏季节庆季不是偶然出现的；只有我们大家都出一份力，才会有这样的节庆季。

paras.en: In an effort to support restoration programmes, specialists are developing supplies of seeds and seedlings, maintaining gene banks and sequencing the genomes of indigenous trees and other crops.
Their work deals with one of the problems that could block major restoration efforts in different parts of the world.
“Where’s the planting material going to come from?
That’s one big bottleneck,” says genetic-resources specialist Ramni Jamnadass.
Asia is arguably the region most neglected by global efforts to increase diversity in restoration and to study native species.

Christopher Kettle, Bioversity International’s director for forest genetic resources and restoration in Rome, says that the need for infrastructure—things such as mechanisms for collecting and storing seeds, and nurseries to raise seedlings—might be most desperate here because many trees are ‘masting’ species, which don’t produce seeds every year.
People need to be ready.
“Otherwise, you miss the boat, you lose all the seed and you’ve got to wait another seven years,” says Kettle.

“This is a really, really critical issue for restoration in Southeast Asia, because many of the most important timber species and tree species—the ones that will lock up the most carbon—they’re all masting species.”
Climate change is a driving factor in the push to restore forests, but it also raises questions, such as where trees can thrive in the future.
Climate change is also expected to alter relationships between trees, insects, diseases and other forest species.
“Insects that today are a minor problem may become a major problem if they can produce three or four generations in a year,” says forest ecologist John Stanturf.
This remains a significant knowledge gap.
“We know enough to know that this is a concern, but we don’t know enough about how to respond to it yet.
That’s a great area to be doing research.”
So is soil, says Cindy Prescott, a forest ecologist at the University of British Columbia in Vancouver.
“If you don’t look at the soil at the start, you can spend a lot of money and time putting in species that aren’t going to survive there.”
With so much research left to do, leaders in the field have been doing some soul-searching, and acknowledging that restoration can be motivated by—and designed to meet—different needs.
“When you talk about conservation or restoration, the first question has to be restoration by whom, for whom?” says Daniel Janzen, a biologist at the University of Pennsylvania.
The question can have more than one answer.
Much of the global funding for restoration is dedicated to developing it as a tool to mitigate climate change, notes restoration ecologist Pedro Brancalion.
“But if you ask a farmer in Brazil if he or she is concerned about climate change, they would say, ‘No, I am concerned about water,’” he says.
Their interests as stewards of the land need to be better integrated with those who have the money to support restoration.
That has been the strongest lesson of all for forest ecologist Robin Chazdon.
Restoration is about more than what gets planted in the ground, she says.
“Yes, it’s about forests, but it’s really about people.
They are the agents of restoration.”
Ramni Jamnadass: The supply of seeds is a tough problem that has to be dealt with.
Christopher Kettle: People must pay attention to the fact that some kinds of trees do not produce seeds annually.
John Stanturf: Some creatures in the forest that multiply fast can become a great threat to forest restoration.
Pedro Brancalion: The purpose of restoration efforts may be different from the real needs of the people involved.
Robin Chazdon: Human factors, as well as trees planted, should be emphasized in forest restoration.

passages.name: 2025年考研英语一 Text 1
passages.title: 表演莎剧有助于儿童读写与情感发展
passages.genre: 说明文 · 教育与艺术
passages.summary: 英国皇家莎士比亚剧团委托开展的一项随机对照试验发现，用“排练室”方法教莎士比亚，扩大了儿童的词汇量，提高了其写作的复杂程度，也提升了其情感素养。与对照组相比，参加了戏剧活动的目标组学生用词范围更广、更高级，写得更长，似乎也更能自如地代入文学人物、表达人物的情感。至于换成其他剧作家能否取得同样的效果，剧团的奥汉隆表示还需要更多研究，但她认为，莎士比亚用词之多远超日常用语，让语言大规模地扩展到孩子们的生活中。

paras.en: The grammar school boy from Stratford-upon-Avon has landed a scholarly punch after groundbreaking research showed that Shakespeare does benefit children’s literacy and emotional development.
paras.zh: 一项开创性研究表明，莎士比亚确实有益于儿童的读写能力和情感发展，这位来自埃文河畔斯特拉特福的文法学校男孩由此在学术上打出了漂亮的一拳。

w.m: adj. 开创性的；突破性的

paras.en: But only if you act him out.
paras.zh: 但前提是要把他的戏演出来。

paras.en: A study found that a “rehearsal room” approach to teaching Shakespeare broadened children’s vocabulary and the complexity of their writing as well as their emotional literacy.
paras.zh: 这项研究发现，用“排练室”方法教莎士比亚，扩大了孩子们的词汇量，提高了他们写作的复杂程度，也提升了他们的情感素养。

paras.en: “The research shows that the way actors work makes a big difference to the way children use language and also how they think about themselves,” Jacqui O’Hanlon of the Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC), which commissioned the study, said.
paras.zh: 皇家莎士比亚剧团（RSC）委托开展了这项研究，该剧团的杰姬·奥汉隆说：“研究表明，演员的工作方式对孩子们使用语言的方式，以及他们看待自己的方式，都有很大影响。”

paras.en: The randomised controlled trial involved hundreds of year 5 pupils—aged nine and ten—at 45 state primary schools that had not been “previously exposed to RSC pedagogy”.
paras.zh: 这项随机对照试验的参与者是45所公立小学的数百名五年级学生，年龄在九岁到十岁之间；这些学校此前没有“接触过皇家莎士比亚剧团的教学法”。

paras.en: They were split into target and control groups and asked to write, for example, a message in a bottle as Ferdinand following the shipwreck in The Tempest.
paras.zh: 学生们被分成目标组和对照组，并按要求写作，比如以《暴风雨》中费迪南德的身份，在海难之后写一封瓶中信。

w.m: n. 目标（此处指目标组）

paras.en: The target group were given a 30-minute drama-based activity to accompany the passage.
paras.zh: 研究者为目标组安排了一项时长30分钟、以戏剧为基础的活动，配合相应的选段进行。

paras.en: The peer-reviewed results showed that the target group of pupils drew on a wider vocabulary, used words “classed as more sophisticated or rarer”, and wrote at greater length.
paras.zh: 经同行评审的研究结果显示，目标组的学生调用的词汇范围更广，用上了“被归为更高级或更生僻”的词语，写得也更长。

paras.en: They also “appear to be more comfortable writing in role…while [control] pupils imagine how they themselves would react to being shipwrecked, [target] children put themselves in the shoes of a literary character and express that character’s emotion”.
paras.zh: 他们还“似乎更能自如地以角色身份写作……［对照组］学生想象的是他们自己遭遇海难会作何反应，而［目标组］孩子则设身处地站在文学人物的角度，表达这个人物的情感”。

w.m: n. 目标（此处指目标组）
设身处地；站在某人的角度

paras.en: The Time to Act study, which is published by the RSC this week, also found that while control pupils relied on “desert island clichés” such as palm trees, target pupils were “more expansive, [giving] a broader picture of the sky, the sea and the atmospheric conditions”.
paras.zh: 皇家莎士比亚剧团本周发布的这项“该表演了”（Time to Act）研究还发现，对照组学生依赖棕榈树之类的“荒岛俗套”，而目标组学生则“写得更开阔，［呈现出］一幅更全面的画面，描绘出天空、大海和天气状况”。

w.m: n. 目标（此处指目标组）
adj. （内容）广泛的；（视野）开阔的

paras.en: O’Hanlon said she had been most surprised by the “emotional literacy that was evident in the [target] children’s writing” and that they were “more resilient in their writing, more hopeful”.
paras.zh: 奥汉隆说，最让她惊讶的是“［目标组］孩子们的作文中明显流露出的情感素养”，而且他们“在写作中更坚韧，更充满希望”。

w.m: n. 目标（此处指目标组）
adj. 充满希望的；乐观的

paras.en: She added: “The emotional understanding was very evident and it is probably related to the [rehearsal room process] where you are used to trying to imagine your way through.
paras.zh: 她补充说：“对情感的理解体现得非常明显，这很可能与［排练室流程］有关，在这个流程中，你习惯了设法凭想象一步步摸索前行。

w.m: 凭想象一步步摸索前行（以走完某个情境）

paras.en: They were comfortable in describing different emotional states and part of what you do in drama is put yourself in different shoes.”
paras.zh: 他们能自如地描述各种不同的情绪状态，而你在戏剧中要做的事，有一部分就是设身处地，站到不同人的立场上去。”

w.m: 设身处地；站在别人的角度

paras.en: The study showed the importance of embedding arts in education, she said.
paras.zh: 她说，这项研究表明了将艺术融入教育的重要性。

paras.en: But could the results be replicated with any old dramatist?
paras.zh: 但换成随便哪位剧作家，这些结果能否复现呢？

w.m: v. 复现；重复（实验结果）

paras.en: O’Hanlon said more research would be needed but suggested that Shakespeare’s use of 20,000 words, compared with the everyday 2,000 words, gave a “massive expansion of language into children’s lives”, which was combined with children “using their whole bodies to bring words to life”.
paras.zh: 奥汉隆说，这还需要更多研究，但她表示，莎士比亚用了20,000个词，而日常用语只有2,000个词，这让“语言大规模地扩展到孩子们的生活中”，与之相结合的，是孩子们“用整个身体让文字活起来”。

passages.name: 2025年考研英语一 Text 2
passages.title: 科研的碳排放是值得付出的代价
passages.genre: 议论文 · 科技与环境
passages.summary: 作者最近得知，一些科学家为了减少碳排放，想要缩减自己的研究，对此大为震惊。作者承认，实验室、科学仪器、火箭、卫星以及数据中心都要消耗大量能源，但认为这是了解世界必须付出的代价，因为技术研究最终将守护地球的未来；要解决人类面临的最大挑战，证明科学的功效至关重要。作者以马丁·格林发明的太阳能电池技术和位于芬兰、实现了负碳排放的超级计算机LUMI为例，说明科学与工程能够带来希望，并指出世界要实现净零目标，就必须认真思考如何实现可持续计算、打造更多像LUMI这样的超级计算机。

paras.en: I was shocked to learn recently that some scientists want to scale back their research in an effort to decrease carbon emissions.
paras.zh: 我最近得知，一些科学家为了减少碳排放，想要缩减自己的研究，这让我大为震惊。

paras.en: The crisis is here, they said, and we need to cut back on our energy-intensive modelling.
paras.zh: 他们说，危机已经到来，我们需要减少高耗能的建模工作。

w.m: adj. 高耗能的；能源密集型的

paras.en: At the very least, we need to make our energy use far more sustainable.
paras.zh: 最起码，我们需要大幅提高自身能源使用的可持续性。

paras.en: It is unarguable that our laboratories, scientific instruments, rockets and satellites—the tools we scientists need to measure the planet’s pulse—demand significant amounts of energy in both their construction and operation.
paras.zh: 无可争辩的是，我们的实验室、科学仪器、火箭和卫星，也就是我们科学家测量地球脉搏所需的工具，无论建造还是运行，都需要消耗大量能源。

w.m: adj. 无可争辩的；不容置疑的

paras.en: And it is equally true that science’s unrelenting appetite for information has caused a mushrooming of energy-intensive data centres around the world.
paras.zh: 而且同样属实的是，科学对信息永无止境的渴求，已导致高耗能的数据中心在世界各地如雨后春笋般涌现。

w.m: adj. 无休止的；持续不断的
n. （如雨后春笋般）迅速涌现；激增
adj. 高耗能的；能源密集型的

paras.en: According to the International Energy Agency, these buildings now consume about 1 percent of the world’s electricity.
paras.zh: 据国际能源署称，这些建筑如今消耗着全世界约1%的电力。

paras.en: However, this is a price we must pay for understanding the world.
paras.zh: 然而，这是我们为认识世界而必须付出的代价。

paras.en: How can we inform decision makers about the best ways to bring down carbon emissions if we can’t track the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, where it’s coming from and who’s producing it?
paras.zh: 如果我们无法追踪大气中二氧化碳的含量，以及它从哪里来、是谁排放的，又怎能告诉决策者减少碳排放的最佳途径呢？

paras.en: The carbon emissions from technological research are well spent: ultimately this research will safeguard the future of our planet.
paras.zh: 技术研究产生的碳排放是物有所值的：这类研究最终将守护我们这个星球的未来。

w.m: 物有所值的；（花得）值得的

paras.en: It can be hard for scientists to make the case because our work is complex, often takes place behind closed doors and does not always lend itself to easy interpretation or explanation.
paras.zh: 科学家可能很难把这个道理讲清楚，因为我们的工作很复杂，往往关起门来进行，而且并不总是易于解读或解释。

w.m: 讲清道理；（为某观点）论证

paras.en: But demonstrating the efficacy of science will be crucial if we are to solve humanity’s greatest challenges.
paras.zh: 但如果我们要解决人类面临的最大挑战，证明科学的功效将至关重要。

paras.en: It is all too easy to feel paralysed in the face of daunting problems such as climate change and to do nothing.
paras.zh: 面对气候变化这类令人生畏的难题，人们实在太容易感到不知所措，什么也不做。

w.m: adj. （因恐惧等）不知所措的；无法行动的

paras.en: But then I think of a friend’s daughter who turned her fears into action: she became a wind energy engineer and now thrives on delivering renewable energy, limiting emissions.
paras.zh: 但这时我就会想起一位朋友的女儿，她把恐惧化作了行动：她成了一名风能工程师，如今在提供可再生能源、限制排放的工作中如鱼得水。

paras.en: Recognising the hope that science and engineering can bring was the impetus behind the creation of the Millennium Technology Prize, which is now entering its 20th year as a celebration of human ingenuity.
paras.zh: 认识到科学与工程能够带来希望，正是设立千禧技术奖的动力所在；这一礼赞人类创造才能的奖项，如今正迈入第20个年头。

w.m: n. 创造才能；聪明才智

paras.en: One of the past winners, Professor Martin Green from the University of New South Wales, Australia, is the inventor of the Passivated Emitter and Rear Cell technology, which is now found in most of the world’s solar panels.
paras.zh: 往届得主之一、澳大利亚新南威尔士大学的马丁·格林教授，是钝化发射极和背面电池技术的发明者，如今世界上大多数太阳能电池板都采用了这项技术。

paras.en: Thanks to his invention, we have a real chance to decrease the world’s carbon emissions.
paras.zh: 多亏了他的这项发明，我们才真正有机会减少全世界的碳排放。

paras.en: Every day, scientists, technologists and engineers are discovering new ways to exploit renewable energy sources and develop techniques not just to use power more intelligently but to power our intelligence.
paras.zh: 科学家、技术专家和工程师每天都在发现新的方法，以开发利用可再生能源，并研发各种技术，这些技术不仅能让我们更智能地使用电力，还能为我们的智能提供动力。

w.m: v. 为……提供动力；为……供电

paras.en: A great example of this is Europe’s largest supercomputer, LUMI in Finland, which is astonishingly carbon-negative.
paras.zh: 欧洲最大的超级计算机、位于芬兰的LUMI就是这方面的一个绝佳例子，令人惊讶的是，它实现了负碳排放。

w.m: adv. 惊人地；令人惊讶地

paras.en: Established in an old paper mill, it is powered by a nearby river, and its waste heat warms the people who live in the surrounding town of Kajaani.
paras.zh: 它设在一座旧造纸厂里，由附近的一条河流供电，产生的余热则为周边卡亚尼镇的居民供暖。

w.m: v. 为……供电；为……提供动力

paras.en: If the world is to meet its net-zero ambitions, we must think hard about how we can deliver sustainable computing and deliver more LUMIs.
paras.zh: 如果世界要实现净零目标，我们就必须认真思考，如何才能实现可持续计算、打造更多像LUMI这样的超级计算机。

passages.name: 2025年考研英语一 Text 3
passages.title: 非法流媒体获利丰厚，好莱坞出手打击
passages.genre: 说明文 · 传媒与版权
passages.summary: 自从在Netflix的拿手领域向其发起挑战以来，老牌好莱坞在流媒体业务上一直难以盈利，盗版者却成了意外的赢家：他们翻录正版平台上的影视作品，放到自己的非法平台上，每年从广告和订阅中进账约20亿美元。据美国商会全球创新政策中心估计，盗版每年给美国经济造成约300亿美元的收入损失。美国电影协会正致力于打击非法平台，其成立的创意与娱乐联盟称，已帮助把北美的非法流媒体服务从2018年的1400多个减少到126个；但分析师指出，对于盗版何时可能开始减少，各利益相关方尚无共识。

paras.en: Ever since taking on Netflix Inc. at its own game, old Hollywood has struggled to turn a profit in streaming, with the likes of Disney+, Peacock and Paramount+ losing billions of dollars each year, sparking concerns that the services will never be as profitable as cable once was.
paras.zh: 自从在Netflix公司的拿手领域向其发起挑战以来，老牌好莱坞在流媒体业务上一直难以盈利，Disney+、Peacock和Paramount+等平台每年都亏损数十亿美元，由此引发担忧：这些流媒体服务永远不会像有线电视当年那样赚钱。

w.m: 在对方的拿手领域向其发起挑战
老牌好莱坞（传统电影公司）

paras.en: But the age of streaming has been a boon for some unintended winners: pirates that use software to rip a film or television show in seconds from legitimate online video platforms and host the titles on their own illegitimate services, which rake in about $2 billion annually from ads and subscriptions.
paras.zh: 但流媒体时代却成了一些意外赢家的福音：盗版者利用软件，几秒钟就能从正版在线视频平台上翻录一部电影或一档电视节目，再把这些作品放到自己的非法平台上，这些非法平台每年从广告和订阅中捞进约20亿美元。

w.m: v. 翻录；（从光盘、网站等）提取
v. （在网上）存放并提供；托管

paras.en: With no video production costs, illegal streaming sites have achieved profit margins approaching 90%, according to the Motion Picture Association (MPA), a trade group representing Hollywood studios that’s working to crack down on the thousands of illegal platforms that have cropped up in recent years.
paras.zh: 据美国电影协会（MPA）称，由于没有视频制作成本，非法流媒体网站的利润率已接近90%。该协会是代表好莱坞各电影公司的行业组织，正致力于打击近年来冒出来的数千个非法平台。

paras.en: Initially the rise of legitimate online businesses such as Netflix actually helped curb digital piracy, which had largely been based on file uploads.
paras.zh: 起初，Netflix等正版在线企业的兴起实际上帮助遏制了数字盗版，此前的数字盗版主要依托于文件上传。

w.m: adv. 主要地；在很大程度上

paras.en: But now piracy involving illegal streaming services as well as file-sharing costs the US economy about $30 billion in lost revenue a year and some 250,000 jobs, estimates the US Chamber of Commerce’s Global Innovation Policy Center.
paras.zh: 但据美国商会全球创新政策中心估计，如今，涉及非法流媒体服务和文件共享的盗版行为每年给美国经济造成约300亿美元的收入损失，还使约25万个就业岗位流失。

w.m: v. 使损失；使付出（代价）

paras.en: The global impact is about $71 billion annually.
paras.zh: 在全球范围内，盗版每年造成的经济影响约为710亿美元。

w.m: adj. 全球的；全球范围的

paras.en: “The people who are stealing our movies and our television shows and operating piracy sites are not mom-and-pop operations,” says Charlie Rivkin, chief executive officer of the MPA.
paras.zh: 美国电影协会首席执行官查理·里夫金说：“那些窃取我们的电影和电视节目、经营盗版网站的，并不是什么夫妻店。”

paras.en: “This is organized crime.”
paras.zh: “这是有组织犯罪。”

paras.en: Rivkin joined the MPA in 2017 after the organization failed five years earlier to build consensus between Hollywood and Silicon Valley to win passage of legislation in Congress aimed at stopping online piracy.
paras.zh: 里夫金于2017年加入美国电影协会，在那之前五年，该协会曾试图促成好莱坞与硅谷达成共识，以争取国会通过一项旨在制止网络盗版的立法，但没能成功。

w.m: 促成（法案）获得通过；使……得以通过

paras.en: In 2017 the association formed the Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment (ACE), an enforcement task force of about 100 detectives circling the globe to help local authorities arrest streaming pirates.
paras.zh: 2017年，该协会成立了创意与娱乐联盟（ACE），这是一支约有100名侦探的执法特别工作组，他们奔走全球，协助各地当局逮捕流媒体盗版者。

w.m: 奔走全球；在世界各地奔波

paras.en: ACE says it’s helped shrink the number of illegal streaming services in North America to 126, from more than 1,400 in 2018, aided in part by the MPA’s support for a 2020 federal law that made large-scale streaming of copyright material a serious crime.
paras.zh: 创意与娱乐联盟称，已协助将北美的非法流媒体服务从2018年的1400多个减少到126个，这在一定程度上得益于美国电影协会对2020年一项联邦法律的支持，该法律将以流媒体方式大规模传播受版权保护的内容定为严重犯罪。

w.m: 受版权保护的内容（作品）

paras.en: Consulting firm Parks Associates predicts that legitimate US streaming services’ cumulative loss from piracy since 2022 will reach $113 billion in the next two years.
paras.zh: 咨询公司Parks Associates预测，美国正版流媒体服务自2022年以来因盗版蒙受的累计损失，将在未来两年内达到1130亿美元。

paras.en: “While there is some optimism that emerging countermeasures and best practices may see piracy begin to plateau by 2027, there is no consensus among stakeholders as to when it may begin to decline,” says analyst Steve Hawley.
paras.zh: 分析师史蒂夫·霍利说：“虽然有人抱有一定的乐观态度，认为新出现的应对措施和最佳做法可能会使盗版到2027年开始趋于平稳，但对于盗版何时可能开始减少，各利益相关方之间尚无共识。”

w.m: v. 进入平稳期；趋于平稳

passages.name: 2025年考研英语一 Text 4
passages.title: 图书馆员与数字时代的历史记录
passages.genre: 议论文 · 文化与科技
passages.summary: 古董店里的照片、信件等物件历经几十年乃至几百年依然留存，因为它们是有形的；而数字信息的制作者很少为其长期保存预作安排。作者指出，数字信息需要的照管比模拟资料多得多：即使数字对象得到保存，保存下来的也可能只是载体，格式一旦过时，数字对象便毫无用处；历史学家担心，如果数字资产得不到持续迁移，历史记录会在数字取代模拟之时戛然而止。作者坦言目前还没有全面的保存方案，但认为图书馆员在识别和保存数字产物、使其可供获取方面发挥着不可或缺的作用，这样一来，未来的研究人员在数字领域开展工作虽然可能颇具挑战，却不至于无法进行。

paras.en: Visit any antiques store and you’ll encounter artifacts from the past: photographs, letters, a brochure detailing the Sinclair dinosaur exhibit from the 1964–1965 World’s Fair, the ephemera of history.
paras.zh: 随便走进哪家古董店，你都会看到往昔留下的物件：照片、信件、一本详细介绍1964至1965年世界博览会上辛克莱恐龙展的宣传册，这些都是历史上的易逝之物。

w.m: n. （有历史价值的）物件；人工制品
n. （原本只供短期使用的）易逝之物；短期印刷品

paras.en: Yet these objects aren’t truly ephemeral, because they’re still here, decades, even centuries later.
paras.zh: 然而，这些物件并非真的易逝，因为几十年、甚至几百年过去了，它们依然存在。

w.m: adj. 短暂的；转瞬即逝的

paras.en: Why?
paras.zh: 为什么？

paras.en: Because they’re tangible.
paras.zh: 因为它们是有形的。

paras.en: Have you pondered the life cycle of intangible formats, digital information, given that those who produce these artifacts seldom make provision for their long-term preservation?
paras.zh: 鉴于数字产物的制作者很少为其长期保存预作安排，你是否思考过数字信息这类无形形式的生命周期？

w.m: adj. 无形的；不可触摸的
n. 格式；（信息的）存储形式
n. 人工制品；（数字）产物

paras.en: For millennia, we’ve known what we’ve known due to artifacts that have survived, often despite their original creators’ neglect.
paras.zh: 数千年来，我们所知道的一切，都得益于那些留存至今的物件，而它们往往是在最初的创造者疏于照管的情况下幸存下来的。

w.m: n. （有历史价值的）物件；人工制品

paras.en: The thing itself is the medium that delivers the information.
paras.zh: 物件本身就是传递信息的媒介。

paras.en: At the time of creation, no attempts were made at intentional preservation, yet analog materials have a chance of surviving and serving as the historical record that biographers, historians, and novelists rely on.
paras.zh: 在制作之时，没有人试图刻意保存它们，但模拟资料仍有机会留存下来，成为传记作家、历史学家和小说家所依赖的历史记录。

paras.en: Libraries and archives have traditionally shouldered the responsibility of organization, preservation, and access to information.
paras.zh: 图书馆和档案馆历来承担着整理、保存信息以及提供信息获取途径的责任。

w.m: 获取……的途径；接触……的机会

paras.en: Thus, librarians digitize the tangible so that researchers the world over can quickly search and access their holdings.
paras.zh: 因此，图书馆员将有形资料数字化，好让世界各地的研究人员能够快速检索和查阅馆藏。

w.m: n. 有形之物；有形资料

paras.en: The result is an embarrassment of historical riches, which brings its own needle-and-haystack problems.
paras.zh: 结果是，历史资料多得让人应接不暇，而这本身又带来了大海捞针式的难题。

w.m: 多得应接不暇；多得不知如何是好

paras.en: Librarians’ selfless devotion can act against us when users point to universality of access by holding up a cellphone and saying, “It’s all in here,” as evidence that libraries are less vital for researchers today.
paras.zh: 图书馆员的无私奉献可能会对我们不利：用户举起手机说“全都在这里面”，以信息人人可得为证据，表明如今图书馆对研究人员已没那么重要。

paras.en: Yet how was that universality of access made possible and, perhaps more importantly, how is it maintained?
paras.zh: 然而，这种信息人人可得的局面是如何实现的？或许更重要的是，它又是如何维持的？

paras.en: Who curates what is preserved?
paras.zh: 所保存的内容由谁来甄选和管理？

w.m: v. 甄选并管理（藏品）；策展

paras.en: When it comes to born-digital information, the terrifying answer can be: if not librarians and archivists, then no one.
paras.zh: 说到原生数字信息，令人恐惧的答案可能是：如果图书馆员和档案管理员不来做，那就没有人会做。

w.m: adj. 原生数字的（直接以数字形式产生的）
adj. 令人恐惧的；可怕的

paras.en: Digital information requires a great deal more care than analog.
paras.zh: 数字信息需要的照管比模拟资料多得多。

w.m: n. 模拟资料（非数字形式）

paras.en: Even when a digital object is preserved, it may only be the carrier that’s saved, not the information itself.
paras.zh: 即使数字对象得到了保存，保存下来的可能也只是载体，而不是信息本身。

paras.en: As technology advances and a format becomes obsolete, the object is useless.
paras.zh: 随着技术进步，格式一旦过时，这个数字对象就毫无用处了。

paras.en: Have you ever stared helplessly at a ZIP disk, thinking: how do I get the files off this?
paras.zh: 你是否曾束手无策地盯着一张ZIP磁盘，心想：怎样才能把里面的文件取出来呢？

w.m: adv. 无助地；束手无策地
ZIP磁盘（一种老式移动存储盘）

paras.en: Without constant migration of digital assets, a nightmare about the foreseeable future is what keeps historians up at night: a historical record that abruptly stops when digital replaced analog.
paras.zh: 如果数字资产得不到持续迁移，那么让历史学家夜不能寐的，就是在可预见的未来会出现的一幕噩梦：历史记录在数字取代模拟之时戛然而止。

w.m: n. 模拟资料（非数字形式）

paras.en: As a librarian whose day job revolves around special collections and digital assets, I share the night terrors of historians, and I’d be lying if I said a comprehensive preservation solution currently exists.
paras.zh: 我是一名图书馆员，日常工作围绕特藏和数字资产展开，和历史学家一样，我也会在夜里惊恐难眠；而且，如果我说目前已经有了全面的保存方案，那我就是在撒谎。

w.m: 特藏（图书馆的珍稀特色馆藏）
v. 有同样的（感受）；共有

w.h: I'd be lying if I said
w.m: 如果我说……那我就是在撒谎

paras.en: Yet researchers can take some comfort in the fact that there are a multitude of librarians devoted to discovering, organizing, and preserving digital information for researchers current and future.
paras.zh: 不过，研究人员可以从这一事实中获得些许安慰：有众多图书馆员致力于为现在和未来的研究人员发现、整理和保存数字信息。

paras.en: Librarians are uniquely positioned to understand how end users seek and use information.
paras.zh: 图书馆员具有独特的优势，能够了解最终用户如何查找和使用信息。

w.m: 具有做……的独特优势；处于独特地位

paras.en: Thus we play an integral role in identifying, preserving, and providing accessibility to digital artifacts so that, while future researchers may find the digital realm a challenging place to ply their trade, they won’t find it an impossible one.
paras.zh: 因此，我们在识别和保存数字产物、使其可供获取方面发挥着不可或缺的作用，这样一来，未来的研究人员虽然可能会觉得在数字领域从事本行颇具挑战，却不会觉得无法做到。

w.m: adj. 不可或缺的；必需的
n. 可获取性；可访问性
n. 人工制品；（数字）产物
adj. 不可能的；无法做到的
v. 觉得；认为（某事物具有某特点）

passages.name: 2025年考研英语二 Text 1
passages.title: 小费蔓延与小费通胀
passages.genre: 说明文 · 经济与社会
passages.summary: 过去，美国顾客会给他们认为大部分收入来自小费的人付小费，而且几乎总是在接受服务之后付。21世纪10年代初，数字支付系统开始普及，小费请求随之蔓延到以往不付小费的服务中，事先索要小费的情况也越来越常见，小费数额则从20世纪50年代的10%或更低升至如今的20%或更高，即所谓的“小费通胀”。为了在不提价的情况下增加员工工资，越来越多的雇主经不住小费蔓延和小费通胀的诱惑，许多顾客则觉得被索要小费过于频繁、数额过高，因而感到恼火；作者的研究强调，如今付小费似乎更具强制性、慷慨的成分更少，并且常常与服务质量完全脱节。

paras.en: U.S. customers historically tipped people they assumed were earning most of their income via tips, such as restaurant servers earning less than the minimum wage.
paras.zh: 过去，美国顾客会给他们认为大部分收入来自小费的人付小费，比如工资低于最低工资标准的餐厅服务员。

paras.en: In the early 2010s, a wide range of businesses started processing purchases with iPads and other digital payment systems.
paras.zh: 21世纪10年代初，各种各样的商家开始用iPad和其他数字支付系统处理消费交易。

w.m: 各种各样的；范围广泛的

paras.en: These systems often prompted customers to tip for services that were not previously tipped.
paras.zh: 这些系统常常提示顾客为以往不付小费的服务付小费。

paras.en: Today’s tip requests are often not connected to the salary and service norms that used to determine when and how people tip.
paras.zh: 如今的小费请求往往与工资和服务方面的规范无关，而过去正是这些规范决定了人们何时付小费、怎样付小费。

paras.en: Customers in the past nearly always paid tips after receiving a service, such as at the conclusion of a restaurant meal, after getting a haircut or once a pizza was delivered.
paras.zh: 过去，顾客几乎总是在接受服务之后付小费，比如在餐厅用餐结束时、理完发后，或是披萨刚送到时。

paras.en: That timing could reward high-quality service and give workers an incentive to provide it.
paras.zh: 在这个时机付小费，能够奖励优质服务，并让服务人员有动力提供优质服务。

paras.en: It’s becoming more common for tips to be requested beforehand.
paras.zh: 事先索要小费的情况越来越普遍了。

paras.en: And new tipping technology may even automatically add tips.
paras.zh: 而且，新的小费支付技术甚至可能自动加上小费。

paras.en: The prevalence of digital payment devices has made it easier to ask customers for a tip.
paras.zh: 数字支付设备的普及，使向顾客索要小费变得更加容易。

paras.en: That helps explain why tip requests are creeping into new kinds of services.
paras.zh: 这有助于解释为什么小费请求正悄然蔓延到新的服务类型中。

paras.en: Customers now routinely see menus of suggested default options—often well above 20% of what they owe.
paras.zh: 如今，顾客经常会看到一组建议的默认小费选项，往往远高于应付金额的20%。

w.m: n. （供选择的）一组选项；菜单

paras.en: The amounts have risen from 10% or less in the 1950s to 15% around the year 2000 to 20% or higher today.
paras.zh: 小费数额已从20世纪50年代的10%或更低，升至2000年前后的15%，再到如今的20%或更高。

paras.en: This increase is sometimes called tipflation—the expectation of ever-higher tip amounts.
paras.zh: 这种上涨有时被称为“小费通胀”，即预期小费数额会越来越高。

paras.en: Tipping has always been a vital source of income for workers in historically tipped services, like restaurants, where the tipped minimum wage can be as low as US$2.13 an hour.
paras.zh: 在餐馆等历来收取小费的服务行业，小费一直是从业者至关重要的收入来源；这些行业中，领取小费的员工，最低工资可以低至每小时2.13美元。

w.m: （领取小费员工的）小费最低工资

paras.en: Tip creep and tipflation are now further supplementing the income of many low-wage service workers.
paras.zh: 如今，小费蔓延和小费通胀正进一步补充许多低薪服务业从业者的收入。

w.m: 小费蔓延（索要小费的范围不断扩大）

paras.en: Notably, tipping primarily benefits some of these workers, such as waiters, but not others, such as cooks and dishwashers.
paras.zh: 值得注意的是，小费主要让这些从业者中的一部分人受益，比如服务员；另一部分人，比如厨师和洗碗工，则不然。

w.m: adv. 值得注意的是；尤其

paras.en: To ensure that all employees were paid fair wages, some restaurants banned tipping and increased prices, but this movement towards no-tipping services has largely fizzled out.
paras.zh: 为了确保所有员工都能拿到公平的工资，一些餐馆禁止给小费，同时提高了价格，但这场向免小费服务转变的运动基本上已经不了了之。

w.m: adj. 免小费的；不收小费的
adv. 基本上；在很大程度上

paras.en: So to increase employee wages without raising prices, more employers are succumbing to the temptations of tip creep and tipflation.
paras.zh: 因此，为了在不提高价格的情况下增加员工工资，越来越多的雇主经不住小费蔓延和小费通胀的诱惑。

paras.en: However, many customers are frustrated because they feel they are being asked for too high a tip too often.
paras.zh: 然而，许多顾客感到恼火，因为他们觉得自己被索要小费过于频繁，要的数额也过高。

paras.en: And, as our research emphasizes, tipping now seems to be more coercive, less generous, and often completely dissociated from service quality.
paras.zh: 而且，正如我们的研究所强调的，如今付小费似乎更具强制性，慷慨的成分更少，并且常常与服务质量完全脱节。

passages.name: 2025年考研英语二 Text 2
passages.title: 英国医疗模式亟须重新思考
passages.genre: 议论文 · 医疗与公共政策
passages.summary: 英国国民医疗服务体系（NHS）建立之初颇具远见，但近75年后，英国面临的健康挑战已大不相同，这一模式显然已经过时：从预期寿命到癌症死亡率和婴儿死亡率，英国都落后于许多同类国家；候诊人数超过680万，无法选择付费接受私立医疗的人越来越难以获得医疗服务；医疗成本日益挤占对其他公共服务的投入；医护队伍承受的压力也只会愈发严峻。应对这场危机的许多办法早已反复讨论过，但尽管二十年来出台了种种战略、推行了多项重大改革，英国在落实这些办法上都未能取得实质性进展。为此，“改革”智库在十位前卫生大臣的支持下启动“重新构想健康”工作计划，呼吁对以医院为中心的模式展开“紧急反思”，从如何最大限度地增进国民健康入手，并探讨卫生体系中的权力和资源应当如何分配。

paras.en: When it was established, the National Health Service (NHS) was visionary: offering high-quality, timely care to meet the dominant needs of the population it served.
paras.zh: 国民医疗服务体系（NHS）建立之初颇具远见：它提供高质量、及时的医疗服务，满足其所服务人群的主要需求。

w.m: adj. 有远见的；高瞻远瞩的
adj. 主要的；占主导地位的

paras.en: Nearly 75 years on, with the UK facing very different health challenges, it is clear that the model is out of date.
paras.zh: 近75年过去了，英国面临的健康挑战已大不相同，这一模式显然已经过时。

paras.en: From life expectancy to cancer and infant mortality rates, we are lagging behind many of our peers.
paras.zh: 从预期寿命到癌症死亡率和婴儿死亡率，我们都落后于许多同类国家。

w.m: n. 同类者；（地位、水平）相当的国家或人

paras.en: With more than 6.8 million on waitlists, healthcare is becoming increasingly inaccessible for those who cannot opt to pay for private treatment; and the cost of providing healthcare is increasingly squeezing our investment in other public services.
paras.zh: 候诊名单上的人数超过680万，对于那些无法选择付费接受私立医疗的人来说，医疗服务越来越难以获得；而提供医疗服务的成本也日益挤占我们对其他公共服务的投入。

w.m: n. 候诊名单；等候名单
n. 医疗服务；医疗保健
adj. 难以获得的；无法利用的

paras.en: As demand for healthcare continues to grow, pressures on the workforce—which is already near breaking point—will only become more acute.
paras.zh: 随着医疗需求持续增长，医护队伍本已濒临崩溃，所承受的压力只会愈发严峻。

w.m: n. 医疗服务；医疗保健

paras.en: Many of the answers to the crisis in health and care are well rehearsed.
paras.zh: 应对医疗与照护危机的许多办法，人们早已反复讨论过。

w.m: 被反复讨论过的；人们耳熟能详的

paras.en: We need to be much better at reducing and diverting demand on health services, rather than simply managing it.
paras.zh: 我们需要在减少和分流医疗服务需求方面做得好得多，而不仅仅是管理需求。

w.m: 更擅长……；在……方面做得更好

paras.en: Much more needs to be invested in communities and primary care to reduce our reliance on hospitals.
paras.zh: 需要向社区和初级医疗投入多得多的资源，以减少我们对医院的依赖。

w.m: 初级医疗；基层医疗保健

paras.en: And capacity in social care needs to be greater, to support the growing number of people living with long-term conditions.
paras.zh: 此外，社会照护的服务能力也需要扩大，以便为越来越多身患长期疾病的人提供支持。

paras.en: Yet despite two decades of strategies and a number of major health reforms, we have failed to make meaningful progress on any of these aims.
paras.zh: 然而，尽管二十年来出台了种种战略，又推行了多项重大医疗改革，我们却在这些目标上都未能取得实质性进展。

w.m: adj. 实质性的；有意义的

paras.en: That is why the Reform think tank is launching a new programme of work entitled “Reimagining health”, supported by ten former health ministers.
paras.zh: 正因如此，“改革”智库正在启动一项新的工作计划，名为“重新构想健康”，得到了十位前卫生大臣的支持。

w.m: 正因如此；这就是……的原因
v. 给（书、作品等）题名（此处过去分词作后置定语：题为……的）
v. 重新构想；重新设想

paras.en: Together, we are calling for a much more open and honest conversation about the future of health in the UK, and an “urgent rethink” of the hospital-centric model we retain.
paras.zh: 我们共同呼吁，就英国国民健康的未来展开开放、坦诚得多的讨论，并“紧急反思”我们仍在沿用的以医院为中心的模式。

paras.en: This must begin with the question of how we maximise the health of the nation, rather than “fix” the NHS.
paras.zh: 这必须从这样一个问题入手：我们如何最大限度地增进国民健康，而不是如何“修补”NHS。

w.m: v. 最大限度地增进；使最大化

paras.en: It is estimated, for example, that healthcare accounts for only about 20% of health outcomes.
paras.zh: 例如，据估计，医疗服务对健康结果的影响只占约20%。

w.m: n. 医疗服务；医疗保健

paras.en: Much more important are the places we live, work and socialise—yet there is no clear cross-government strategy for improving these social determinants of health.
paras.zh: 重要得多的是我们生活、工作和社交的场所——然而，并没有一项明确的跨政府部门战略来改善这些健康的社会决定因素。

paras.en: Worse, when policies like the national obesity strategy are scrapped, taxpayers are left with the hefty price tag of treating the illnesses, like diabetes, that result.
paras.zh: 更糟糕的是，一旦废除国家肥胖症防治战略之类的政策，纳税人就得承担治疗由此引发的疾病（如糖尿病）的高昂费用。

w.m: v. （作为结果）产生；随之发生

paras.en: Reform wants to ask how power and resources should be distributed in our health system.
paras.zh: “改革”智库想要探讨：在我们的卫生体系中，权力和资源应当如何分配。

paras.en: What health functions should remain at the centre, and what should be given to local leaders, often responsible for services that create health, and with a much better understanding of the needs of their populations?
paras.zh: 哪些卫生职能应当保留在中央？哪些应当交给地方领导者？这些领导者往往负责促进健康的服务，对当地居民的需求也了解得透彻得多。

w.m: n. （某地区的）全体居民；人口

passages.name: 2025年考研英语二 Text 3
passages.title: 印度高温行动计划有待完善
passages.genre: 说明文 · 气候与公共政策
passages.summary: 过去几年，高温行动计划在印度迅速增多，但据政策研究中心的一份报告，现有计划的执行情况参差不齐：许多计划缺乏足够的资金，触发阈值也往往没有根据当地气候量身设定。研究人员表示，孟买4月的中暑死亡事件凸显出预警需要更加细致、更加因地制宜。城市规划师科塔尔卡尔认为，所有城市都应绘制脆弱性地图，把应对措施集中于风险最高的人群。此外，研究人员认为，高温行动计划不应只包括短期应急响应，还应建议采取能让社区变得更凉爽的中长期措施。

paras.en: Heat action plans, or HAPs, have been proliferating in India in the past few years.
paras.zh: 过去几年，高温行动计划（HAP）在印度迅速增多。

paras.en: In general, an HAP spells out when and how officials should issue heat warnings and alert hospitals and other institutions.
paras.zh: 一般来说，高温行动计划会详细规定官员应在何时、以何种方式发布高温预警，并向医院和其他机构发出警报。

w.m: v. 向……发出警报；提醒……警惕

paras.en: Nagpur’s plan, for instance, calls for hospitals to set aside “cold wards” in the summer for treating heatstroke patients, and advises builders to give construction laborers a break from work on very hot days.
paras.zh: 例如，那格浦尔的计划要求医院在夏季专门留出“降温病房”，用于救治中暑患者，并建议建筑商在酷热的日子里让建筑工人停工休息。

paras.en: But implementation of existing HAPs has been uneven, according to a report from the Centre for Policy Research.
paras.zh: 但根据政策研究中心的一份报告，现有高温行动计划的执行情况一直参差不齐。

w.m: adj. 参差不齐的；不均衡的
政策研究中心（印度智库）

paras.en: Many lack adequate funding, it found.
paras.zh: 报告发现，许多计划缺乏足够的资金。

paras.en: And their triggering thresholds often are not customized to the local climate.
paras.zh: 而且，这些计划的触发阈值往往没有根据当地气候量身设定。

paras.en: In some areas, high daytime temperatures alone might serve as an adequate trigger for alerts.
paras.zh: 在一些地区，单是白天高温这一项，或许就足以作为发布预警的触发条件。

paras.en: But in other places, nighttime temperatures or humidity might be as important a gauge of risk as daytime highs.
paras.zh: 但在其他地方，夜间气温或湿度作为衡量风险的指标，可能与白天的最高气温同样重要。

w.m: 和……一样（as + 形容词 + a + 名词 + as 结构）

paras.en: Mumbai’s April heatstroke deaths highlighted the need for more nuanced and localized warnings, researchers say.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，孟买4月的中暑死亡事件凸显出，预警需要更加细致、更加因地制宜。

w.m: adj. 细致入微的；考虑周全的
adj. 本地化的；因地制宜的

paras.en: That day’s high temperature of roughly 36°C was 1°C shy of the heat wave alert threshold for coastal cities set by national meteorological authorities.
paras.zh: 那天的最高气温约为36°C，距国家气象部门为沿海城市设定的热浪预警阈值还差1°C。

w.m: n. （常用复数）当局；主管部门

paras.en: But the effects of the heat were amplified by humidity—an often neglected factor in heat alert systems—and the lack of shade at the late-morning outdoor ceremony.
paras.zh: 但有两点放大了高温的影响：一是湿度——这是高温预警系统中一个常被忽视的因素；二是那场临近中午举行的户外典礼现场缺少遮阴。

w.m: adj. 上午晚些时候的；临近中午的

paras.en: To help improve HAPs, urban planner Kotharkar’s team is working on a model plan that outlines best practices and could be adapted to local conditions.
paras.zh: 为帮助完善高温行动计划，城市规划师科塔尔卡尔的团队正在制定一份示范计划，该计划概述各项最佳做法，并可根据当地情况加以调整。

paras.en: Among other things, she says, all cities should create a vulnerability map to help focus responses on the populations most at risk.
paras.zh: 她说，所有城市都应该做的事情之一，是绘制一份脆弱性地图，以帮助把应对措施集中到风险最高的人群身上。

w.m: n. 脆弱性；易受伤害性

paras.en: Such mapping doesn’t need to be complex, Kotharkar says.
paras.zh: 科塔尔卡尔说，绘制这种地图不必很复杂。

paras.en: “A useful map can be created by looking at even a few key parameters.”
paras.zh: “哪怕只看几个关键参数，也能绘制出一份有用的地图。”

paras.en: For example, neighborhoods with a large elderly population or informal dwellings that cope poorly with heat could get special warnings or be bolstered with cooling centers.
paras.zh: 例如，有些街区老年人口众多，或者有难以应对高温的非正规住房，这些街区可以收到专门的预警，或者通过增设纳凉中心来加强保障。

w.m: adj. 年长的；上了年纪的
adj. 非正规的；非正式的

paras.en: The Nagpur project has already created a risk and vulnerability map, which enabled Kotharkar to tell officials which neighborhoods to focus on in the event of a heat wave this summer.
paras.zh: 那格浦尔的项目已经绘制出一份风险与脆弱性地图，科塔尔卡尔因此得以告诉官员，今年夏天一旦出现热浪，应重点关注哪些街区。

w.m: n. 脆弱性；易受伤害性

paras.en: HAPs shouldn’t just include short-term emergency responses, researchers say, but also recommend medium- to long-term measures that could make communities cooler.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，高温行动计划不应只包括短期应急响应，还应建议采取能让社区变得更凉爽的中长期措施。

w.m: n. 高温行动计划（heat action plan 的缩写）

paras.en: In Nagpur, for example, Kotharkar’s team has been able to advise city officials about where to plant trees to provide shade.
paras.zh: 例如，在那格浦尔，科塔尔卡尔的团队已经能够向市政官员建议在哪些地方种树来提供树荫。

paras.en: HAPs could also guide efforts to retrofit homes or modify building regulations.
paras.zh: 高温行动计划还可以为改造住宅或修订建筑法规的工作提供指导。

w.m: n. 高温行动计划（heat action plan 的缩写）
n. （为实现目标的）努力；工作

paras.en: “Reducing deaths in an emergency is a good target to have, but it’s the lowest target,” says climate researcher Chandni Singh.
paras.zh: “在紧急情况下减少死亡人数是个好目标，但这只是最低目标。”气候研究人员钱德妮·辛格说。

passages.name: 2025年考研英语二 Text 4
passages.title: 期望路径：集体选择踩出的小路
passages.genre: 说明文 · 城市与社会
passages.summary: 期望路径是人们在规整的人行道和公园之外踩出的非官方小路，揭示出人们未曾言明的偏好和集体的选择。城市规划者认为它们有助于认识规划与行为之间的关系，俄亥俄州立大学就把学生踩出的期望路径铺成了道路；但另一些规划者担心安全问题和环境影响，而最主要的是担心美观，因此仍不愿把它们纳入正式规划。纽约的百老汇大道就是由一条历史上的期望路径演变而来的；如今，期望路径在网络上也引发了浓厚的兴趣。

paras.en: Navigating beyond the organised pavements and parks of our urban spaces, desire paths are the unofficial footprints of a community, revealing the unspoken preferences, shared shortcuts and collective choices of humans.
paras.zh: 期望路径游走于城市空间里规整有序的人行道和公园之外，是一个社区留下的非官方足迹，揭示出人们未曾言明的偏好、大家共用的捷径和集体的选择。

w.m: adj. 规整有序的；有组织的
期望路径（行人自发踩出的小路）
adj. 未说出口的；心照不宣的

paras.en: Often appearing as trodden dirt tracks through otherwise neat green spaces, these routes of collective disobedience cut corners, bisect lawns and cross hills, representing the natural capability of people (and animals) to go from point A to point B most effectively.
paras.zh: 它们常常表现为一条条踩出来的土路，穿过原本整洁的绿地；这些集体违抗规矩的路线抄近路斜穿拐角，把草坪一分为二，翻越山丘，体现了人（以及动物）以最有效的方式从A点到达B点的天然能力。

w.m: adj. 踩出来的；被踩踏过的
抄近路（斜穿拐角）；（喻）偷工减料

paras.en: Urban planners interpret desire paths as more than just convenient shortcuts; they offer valuable insights into the dynamics between planning and behaviour.
paras.zh: 城市规划者并不把期望路径仅仅解读为方便的捷径；它们为认识规划与行为之间的动态关系提供了宝贵的洞见。

w.m: n. 动态关系；相互作用

paras.en: Ohio State University allowed its students to navigate the Oval, a lawn in the centre of campus, freely, then proceeded to pave the desire paths, creating a web of effective routes students had established.
paras.zh: 俄亥俄州立大学曾允许学生在位于校园中心的“椭圆草坪”上自由穿行，随后把这些期望路径铺上了路面，形成了一张由学生开辟出的有效路线网。

w.m: n. 椭圆形；此处指椭圆草坪
一张……网；错综复杂的一系列

paras.en: Yet other planners remain reluctant to integrate desire paths into formal plans, citing concerns about safety, environmental impact, or, primarily, aesthetics.
paras.zh: 然而，另一些规划者仍然不愿把期望路径纳入正式规划，理由是担心安全问题和环境影响，而最主要的是担心美观。

paras.en: A Reddit webpage devoted to the phenomenon, boasting nearly 50,000 members, showcases images of local desire paths adorned with signs instructing pedestrians to adhere to designated walkways, underscoring the rebellious nature inherent in these human-made tracks.
paras.zh: Reddit上有一个专门讨论这一现象的网页，拥有近50,000名成员，网页上展示了各地期望路径的图片，这些小路旁装点着指示牌，要求行人走指定的步道，这凸显出这类人为踩出的小路所固有的叛逆本性。

w.m: v. 拥有（值得夸耀的东西）

paras.en: This clash highlights an ongoing struggle between the organic, user-driven evolution of public spaces and the desire for a visually curated and controlled urban environment.
paras.zh: 这种冲突凸显了一场持续不断的较量：一方是公共空间由使用者推动的自然演变，另一方是对视觉上经过精心编排、受到管控的城市环境的追求。

w.m: adj. 持续的；仍在进行的
adj. 自然发展的；有机的
adj. 经过精心编排的；精心策划的
adj. 受控制的；受管控的

paras.en: The Wickquasgeck Trail is an example of a historical desire path, created by Native Americans to cross the forests of Manhattan and move between settlements quickly.
paras.zh: 威克夸斯盖克小道就是历史上期望路径的一个例子，它由美洲原住民开辟，用来穿越曼哈顿的森林，在各定居点之间快速往来。

paras.en: This trail, when Dutch colonists arrived, was widened and made into one of the main trade roads across the island, known at the time as de Heere Straat, or Gentlemen’s Street.
paras.zh: 荷兰殖民者到来后，这条小道得到拓宽，并改建为横贯全岛的主要贸易道路之一，当时称为de Heere Straat，即“绅士街”。

paras.en: Following the British assumption of control in New York, the street was renamed Broadway.
paras.zh: 英国人接管纽约后，这条街更名为百老汇大道。

paras.en: Notably, Broadway stands out as one of the few areas in NYC that defy the grid-based system applied to the rest of the city, cutting a diagonal across parts of the city.
paras.zh: 值得注意的是，百老汇大道在纽约市显得与众不同：城市其余部分都采用网格系统，它却斜穿城市的部分地区，是少数不受这一系统约束的区域之一。

w.m: adv. 值得注意的是；尤其
adj. 网格式的；基于网格的

paras.en: In online spaces, desire paths have sparked a fascination that can approach obsession, with the Reddit page serving as a hub.
paras.zh: 在网络空间，期望路径引发了人们的浓厚兴趣，有时甚至近乎痴迷，而那个Reddit网页则充当着交流中心。

paras.en: Contributors offer a wide array of stories, from little-known new shortcuts to long-established alternate routes.
paras.zh: 发帖者分享了各种各样的故事，从鲜为人知的新捷径到由来已久的替代路线都有。

w.m: adj. 由来已久的；历史悠久的

paras.en: Animal desire paths, such as ducks forging trails through frozen ponds or dogs carving direct routes in gardens, highlight the adaptability of these trails in both human and animal experiences.
paras.zh: 动物的期望路径，比如鸭子穿过结冰的池塘开出的小道，或是狗在花园里辟出的直达路线，凸显出这类小路无论在人类还是动物的经历中都具有适应性。

paras.en: As desire paths criss-cross through both physical and virtual landscapes, they stand as a proof of the collective insistence on forging unconventional routes and embracing the spirit of communal choice.
paras.zh: 期望路径在现实与虚拟两种天地里纵横交错，证明了人们集体坚持开辟非常规的路线，并坚持拥抱共同选择的精神。

w.m: adj. 非常规的；不寻常的

passages.name: 2024年考研英语一 Text 1
passages.title: 从钉子看廉价技术如何改变世界
passages.genre: 议论文 · 经济与技术史
passages.summary: 近2000年前，罗马人撤出苏格兰时埋下了近100万枚钉子，可能的解释是当时撤退仓促，他们不想让当地的喀里多尼亚人弄到这批可用来制造武器的铁；17世纪初的弗吉尼亚人打算搬家时，有时会烧掉房子来回收钉子，可见这项看似简单的技术当时多么稀缺、昂贵和珍贵。经济学家西切尔指出，从18世纪末到20世纪中叶，钉子价格下降了90%，而这大部分要归功于钉子制造商，是他们找到了把钢制成钉子的更高效方法。作者认为，受到大肆炒作的是精巧迷人的技术，改变世界的却是廉价技术，并以印刷机、纸和太阳能电池板为例。

paras.en: Nearly 2,000 years ago, as the Romans began to pull out of Scotland, they left behind a curious treasure: 10 tons of nails, nearly a million of the things.
paras.zh: 近2000年前，罗马人开始撤出苏格兰时，留下了一批奇特的宝藏：10吨钉子，将近100万枚。

paras.en: The nail hoard was discovered in 1960 in a four-metre-deep pit covered by two metres of gravel.
paras.zh: 1960年，人们在一个4米深的坑里发现了这批窖藏的钉子，坑上覆盖着2米厚的砾石。

w.m: n. 窖藏；（秘藏的）一批财物

paras.en: Why had the Romans buried a million nails?
paras.zh: 罗马人为什么要埋下100万枚钉子？

paras.en: The likely explanation is that the withdrawal was rushed, and they didn’t want the local Caledonians getting their hands on 10 tons of weapon-grade iron.
paras.zh: 可能的解释是：当时撤退仓促，而且他们不想让当地的喀里多尼亚人弄到10吨可用来制造武器的铁。

w.m: n. 喀里多尼亚人（古代苏格兰北部居民）
adj. 武器级的；可用来制造武器的

paras.en: The Romans buried the nails so deep that they would not be discovered for almost two millennia.
paras.zh: 罗马人把钉子埋得如此之深，以至于此后近两千年都无人发现。

paras.en: Later civilisations would value the skilled blacksmith’s labour in a nail even more than the raw material.
paras.zh: 后来的文明看重熟练铁匠打制一枚钉子所付出的劳动，甚至胜过看重原材料。
