paras.en: As Roma Agrawal explains in her delightful new book Nuts and Bolts, early 17th-century Virginians would sometimes burn down their homes if they were planning to relocate.
paras.zh: 正如罗玛·阿格拉沃尔在她妙趣横生的新书《螺母与螺栓》中所解释的，17世纪初的弗吉尼亚人如果打算搬家，有时会把自己的房子烧掉。

w.m: adj. 令人愉快的；妙趣横生的

paras.en: This was an attempt to recover the valuable nails, which could be reused after sifting the ashes.
paras.zh: 这样做是试图回收那些值钱的钉子：筛过灰烬之后，这些钉子可以重新使用。

paras.en: The idea that one might burn down an entire house just to reclaim the nails underlines how scarce, costly and valuable the simple-seeming technology was.
paras.zh: 竟会有人仅仅为了回收钉子就把整座房子烧掉，这一点凸显出这项看似简单的技术当时是多么稀缺、昂贵和珍贵。

paras.en: The price of nails fell by 90% between the late 1700s and mid-1900s, as economist Daniel Sichel points out in a research paper.
paras.zh: 正如经济学家丹尼尔·西切尔在一篇研究论文中指出的，从18世纪末到20世纪中叶，钉子的价格下降了90%。

paras.en: According to Sichel, although the falling price of nails was driven partly by cheaper iron and cheaper energy, most of the credit goes to nail manufacturers who simply found more efficient ways to turn steel into nails.
paras.zh: 西切尔认为，钉子价格下降虽然部分是受铁和能源降价的推动，但大部分功劳要归于钉子制造商，他们只不过是找到了把钢制成钉子的更高效方法。

paras.en: Nails themselves have changed over the years, but Sichel studied them because they haven’t changed much.
paras.zh: 钉子本身随着时间的推移确实有所变化，但西切尔之所以研究钉子，是因为它们变化不大。

paras.en: Roman lamps and Roman chariots are very different from LED strips and sports cars, but Roman nails are still clearly nails.
paras.zh: 古罗马的灯和战车与LED灯带和跑车大不相同，但古罗马的钉子显然仍是钉子。

paras.en: It would be absurd to try to track the changing price of sports cars since 1695, but to ask the same question of nails makes perfect sense.
paras.zh: 试图追踪跑车自1695年以来的价格变化会很荒唐，但对钉子提出同样的问题却完全说得通。

w.m: 完全说得通；非常有道理

paras.en: I make no apology for being obsessed by a particular feature of these objects: their price.
paras.zh: 我痴迷于这些物品的一个特定方面——它们的价格，对此我并不觉得有什么可抱歉的。

paras.en: I am an economist, after all.
paras.zh: 毕竟，我是个经济学家。

paras.en: One thing I’ve learnt from writing two books about the history of inventions is that while it is the enchantingly sophisticated technologies that get all the hype, it’s the cheap technologies that change the world.
paras.zh: 在写两本发明史著作的过程中，我认识到一点：虽然受到大肆炒作的都是那些精巧得令人着迷的技术，但改变世界的却是廉价技术。

w.m: adv. 令人着迷地；迷人地
adj. 精巧的；复杂精密的

paras.en: The Gutenberg printing press transformed civilisation not by changing the nature of writing but by changing its cost—and it would have achieved little without a parallel collapse in the price of surfaces to write on, thanks to an often-overlooked technology called paper.
paras.zh: 古登堡印刷机彻底改变了文明，靠的不是改变书写的本质，而是改变书写的成本；而且，如果不是书写载体的价格同时暴跌，它也难有多大作为——这次暴跌要归功于一项常被忽视的技术：纸。

w.m: adj. 同时发生的；平行的

paras.en: Solar panels had few niche uses until they became cheap; now they are transforming the global energy system.
paras.zh: 在变得便宜之前，太阳能电池板只有寥寥几种小众用途；如今，它们正在彻底改变全球能源体系。

passages.name: 2024年考研英语一 Text 2
passages.title: 狩猎采集者育儿方式的启示
passages.genre: 说明文 · 育儿与家庭
passages.summary: 研究人员提出，要养育出更有满足感的孩子，关键或许就在于从非洲狩猎采集者那里获得的育儿窍门。这一观点基于对博茨瓦纳昆族等社群的研究，在昆族中，每个孩子都由许多成年人照料；剑桥大学的乔杜里博士认为，这种被称为“异亲抚育”的做法可能会减轻儿童和父母的焦虑；儿童精神科医生斯瓦内普尔博士认为，有办法把这些做法融入西方生活，德国一个把养老院和托儿所结对、由老人帮忙照看孩子的项目就类似于异亲抚育。研究人员认为，西方的核心家庭是晚近才出现的发明，骤然转向“密集母职叙事”很可能是有害的；乔杜里指出，引入额外的照料者可能会减轻压力和母亲抑郁。研究人员还说，西方的“指导式教学”可能是导致注意缺陷多动障碍等病症的原因之一。

paras.en: Parenting tips obtained from hunter-gatherers in Africa may be the key to bringing up more contented children, researchers have suggested.
paras.zh: 研究人员提出，要养育出更有满足感的孩子，关键或许就在于从非洲狩猎采集者那里获得的育儿窍门。

paras.en: The idea is based on studies of communities such as the Kung of Botswana, where each child is cared for by many adults.
paras.zh: 这一观点的依据，是对博茨瓦纳昆族等社群的研究；在昆族中，每个孩子都由许多成年人照料。

paras.en: Kung children as young as four will help to look after younger ones, and “baby-wearing”, in which infants are carried in slings, is considered the norm.
paras.zh: 昆族孩子年仅四岁就会帮忙照看更小的孩子，而“背娃”——用背巾把婴儿兜在身上——被视为常态。

w.m: n. 背娃（用背巾把婴儿带在身上）

paras.en: According to Dr Nikhil Chaudhary, an evolutionary anthropologist at Cambridge University, these practices, known as alloparenting, could lead to less anxiety for children and parents.
paras.zh: 据剑桥大学进化人类学家尼基尔·乔杜里博士说，这些被称为“异亲抚育”的做法可能会减轻儿童和父母的焦虑。

w.m: n. 异亲抚育（由父母以外的人参与照料孩子）

paras.en: Dr Annie Swanepoel, a child psychiatrist, believes that there are ways to incorporate them into western life.
paras.zh: 儿童精神科医生安妮·斯瓦内普尔博士认为，有办法把这些做法融入西方生活。

w.m: n. 精神科医生；精神病学家

paras.en: In Germany, one scheme has paired an old people’s home with a nursery.
paras.zh: 德国有一个项目把一家养老院和一所托儿所结成了对子。

paras.en: The residents help to look after the children, an arrangement akin to alloparenting.
paras.zh: 养老院的老人帮忙照看孩子，这种安排类似于异亲抚育。

w.m: n. 居民；（养老院等机构的）入住者

paras.en: Another measure could be encouraging friendships between children in different school years, to mirror the unsupervised mixed-age playgroups in hunter-gatherer communities.
paras.zh: 另一项措施或许是鼓励不同年级的孩子相互交朋友，以此再现狩猎采集社群中那种无人看管的混龄玩伴群体。

w.m: adj. 无人看管的；无人监督的
n. 玩伴群体；游戏小组

paras.en: In a paper published in the Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry, researchers said that the western nuclear family was a recent invention which broke with evolutionary history.
paras.zh: 研究人员在《儿童心理学与精神病学杂志》上发表的一篇论文中称，西方的核心家庭是晚近才出现的发明，背离了进化史。

w.m: n. 发明；创造出来的事物

paras.en: This abrupt shift to an “intensive mothering narrative”, which suggests that mothers should manage childcare alone, was likely to have been harmful.
paras.zh: 这样骤然转向“密集母职叙事”很可能是有害的；这种叙事认为，母亲应该独自承担育儿事务。

paras.en: “Such narratives can lead to maternal exhaustion and have dangerous consequences,” they wrote.
paras.zh: 他们写道：“这样的叙事可能导致母亲精疲力竭，并带来危险的后果。”

w.m: n. 精疲力竭；筋疲力尽

paras.en: By contrast, in hunter-gatherer societies adults other than the parents can provide almost half of a child’s care.
paras.zh: 相比之下，在狩猎采集社会中，父母以外的成年人可以承担孩子近一半的照料工作。

paras.en: One previous study looked at the Efé people of the Democratic Republic of Congo.
paras.zh: 此前的一项研究考察了刚果民主共和国的埃费人。

paras.en: It found that infants had an average of 14 alloparents a day by the time they were 18 weeks old, and were passed between caregivers eight times an hour.
paras.zh: 该研究发现，婴儿长到18周大时，平均每天有14位异亲抚育者，而且每小时要在照料者之间换手八次。

w.m: n. 异亲抚育者（父母以外参与照料孩子的人）
v. 传递；（从一人手中）递给（另一人）

paras.en: Chaudhary said that parents now have less childcare support from family and social networks than during most of humans’ evolutionary history, but introducing additional caregivers could reduce stress and maternal depression, which could have a “knock-on” benefit to a child’s wellbeing.
paras.zh: 乔杜里说，与人类进化史上的大部分时期相比，如今父母从家人和社会关系网中获得的育儿支持更少；但引入额外的照料者可能会减轻压力和母亲抑郁，进而可能给孩子的身心健康带来“连带”益处。

paras.en: An infant born into a hunter-gatherer society could have more than ten caregivers—this contrasts starkly with nursery settings in the UK where regulations call for a ratio of one carer to four children aged two to three.
paras.zh: 出生在狩猎采集社会的婴儿可能有超过十位照料者，这与英国的托儿机构形成了鲜明对比：在英国，相关规定要求照看两到三岁儿童的保育员与儿童之比为一比四。

w.m: n. 场所；机构（此处指托儿机构）

paras.en: While hunter-gatherer children learnt from observation and imitation in mixed-age playgroups, researchers said that western “instructive teaching”, where pupils are asked to sit still, may contribute to conditions such as attention deficit hyperactivity disorder.
paras.zh: 狩猎采集社会的孩子在混龄玩伴群体中通过观察和模仿来学习，而研究人员说，西方那种要求学生坐着不动的“指导式教学”，可能是导致注意缺陷多动障碍等病症的原因之一。

w.m: n. 玩伴群体；游戏小组
adj. 指导性的；有教育意义的

paras.en: Chaudhary said that Britain should explore the possibility that older siblings helping their parents “might also enhance their own social development.”
paras.zh: 乔杜里说，英国应该探讨这样一种可能性：哥哥姐姐通过帮助父母，“或许也能促进自身的社会性发展”。

passages.name: 2024年考研英语一 Text 3
passages.title: 人工智能文生图引发伦理与版权难题
passages.genre: 说明文 · 科技与艺术
passages.summary: 波兰数字艺术家格雷格·鲁特科夫斯基的独特风格已成为开源人工智能艺术生成工具Stable Diffusion中最常用的提示词之一。这类开源程序靠从互联网上抓取图像构建起来，往往未经许可，也没有恰当地为艺术家署名，因此正在引发伦理和版权方面的棘手问题。鲁特科夫斯基担心，互联网将充斥人工智能艺术作品，他很可能在网上找不到自己的作品；艺术家们也表示面临损失收入的风险，一些人正在奋起反击。插画师卡拉·奥尔蒂斯说，艺术相关行业内部有一个联盟正在壮大，设法应对或缓解这一问题；有一种建议是，人工智能模型可以用公有领域的图像来训练，人工智能公司也可以与博物馆和艺术家建立合作伙伴关系。

paras.en: A Polish digital artist who uses classical painting styles to create dreamy fantasy landscapes, Greg Rutkowski has made illustrations for games such as Dungeons & Dragons and Magic: The Gathering.
paras.zh: 格雷格·鲁特科夫斯基是一位波兰数字艺术家，他运用古典绘画风格创作梦幻般的奇幻风景画，曾为《龙与地下城》和《万智牌》等游戏绘制插画。

paras.en: And he’s become a sudden hit in the new world of text-to-image AI generation.
paras.zh: 而在人工智能文生图这个新天地里，他突然走红了。

w.m: n. 红人；风靡一时的人（或事物）
adj. 文本生成图像的；文生图的

paras.en: His distinctive style is now one of the most commonly used prompts in the new open-source AI art generator Stable Diffusion.
paras.zh: 在新推出的开源人工智能艺术生成工具Stable Diffusion中，他那独特的风格如今是最常用的提示词之一。

w.m: adj. 独特的；与众不同的

paras.en: The tool, along with other popular image-generation AI models, allows anyone to create impressive images based on text prompts.
paras.zh: 这款工具连同其他流行的图像生成人工智能模型，都能让任何人根据文本提示词生成令人惊叹的图像。

w.m: adj. 令人惊叹的；给人深刻印象的

paras.en: For example, type in “Wizard with sword and a glowing orb of magic fire fights a fierce dragon Greg Rutkowski,” and the system will produce something that looks not a million miles away from works in Rutkowski’s style.
paras.zh: 例如，输入“手持利剑和一团发光魔法火球的巫师与一条凶猛的龙搏斗，格雷格·鲁特科夫斯基”，系统就会生成一幅图像，看上去与鲁特科夫斯基风格的作品相差无几。

w.h: not a million miles away from

paras.en: But these open-source programs are built by scraping images from the internet, often without permission and proper attribution to artists.
paras.zh: 但这些开源程序是靠从互联网上抓取图像构建起来的，而且往往未经许可，也没有恰当地为艺术家署名。

paras.en: As a result, they are raising tricky questions about ethics and copyright.
paras.zh: 因此，这些程序正在引发有关伦理和版权的棘手问题。

w.m: n. 伦理（问题）；道德准则

paras.en: And artists like Rutkowski have had enough.
paras.zh: 而像鲁特科夫斯基这样的艺术家已经受够了。

paras.en: According to the website Lexica, which tracks over 10 million images and prompts generated by Stable Diffusion, Rutkowski’s name has been used as a prompt around 93,000 times.
paras.zh: Lexica网站追踪着超过1000万个由Stable Diffusion生成的图像和提示词；据该网站统计，鲁特科夫斯基的名字已作为提示词使用了约93,000次。

paras.en: Rutkowski was initially surprised but thought it might be a good way to reach new audiences.
paras.zh: 鲁特科夫斯基起初很惊讶，但又觉得这或许是接触新受众的好办法。

w.m: v. 接触到；（信息等）传达到

paras.en: Then he tried searching for his name to see if a piece he had worked on had been published.
paras.zh: 后来，他试着搜索自己的名字，想看看自己创作过的一件作品是否已经发表。

paras.en: The online search brought back work that had his name attached to it but wasn’t his.
paras.zh: 网上搜索返回的结果中，有些作品挂着他的名字，却并非出自他手。

paras.en: “It’s been just a month.
paras.zh: “这才过了一个月。

paras.en: What about in a year?
paras.zh: 一年以后又会怎样？

paras.en: I probably won’t be able to find my work out there because the internet will be flooded with AI art,” Rutkowski says.
paras.zh: 我很可能没法在网上找到自己的作品了，因为互联网上将充斥着人工智能艺术作品。”鲁特科夫斯基说。

w.m: 在外面（的世界）；（此处指）在网上

paras.en: “That’s concerning.”
paras.zh: “这令人担忧。”

paras.en: Other artists besides Rutkowski have been surprised by the apparent popularity of their work in text-to-image generators—and some are now fighting back.
paras.zh: 除了鲁特科夫斯基，其他艺术家也惊讶地发现，自己的作品在文生图工具中似乎很受欢迎——一些人如今正在奋起反击。

w.m: adj. 看来（如此）的；表面上的
adj. 文本生成图像的；文生图的

paras.en: Karla Ortiz, an illustrator based in San Francisco who found her work in Stable Diffusion’s data set, has been raising awareness about the issues around AI art and copyright.
paras.zh: 常驻旧金山的插画师卡拉·奥尔蒂斯在Stable Diffusion的数据集中发现了自己的作品，她一直在提高人们对人工智能艺术与版权相关问题的认识。

w.m: 常驻（某地）；以（某地）为基地

paras.en: Artists say they risk losing income as people start using AI-generated images based on copyrighted material for commercial purposes.
paras.zh: 艺术家们说，随着人们开始将人工智能根据受版权保护的素材生成的图像用于商业目的，他们面临着损失收入的风险。

paras.en: But it’s also a lot more personal, Ortiz says, arguing that because art is so closely linked to a person, it could raise data protection and privacy problems.
paras.zh: 但奥尔蒂斯说，这件事与个人相关的程度还要深得多。她认为，由于艺术与人本身联系如此紧密，这可能会引发数据保护和隐私问题。

paras.en: “There is a coalition growing within artist industries to figure out how to tackle or mitigate this,” says Ortiz.
paras.zh: “在艺术相关行业内部，一个联盟正在壮大，目的是弄清楚该如何应对或缓解这一问题。”奥尔蒂斯说。

paras.en: The group is in its early days of mobilization, which could involve pushing for new policies or regulation.
paras.zh: 这个联盟正处于动员初期，动员可能包括推动出台新的政策或法规。

paras.en: One suggestion is that AI models could be trained on images in the public domain, and AI companies could forge partnerships with museums and artists, Ortiz says.
paras.zh: 奥尔蒂斯说，有一种建议是：人工智能模型可以用公有领域的图像来训练，人工智能公司也可以与博物馆和艺术家建立合作伙伴关系。

w.m: 属于公有领域的；不受版权保护的

passages.name: 2024年考研英语一 Text 4
passages.title: 湿地保护范围收窄危及切萨皮克湾
passages.genre: 议论文 · 环境与法律
passages.summary: 切萨皮克湾的浅水区为数百个物种提供栖息地，还能储存洪水、过滤污染物、保护附近社区免受风暴潮侵袭。美国最高法院上个月下旬的一项裁决大大缩小了环境保护署监管湿地和水道的权力，使这一切面临巨大风险。作者指出，水和污染物不受州界限制，只看马里兰州本州的湿地保护法律是短视的；环境保护署参与切萨皮克湾计划长期以来至关重要；作者因此呼吁各州立法者考虑重新审视本州的湿地保护措施。

paras.en: The miracle of the Chesapeake Bay lies not in its depths, but in the complexity of its natural construction, the interaction of fresh and saline waters, and the mix of land and water.
paras.zh: 切萨皮克湾的神奇之处不在于水深，而在于其天然构造的复杂性、淡水与咸水的交互作用，以及水陆的交错相间。

w.m: n. 相互作用；交互作用

paras.en: The shallows provide homes for hundreds of species while storing floodwaters, filtering pollutants from water, and protecting nearby communities from potentially destructive storm surges.
paras.zh: 湾内的浅水区为数百个物种提供栖息地，同时还储存洪水、过滤水中的污染物，并保护附近社区免受可能具有破坏性的风暴潮侵袭。

paras.en: All this was put at great risk late last month, when the U.S. Supreme Court issued a ruling in an Idaho case that provides the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) far less authority to regulate wetlands and waterways.
paras.zh: 上个月下旬，这一切都面临巨大风险：美国最高法院就爱达荷州的一起案件作出裁决，大大缩小了美国环境保护署（EPA）监管湿地和水道的权力。

w.m: adv. 在（某段时间的）后期

paras.en: Specifically, a 5-4 majority decided that wetlands protected by the EPA under its Clean Water Act authority must have a “continuous surface connection” to bodies of water.
paras.zh: 具体而言，最高法院以5比4的多数裁定：环境保护署依据《清洁水法》授权保护的湿地，必须与水体存在“连续的地表连接”。

w.m: adv. 具体来说；具体而言
adj. 连续的；持续不断的

paras.en: This narrowing of the regulatory scope was a victory for builders, mining operators and other commercial interests often at odds with environmental rules.
paras.zh: 监管范围就此收窄，对建筑商、矿业经营者以及其他常与环保法规相抵触的商业利益方而言，这是一场胜利。

paras.en: And it carries “significant repercussions for water quality and flood control throughout the United States,” as Justice Brett Kavanaugh observed.
paras.zh: 而且，正如大法官布雷特·卡瓦诺所指出的，此举会“给全美各地的水质和防洪带来重大影响”。

paras.en: In Maryland, the good news is that there are many state laws in place that provide wetlands protections.
paras.zh: 对马里兰州来说，好消息是，本州已有许多法律在施行，为湿地提供保护。

paras.en: But that’s a very shortsighted view, particularly when it comes to the Chesapeake Bay.
paras.zh: 但这种看法非常短视，尤其是就切萨皮克湾而言。

w.m: adj. 短视的；目光短浅的

paras.en: The reality is that water, and the pollutants that so often come with it, don’t respect state boundaries.
paras.zh: 现实是，水以及往往随水而来的污染物，都不会顾及州界。

paras.en: The Chesapeake draws from a 64,000-square-mile watershed that extends into Virginia, Pennsylvania, New York, West Virginia, the District of Columbia and Delaware.
paras.zh: 切萨皮克湾的水源来自一片面积为64,000平方英里的流域，这片流域延伸至弗吉尼亚州、宾夕法尼亚州、纽约州、西弗吉尼亚州、哥伦比亚特区和特拉华州。

paras.en: Will those jurisdictions extend the same protections now denied under Sackett v. EPA?
paras.zh: 如今依据萨克特诉环境保护署案被剥夺的那些保护，这些辖区会不会同样提供？

w.m: prep. （用于诉讼案名）诉（versus的缩写）
n. （美国）环境保护署（Environmental Protection Agency的缩写）

paras.en: Perhaps some, but all?
paras.zh: 或许有一些会，但所有辖区都会吗？

paras.en: That seems unlikely.
paras.zh: 这似乎不太可能。

paras.en: It is too easy, and misleading, to see such court rulings as merely standing up for the rights of landowners when the consequences can be so dire for their neighbors.
paras.zh: 把这类法院裁决仅仅看作是在维护土地所有者的权利，未免过于简单，也具有误导性，因为这些裁决给土地所有者的邻居带来的后果可能极为严重。

w.m: adj. 误导性的；引人误解的
adj. 极其严重的；可怕的

paras.en: And it’s a reminder that the EPA’s involvement in the Chesapeake Bay Program has long been crucial as the means to transcend the influence of deep-pocketed special interests in neighboring states.
paras.zh: 而这也提醒我们：长期以来，环境保护署参与切萨皮克湾计划一直至关重要，是摆脱邻近各州财大气粗的特殊利益集团影响的手段。

w.m: n. 提醒；令人想起……的事物
adj. 财大气粗的；财力雄厚的

paras.en: Pennsylvania farmers, to use one telling example, aren’t thinking about next year’s blue crab harvest in Maryland when they decide whether to spread animal waste on their fields, yet the runoff into nearby creeks can have enormous impact downstream.
paras.zh: 举一个很能说明问题的例子：宾夕法尼亚州的农民在决定是否往自家田里撒施动物粪便时，不会去考虑马里兰州明年的蓝蟹收成，然而，流入附近溪流的径流可能会对下游产生巨大影响。

w.m: adj. 很能说明问题的；有力的
n. 径流；（地表）流失的水

paras.en: And so we would call on state lawmakers from Richmond to Albany to consider reviewing their own wetlands protections and see for themselves the enormous stakes involved.
paras.zh: 因此，我们想呼吁从里士满到奥尔巴尼的各州立法者考虑重新审视本州的湿地保护措施，亲自看看其中涉及的利害关系有多么重大。

w.m: adj. 涉及的；牵涉在内的

paras.en: We can offer them a visit to Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge in Dorchester County, where bald eagles fly over tidal marshes so shallow you could not paddle a boat across them but teeming with aquatic life.
paras.zh: 我们可以安排他们去多切斯特县的布莱克沃特国家野生动物保护区参观，那里有白头海雕在潮汐沼泽上空飞翔，这些沼泽浅得连船都划不过去，却到处都是水生生物。

w.m: adj. 潮汐的；受潮汐影响的
adv. 如此（so…+省略that的结果从句：如此……以至于）

paras.en: It’s worth the scenic drive.
paras.zh: 一路风景优美，驱车前往很值得。

passages.name: 2024年考研英语二 Text 1
passages.title: 科技不平等或阻碍人工智能发展
passages.genre: 议论文 · 科技与经济
passages.summary: 剑桥大学经济学家黛安·科伊尔在新书中提出，数字经济需要用新的方式来思考进步，增长的成果必须比近些年分享得更均衡。她担心科技行业的不平等问题可能会阻碍人工智能的部署：如果人们看不到好处，就不能指望他们接受变革。目前人工智能的发明和商业化由少数城市主导，这意味着地区间的财富差距将继续急剧扩大，不仅会助长动荡，还可能阻碍地区经济增长所需的人工智能技术的发展。作者认为，部分解决办法或许在于放松大型科技公司对人工智能议程的钳制，能更快着手的办法则是拓宽数字想象力，构想出不是简单地取代工作、而是能扩大机会的人工智能技术。

paras.en: In her new book Cogs and Monsters: What Economics Is, and What It Should Be, Diane Coyle, an economist at Cambridge University, argues that the digital economy requires new ways of thinking about progress.
paras.zh: 剑桥大学经济学家黛安·科伊尔在新书《齿轮与怪兽：经济学是什么，又应该是什么》中提出，数字经济需要用新的方式来思考进步。

paras.en: “Whatever we mean by the economy growing, by things getting better, the gains will have to be more evenly shared than in the recent past,” she writes.
paras.zh: “无论我们所说的经济增长、情况好转是什么意思，其成果都必须比近些年分享得更均衡。”她写道。

paras.en: “An economy of tech millionaires or billionaires and gig workers, with middle-income jobs undercut by automation, will not be politically sustainable.”
paras.zh: “一边是科技界的百万富翁或亿万富翁，一边是打零工的人，中等收入的工作又遭自动化蚕食，这样的经济在政治上将无法持续。”

paras.en: Improving living standards and increasing prosperity for more people will require greater use of digital technologies to boost productivity in various sectors, including health care and construction, says Coyle.
paras.zh: 科伊尔说，要提高生活水平、让更多人更加富裕，就需要更多地利用数字技术，来提高包括医疗保健和建筑业在内的各个行业的生产率。

paras.en: But people can’t be expected to embrace the changes if they’re not seeing the benefits—if they’re just seeing good jobs being destroyed.
paras.zh: 但如果人们看不到好处，只看到好工作不断被毁掉，就不能指望他们欣然接受这些变革。

paras.en: In a recent interview, Coyle said she fears that tech’s inequality problem could be a roadblock to deploying AI.
paras.zh: 在最近的一次采访中，科伊尔表示，她担心科技行业的不平等问题可能会成为部署人工智能的障碍。

w.m: n. 人工智能（artificial intelligence 的缩写）

paras.en: “We’re talking about disruption,” she says.
paras.zh: “我们谈论的是颠覆性的变革。”她说。

paras.en: “These are transformative technologies that change the ways we spend our time every day, that change business models that succeed.”
paras.zh: “这些都是变革性的技术，它们改变着我们每天怎样花时间，也改变着哪些商业模式能够成功。”

w.m: adj. 变革性的；有改造作用的

paras.en: To make such “tremendous changes,” she adds, you need social buy-in.
paras.zh: 她补充说，要实现这种“巨大的变革”，就需要得到社会的认同。

paras.en: Instead, says Coyle, resentment is simmering among many as the benefits are perceived to go to elites in a handful of prosperous cities.
paras.zh: 科伊尔说，现实却是，由于人们认为好处流向了少数几个繁荣城市的精英，许多人心中的不满正在酝酿。

paras.en: According to the Brookings Institution, a short list of eight American cities that included San Francisco, San Jose, Boston, and Seattle had roughly 38% of all tech jobs by 2019.
paras.zh: 据布鲁金斯学会称，到2019年，包括旧金山、圣何塞、波士顿和西雅图在内的区区8个美国城市就约占所有科技岗位的38%。

paras.en: New AI technologies are particularly concentrated: Brookings’s Mark Muro and Sifan Liu estimate that just 15 cities account for two-thirds of the AI assets and capabilities in the United States.
paras.zh: 新的人工智能技术尤其集中：据布鲁金斯学会的马克·穆罗和刘思凡估计，仅15个城市就占了美国人工智能资产和能力的三分之二。

paras.en: The dominance of a few cities in the invention and commercialization of AI means that geographical disparities in wealth will continue to soar.
paras.zh: 少数几个城市在人工智能的发明和商业化方面占据主导地位，这意味着地区间的财富差距将继续急剧扩大。

paras.en: Not only will this foster political and social unrest, but it could, as Coyle suggests, hold back the sorts of AI technologies needed for regional economies to grow.
paras.zh: 这不仅会助长政治和社会动荡，而且正如科伊尔所说，还可能阻碍地区经济增长所需的那类人工智能技术的发展。

w.m: 不仅……而且（not only 位于句首时句子部分倒装）

paras.en: Part of the solution could lie in somehow loosening the stranglehold that Big Tech has on defining the AI agenda.
paras.zh: 大型科技公司牢牢把持着确定人工智能议程的权力，部分解决办法或许在于设法放松这种钳制。

w.m: 大型科技公司；科技巨头

paras.en: That will likely take increased federal funding for research independent of the tech giants.
paras.zh: 这很可能需要联邦政府加大资助力度，支持独立于科技巨头的研究。

paras.en: A more immediate response is to broaden our digital imaginations to conceive of AI technologies that don’t simply replace jobs but expand opportunities in the sectors that different parts of the country care most about, like health care, education, and manufacturing.
paras.zh: 一个能更快着手的应对办法是拓宽我们的数字想象力，构想出这样的人工智能技术：它们不是简单地取代工作岗位，而是在国内不同地区最关心的行业（比如医疗保健、教育和制造业）中扩大机会。

passages.name: 2024年考研英语二 Text 2
passages.title: 未能植树产材，英国恐陷建筑业危机
passages.genre: 说明文 · 环境与经济
passages.summary: 英国林业与木材行业组织Confor警告，由于未能植树产材，英国未来将面临建筑业危机。目前英国所需木材只有20%产自本土，英国仍是世界第二大木材净进口国；该组织认为，政府为鼓励土地所有者多种树而出台的新激励措施力度不够，政府扶持的重点仍是粮食生产，以及纯粹为了生物多样性而开展的再野化和原生林地种植。Confor呼吁为实现增加植树的目标注入大得多的动力，以确保有足够的木材满足日益增长的需求。

paras.en: The UK is facing a future construction crisis because of a failure to plant trees to produce wood, Confor has warned.
paras.zh: Confor警告称，由于未能植树产材，英国未来将面临一场建筑业危机。

paras.en: The forestry and wood trade body has called for urgent action to reduce the country’s reliance on timber imports and provide a stable supply of wood for future generations.
paras.zh: 这家林业与木材行业组织呼吁采取紧急行动，减少英国对进口木材的依赖，并为子孙后代提供稳定的木材供应。

paras.en: Currently only 20 percent of the UK’s wood requirement is home-grown while it remains the second-largest net importer of timber in the world.
paras.zh: 目前英国所需木材只有20%产自本土，而英国仍是世界第二大木材净进口国。

w.m: adj. 本土种植的；国产的

paras.en: At a time of fresh incentives from the UK government for landowners to grow more trees, the trade body says these don’t go far enough and fail to promote the benefits of planting them to boost timber supplies.
paras.zh: 在英国政府出台新的激励措施、鼓励土地所有者多种树之际，这家行业组织表示，这些措施力度不够，也未能宣传为增加木材供应而植树的好处。

paras.en: “Not only are we facing a carbon crisis now, but we will also be facing a future construction crisis because of a failure to plant trees to produce wood,” said Stuart Goodall, chief executive of Confor.
paras.zh: Confor首席执行官斯图尔特·古道尔说：“我们现在不仅面临碳危机，而且由于未能植树产材，未来还将面临建筑业危机。”

w.m: 不仅……而且（Not only置于句首时句子部分倒装）

paras.en: “For decades we have not taken responsibility for investing in our domestic wood supply, leaving us exposed to fluctuating prices and fighting for future supplies of wood as global demand rises and our own supplies fall.”
paras.zh: “几十年来，我们一直没有承担起投资国内木材供应的责任，这使我们不仅容易受到价格波动的冲击，而且随着全球需求上升、我们自己的供应减少，还不得不去争夺未来的木材供应。”

w.m: adj. 波动的；起伏不定的

paras.en: The UK has ideal conditions for growing wood to build low-carbon homes and is a global leader in certifying that its forests are sustainably managed, Confor says.
paras.zh: Confor表示，英国拥有种树产材以建造低碳住宅的理想条件，并且在认证本国森林的可持续经营方面处于全球领先地位。

paras.en: While around three quarters of Scottish homes are built from Scottish timber, the use of home-grown wood in England is only around 25 percent.
paras.zh: 苏格兰约四分之三的住宅是用苏格兰木材建造的，而在英格兰，本土木材的使用比例只有25%左右。

w.m: adj. 本土种植的；国产的

paras.en: The causes of the UK’s current position are complex and range from outdated perceptions of productive forestry to the decimation of trees by grey squirrels.
paras.zh: 造成英国目前这种状况的原因很复杂，从人们对生产性林业的过时看法，到灰松鼠对树木的大肆毁坏，不一而足。

w.m: adj. 生产性的（以产出木材等为目的的）
n. 大量毁灭；大批杀死

paras.en: They also encompass significant hesitation on the part of farmers and other landowners to invest in long-term planting projects.
paras.zh: 这些原因还包括：农民和其他土地所有者在投资长期植树项目方面相当犹豫。

paras.en: While productive tree planting can deliver real financial benefits to rural economies and contribute to the UK’s net-zero strategy, the focus of government support continues to be on food production and the rewilding and planting of native woodland solely for biodiversity.
paras.zh: 尽管生产性植树能为农村经济带来真金白银的收益，并有助于实现英国的净零排放战略，但政府扶持的重点仍然是粮食生产，以及纯粹为了生物多样性而开展的再野化和原生林地种植。

w.m: adj. 生产性的（以产出木材等为目的的）
adj. 实实在在的；真正的
n. 再野化（让土地恢复自然状态）

paras.en: Goodall added: “While food production and biodiversity health are clearly of critical importance, we need our land to also provide secure supplies of wood for construction and manufacturing, and contribute to net zero.”
paras.zh: 古道尔补充说：“粮食生产和生物多样性的健康显然至关重要，但我们也需要自己的土地为建筑业和制造业提供有保障的木材供应，并助力实现净零排放。”

w.m: adj. 有保障的；稳定可靠的

paras.en: “While the UK government has stated its ambition for more tree planting, there has been little action on the ground.
paras.zh: “虽然英国政府已提出增加植树的目标，但实地行动却寥寥无几。

w.m: adj. （与不可数名词连用）很少的；几乎没有的

paras.en: Confor is now calling for much greater impetus behind those aspirations to ensure we have enough wood to meet increasing demand.”
paras.zh: Confor现在呼吁为实现这些目标注入大得多的动力，以确保我们有足够的木材来满足日益增长的需求。”

w.m: adj. 日益增长的；不断增加的

passages.name: 2024年考研英语二 Text 3
passages.title: 老年司机的行车安全难题
passages.genre: 说明文 · 交通与老龄化
passages.summary: 要让开车不安全的老年司机不再上路，最大的挑战之一是说服他们交出车钥匙。前风险经理门克指出，美国医学会建议医生在特定情况下通知机动车管理局，而各州对医生上报的规定各不相同。老年学家杜根认为，在保障老年司机安全方面，部分问题在于相关难题由各类专业人员零敲碎打地处理，并指出需要更充分的证据；据一项研究，强制要求亲自到场更新驾照与涉及85岁及以上司机的致命车祸减少相关联。杜根还认为，只要路上还有其他汽车，自动驾驶汽车就解决不了车祸问题，但我们仍需做更多工作来提高安全性：如果人要活到100岁，就需要90岁老人也能开得舒舒服服的汽车。

paras.en: One of the biggest challenges in keeping unsafe aging drivers off the road is convincing them that it’s time to turn over the keys.
paras.zh: 要让开车不安全的老年司机不再上路，最大的挑战之一是说服他们：是时候交出车钥匙了。

w.m: adj. 年老的；日渐衰老的

paras.en: “It’s a complete life-changer” when someone stops—or is forced to stop—driving, said former risk manager Anne M. Menke.
paras.zh: 前风险经理安妮·M.门克说，有人不再开车（或是被迫不再开车）时，“这会彻底改变一个人的生活”。

w.m: n. 彻底改变人生的事

paras.en: “The American Medical Association advises physicians that in situations where clear evidence of substantial driving impairment implies a strong threat to patient and public safety, and where the physician’s advice to discontinue driving privileges is ignored, it is desirable and ethical to notify the Department of Motor Vehicles,” Menke wrote.
paras.zh: 门克写道：“美国医学会建议医生：如果有明确证据表明驾驶能力严重受损，意味着患者和公共安全面临重大威胁，而且医生关于中止驾驶资格的建议遭到无视，那么通知机动车管理局既是可取的，也是合乎伦理的。”

w.m: adj. 合乎伦理的；合乎道德的

paras.en: “Some states require physicians to report; others allow but do not mandate reports, while a few consider a report a breach of confidentiality.
paras.zh: “有些州要求医生上报；有些州允许上报，但不强制；还有少数州则认为上报违反了保密义务。

paras.en: There could be liability and penalties if a physician does not act in accordance with state laws on reporting and confidentiality,” she counseled.
paras.zh: 如果医生不依照州里有关上报和保密的法律行事，就可能要承担法律责任、受到处罚。”她告诫说。

paras.en: Part of the problem in keeping older drivers safe is that the difficulties are addressed piecemeal by different professionals with different focuses, including gerontologists, highway administration officials, automotive engineers and others, said gerontologist Elizabeth Dugan.
paras.zh: 老年学家伊丽莎白·杜根说，在保障老年司机安全方面，部分问题在于：这些难题由关注重点各不相同的各类专业人员——包括老年学家、公路管理官员、汽车工程师等——零敲碎打地处理。

w.m: adv. 零敲碎打地；零碎地

paras.en: “There’s not a National Institute of Older Driver Studies,” she said.
paras.zh: 她说：“并没有一家国家老年司机研究院。”

paras.en: “We need better evidence on what makes drivers unsafe” and what can help, said Dugan.
paras.zh: 杜根说，“我们需要更充分的证据，弄清是什么让司机开车变得不安全”，也要弄清什么能有所帮助。

paras.en: One thing that does seem to work is requiring drivers to report in person for license renewal.
paras.zh: 有一种做法看来确实有效，那就是要求司机亲自到场更新驾照。

paras.en: Mandatory in-person renewal was associated with a 31 percent reduction in fatal crashes involving drivers 85 or older, according to one study.
paras.zh: 据一项研究，强制要求亲自到场更新驾照，与涉及85岁及以上司机的致命车祸减少31%相关联。

w.m: adj. 亲自（到场）的；当面的

paras.en: Passing vision tests also produced a similar decline in fatal crashes for those drivers, although there appeared to be no benefit from combining the two.
paras.zh: 通过视力测试也让这些司机的致命车祸出现了类似的降幅，不过把两者结合起来似乎并不能带来额外的好处。

paras.en: Many older drivers don’t see eye doctors or can’t afford to.
paras.zh: 许多老年司机不去看眼科医生，或者负担不起看眼科的费用。

paras.en: Primary care providers have their hands full and may not be able to follow through with patients who have trouble driving because they can’t turn their heads or remember where they are going—or have gotten shorter and haven’t changed their seat settings sufficiently to reach car pedals easily.
paras.zh: 初级保健人员本就忙得不可开交，可能无法对开车有困难的患者跟进到底——这些患者开车困难，是因为转不了头，或者记不住自己要去哪里，又或者是个子变矮了，却没有充分调整座椅设置，因而无法轻松够到汽车踏板。

w.m: n. 提供者；（医疗）服务人员
跟进到底；（对……）坚持处理完

paras.en: As long as there are other cars on the roads, self-driving cars won’t solve the problems of crashes, said Dugan.
paras.zh: 杜根说，只要路上还有其他汽车，自动驾驶汽车就解决不了车祸问题。

paras.en: Avoiding dangers posed by all those human drivers would require too many algorithms, she said.
paras.zh: 她说，要避开所有那些人类司机带来的危险，需要的算法就太多了。

paras.en: But we need to do more to improve safety, said Dugan.
paras.zh: 杜根说，不过我们仍需做更多工作来提高安全性。

paras.en: “If we’re going to have 100-year lives, we need cars that a 90-year-old can drive comfortably.”
paras.zh: “如果我们将来要活到100岁，那就需要90岁的老人也能开得舒舒服服的汽车。”

passages.name: 2024年考研英语二 Text 4
passages.title: 健康应用的数据隐私保护问题
passages.genre: 说明文 · 科技与法律
passages.summary: 健康类应用数量庞大、上市速度很快，但我们输入的个人信息如何收集、保护和共享并不总是清楚；现行健康隐私法主要针对医院、诊所和保险公司等机构，这些应用收集的健康信息通常得不到同等的法律保护。联邦贸易委员会只能在事后对不公平或欺骗性行为采取执法行动，例如曾调查Flo Health公司并与其达成和解。评论人士认为，短期内似乎不太可能出台全面的联邦隐私立法，而加利福尼亚、弗吉尼亚等州已开始自行立法，以加强保护消费者生成的健康数据。

paras.en: If you look at the apps on your phone, chances are you have at least one related to your health—and probably several.
paras.zh: 看看你手机上的应用，其中很可能至少有一个与健康相关——而且多半有好几个。

paras.en: Whether it is a mental health app, a fitness tracker, a connected health device or something else, many of us are taking advantage of this technology to keep better track of our health in some shape or form.
paras.zh: 无论是心理健康应用、健身追踪器、联网健康设备还是别的什么，我们当中很多人都在以某种形式利用这项技术，更好地掌握自己的健康状况。

paras.en: Recent research from the Organisation for the Review of Care and Health Applications found that 350,000 health apps were available on the market, 90,000 of which launched in 2020 alone.
paras.zh: 护理与健康应用评审组织最近的研究发现，市场上有35万款健康应用，其中仅2020年一年就推出了9万款。

w.m: adj. 可获得的；可买到的

paras.en: While these apps have a great deal to offer, it is not always clear how the personal information we input is collected, safeguarded and shared online.
paras.zh: 虽然这些应用大有裨益，但我们输入的个人信息在网上是如何收集、保护和共享的，并不总是清楚。

w.h: have a great deal to offer
w.m: 大有裨益；能提供很多好处

paras.en: Existing health privacy law, such as the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, is primarily focused on the way hospitals, doctors’ offices, clinics and insurance companies store health records online.
paras.zh: 现行的健康隐私法，例如《健康保险流通与责任法案》，主要关注的是医院、医生诊室、诊所和保险公司在网上存储健康记录的方式。

w.m: n. 可转移性；（保险的）可携带性

paras.en: The health information these apps and health-data-tracking wearables are collecting typically does not receive the same legal protections.
paras.zh: 这些应用和追踪健康数据的可穿戴设备正在收集的健康信息，通常得不到同样的法律保护。

paras.en: Without additional protections in place, companies may share (and potentially monetize) personal health information in a way consumers may not have authorized or anticipated.
paras.zh: 如果没有落实额外的保护措施，企业可能会以消费者或许并未授权、也未曾预料的方式共享（并可能借此变现）个人健康信息。

paras.en: In 2021, Flo Health faced a Federal Trade Commission (FTC) investigation.
paras.zh: 2021年，Flo Health公司遭到联邦贸易委员会（FTC）的调查。

paras.en: The FTC alleged in a complaint that “despite express privacy claims, the company took control of users’ sensitive fertility data and shared it with third parties.”
paras.zh: 联邦贸易委员会在一份诉状中指控：“尽管有明确的隐私声明，该公司仍掌控了用户的敏感生育数据，并将其与第三方共享。”

paras.en: Flo Health and the FTC settled the matter with a Consent Order requiring the company to get app users’ express affirmative consent before sharing their health information as well as to instruct the third parties to delete the data they had obtained.
paras.zh: Flo Health公司与联邦贸易委员会通过一项同意令就此事达成和解，该同意令要求这家公司在共享应用用户的健康信息之前，必须征得用户明确的肯定性同意，还必须指示那些第三方删除其已获取的数据。

w.m: 同意令（经当事方同意的和解令）
adj. 肯定的；表示同意的

paras.en: Section 5 of the FTC Act empowers the FTC to initiate enforcement action against unfair or deceptive acts, meaning the FTC can only act after the fact if a company’s privacy practices are misleading or cause unjustified consumer harm.
paras.zh: 《联邦贸易委员会法》第5条授权该委员会对不公平或欺骗性行为发起执法行动，这意味着，如果某家公司的隐私做法具有误导性，或给消费者造成了不合理的损害，联邦贸易委员会只能在事后采取行动。

w.m: adj. 不合理的；无正当理由的

paras.en: While the FTC is doing what it can to ensure apps are keeping their promises to consumers around the handling of their sensitive health information, the rate at which these health apps are hitting the market demonstrates just how immense a challenge this is.
paras.zh: 尽管联邦贸易委员会正在尽其所能，确保各类应用在处理消费者敏感健康信息方面信守对消费者的承诺，但这些健康应用上市的速度表明，这是一项多么巨大的挑战。

paras.en: As to the prospects for federal legislation, commentators suggest that comprehensive federal privacy legislation seems unlikely in the short term.
paras.zh: 至于联邦立法的前景，评论人士认为，短期内似乎不太可能出台全面的联邦隐私立法。

paras.en: States have begun implementing their own solutions to shore up protections for consumer-generated health data.
paras.zh: 一些州已开始实施自己的解决方案，以加强对消费者生成的健康数据的保护。

paras.en: California has been at the forefront of state privacy efforts with the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018.
paras.zh: 加利福尼亚州凭借《2018年加州消费者隐私法》，一直走在各州隐私保护工作的前列。

w.m: 处于……的前列；在……的最前沿

paras.en: Virginia, Colorado and Utah have also recently passed state consumer data privacy legislation.
paras.zh: 弗吉尼亚州、科罗拉多州和犹他州最近也通过了州级消费者数据隐私立法。

passages.name: 2023年考研英语一 Text 1
passages.title: 美国学校气候变化教学之争
passages.genre: 说明文 · 教育与环境
passages.summary: 得克萨斯州教育委员会将就学校如何讲授气候变化展开辩论，委员帕特·哈迪认同能源行业的观点，抵制对青春期前学生科学课程标准的拟议修改，大多数科学家和专家则强烈质疑她的观点；这类辩论反映出美国各地的激烈讨论。美国国家科学教育中心去年的一项研究只给约半数的州评了B+或更高的等级，得州获评最低等级。该中心副主任布兰奇提醒，制定州一级的科学课程标准只是一个作用有限的衡量基准；此外，气候变化在面向低龄儿童的课程以及一些开设更为普遍的科目中体现得没那么充分。布兰奇还指出，传达更偏颇观点的非官方教育材料正在分发到教师手中。

paras.en: The weather in Texas may have cooled since the recent extreme heat, but the temperature will be high at the State Board of Education meeting in Austin this month as officials debate how climate change is taught in Texas schools.
paras.zh: 前不久的极端高温过后，得克萨斯州的天气或许已经转凉，但本月在奥斯汀召开的州教育委员会会议上，“温度”却会很高，届时官员们将就得州学校如何讲授气候变化展开辩论。

w.m: n. 温度（此处喻指争论的激烈程度）

paras.en: Pat Hardy, who sympathises with the views of the energy sector, is resisting proposed changes to science standards for pre-teen pupils.
paras.zh: 帕特·哈迪认同能源行业的观点，正在抵制对青春期前学生科学课程标准的拟议修改。

w.m: adj. 青春期前的（约9至12岁）
n. 学生（尤指中小学生）

paras.en: “There are as many scientists working against all the panic of global climate change as there are those who are pushing it,” she claims.
paras.zh: “对于全球气候变化的种种恐慌，反对的科学家和煽动的科学家一样多。”她声称。

paras.en: “Texas is an energy state and we need to recognise that.
paras.zh: “得州是个能源州，我们得认清这一点。

paras.en: You need to remember where your bread is buttered.”
paras.zh: 你得记住谁是你的衣食父母。”

w.m: （某人的）利益所在；谁是（某人的）衣食父母

paras.en: Most scientists and experts sharply dispute Hardy’s views.
paras.zh: 大多数科学家和专家都强烈质疑哈迪的观点。

paras.en: Board members like her “casually dismiss the career work of scholars and scientists as just another misguided opinion,” says Dan Quinn, senior communications strategist at the Texas Freedom Network, a non-profit group that monitors public education.
paras.zh: 得克萨斯自由网络是一家监督公共教育的非营利组织，其高级传播策略师丹·奎因说，像她这样的委员“随随便便就把学者和科学家毕生的工作斥为不过是又一种错误观点”。

w.m: adv. 随便地；漫不经心地
把……斥为；把……当作……而不予理会
n. 职业生涯；毕生事业
adj. 错误的；误入歧途的

paras.en: Such debates reflect fierce discussions across the US, as researchers, policymakers, teachers and students step up demands for a greater focus on teaching about the facts of climate change in schools.
paras.zh: 这类辩论反映出，随着研究人员、政策制定者、教师和学生加紧呼吁学校更加注重讲授有关气候变化的事实，全美各地的讨论十分激烈。

paras.en: A study last year by the National Center for Science Education, a non-profit group of scientists and teachers, looking at how state public schools across the country address climate change in science classes, gave barely half of US states a grade B+ or higher.
paras.zh: 美国国家科学教育中心是一个由科学家和教师组成的非营利组织，该中心去年的一项研究考察了全国各州公立学校在科学课上如何探讨气候变化，结果只给美国约半数的州评了B+或更高的等级。

paras.en: Among the 10 worst performers were some of the most populous states, including Texas, which was given the lowest grade (F) and has a disproportionate influence because its textbooks are widely sold elsewhere.
paras.zh: 表现最差的10个州中，有几个是人口最多的州，其中包括得州。得州获评最低等级（F），而且因为它的教科书在其他地方广泛销售，其影响力大得不成比例。

w.m: adj. 不成比例的；过大的
adv. 在别处；在其他地方

paras.en: Glenn Branch, the center’s deputy director, cautions that setting state-level science standards is only one limited benchmark in a country that decentralises decisions to local school boards.
paras.zh: 该中心副主任格伦·布兰奇提醒说，在一个把决策权下放给地方学校董事会的国家，制定州一级的科学课程标准只是一个作用有限的衡量基准。

w.m: 学校董事会；学区委员会

paras.en: Even if a state is considered a high performer in its science standards, “that does not mean it will be taught”, he says.
paras.zh: 他说，即使一个州被认为在科学课程标准方面表现出色，“那也不意味着这些内容就会有人教”。

paras.en: Another issue is that, while climate change is well integrated into some subjects and at some ages—such as earth and space sciences in high schools—it is not as well represented in curricula for younger children and in subjects that are more widely taught, such as biology and chemistry.
paras.zh: 另一个问题是，虽然气候变化已经很好地融入了某些科目和某些年龄段的教学——比如高中的地球与空间科学——但在面向低龄儿童的课程中，以及在生物、化学等开设更为普遍的科目中，它却没有得到同样充分的体现。

paras.en: It is also less prominent in many social studies courses.
paras.zh: 在许多社会学科课程中，气候变化同样没那么突出。

paras.en: Branch points out that, even if a growing number of official guidelines and textbooks reflect scientific consensus on climate change, unofficial educational materials that convey more slanted perspectives are being distributed to teachers.
paras.zh: 布兰奇指出，即便越来越多的官方指导方针和教科书反映了有关气候变化的科学共识，传达更偏颇观点的非官方教育材料也仍在分发到教师手中。

paras.en: They include materials sponsored by libertarian think-tanks and energy industry associations.
paras.zh: 其中包括由自由意志主义智库和能源行业协会资助的材料。

w.m: adj. 自由意志主义的；自由至上主义的

passages.name: 2023年考研英语一 Text 2
passages.title: 新英格兰地区的短租房监管
passages.genre: 说明文 · 住房与政策
passages.summary: 自Airbnb等网站兴起以来，新英格兰各地一直在设法监管短租房；如今房价创下历史新高、待售房源处于历史低位，这类监管变得更加紧迫，有人担心开发商会大批收购住房、转手投入短租市场大赚一笔。在新罕布什尔州，住房权益倡导者担心不受管控的短租房会给本已紧张的市场带来更大压力，当地一家房地产经纪人协会的负责人则指出，短租房也为游客提供了住处。经济适用房政策专家霍恩认为，问题的症结不在于短租房本身，而在于开发商试图借大型短租设施规避税收和监管；马萨诸塞州和波士顿已要求房东登记，她认为类似的登记要求可能对处境艰难的城镇有益，但要改变住房市场，最主要的是必须多建房。

paras.en: Communities throughout New England have been attempting to regulate short-term rentals since sites like Airbnb took off in the 2010s.
paras.zh: 自21世纪10年代Airbnb等网站兴起以来，新英格兰各地的社区一直在设法监管短租房。

w.m: 短租房；短期出租的房屋

paras.en: Now, with record-high home prices and historically low inventory, there’s an increased urgency in such regulation, particularly among those who worry that developers will come in and buy up swaths of housing to flip for a fortune on the short-term rental market.
paras.zh: 如今，房价创下历史新高，待售房源处于历史低位，这类监管变得更加紧迫，对于那些担心开发商会进场大批收购住房、转手投入短租市场大赚一笔的人来说，尤其如此。

w.m: adj. 创纪录高的；历史最高的
adv. 从历史上看；历史上

paras.en: In New Hampshire, where the rental vacancy rate has dropped below 1 percent, housing advocates fear unchecked short-term rentals will put further pressure on an already strained market.
paras.zh: 新罕布什尔州的出租房空置率已降至1%以下，当地的住房权益倡导者担心，不受管控的短租房会给本已紧张的市场带来更大的压力。

w.m: adj. 不受管控的；未加约束的

paras.en: The State Legislature recently voted against a bill that would’ve made it illegal for towns to create legislation restricting short-term rentals.
paras.zh: 州议会最近投票否决了一项法案，该法案若获通过，各镇制定限制短租房的法规就会成为违法行为。

w.m: 使（某人做某事）成为违法

paras.en: “We are at a crisis level on the supply of rental housing,” said Nick Taylor, executive director of the Workforce Housing Coalition of the Greater Seacoast.
paras.zh: “在出租房供应方面，我们已经到了危机的地步。”大海岸地区劳动者住房联盟执行主任尼克·泰勒说。

w.m: adj. 大……地区的（用于地名，指某地及其周边一带）

paras.en: Without enough affordable housing in southern New Hampshire towns, “employers are having a hard time attracting employees, and workers are having a hard time finding a place to live,” Taylor said.
paras.zh: 泰勒说，由于新罕布什尔州南部各镇缺少足够的经济适用房，“雇主很难招到员工，劳动者也很难找到住的地方”。

w.m: 经济适用房；可负担住房

paras.en: However, short-term rentals also provide housing for tourists, pointed out Ryan Castle, CEO of a local association of realtors.
paras.zh: 不过，当地一家房地产经纪人协会的首席执行官瑞安·卡斯尔指出，短租房也为游客提供了住处。

paras.en: “A lot of workers are servicing the tourist industry, and the tourism industry is serviced by those people coming in short term,” Castle said, “and so it’s a cyclical effect.”
paras.zh: “很多劳动者都在为旅游业服务，而旅游业又靠那些短期来访的人来维持，”卡斯尔说，“所以这是一种循环效应。”

paras.en: Short-term rentals themselves are not the crux of the issue, said Keren Horn, an expert on affordable housing policy.
paras.zh: 经济适用房政策专家克伦·霍恩说，问题的症结并不在于短租房本身。

w.m: 经济适用房；可负担住房

paras.en: “I think individuals being able to rent out their second home is a good thing.
paras.zh: “我认为，个人能把自己的第二套住房租出去是件好事。

w.m: 第二套住房；第二处住所

paras.en: If it’s their vacation home anyway, and it’s just empty, why can’t you make money off it?” Horn said.
paras.zh: 如果那反正是他们的度假屋，而且就那么空着，为什么不能靠它赚钱呢？”霍恩说。

paras.en: Issues arise, however, when developers attempt to create large-scale short-term rental facilities—de facto hotels—to bypass taxes and regulations.
paras.zh: 然而，如果开发商试图建造大型短租设施——实际上就是酒店——来规避税收和监管，问题就出现了。

paras.en: “I think the question is, shouldn’t a developer who’s really building a hotel, but disguising it as not a hotel, be treated and taxed and regulated like a hotel?” Horn said.
paras.zh: “我认为问题在于：一个开发商实际上是在建酒店，却把它伪装成非酒店设施，难道不应该按酒店的标准来对待他、向他征税、对他实施监管吗？”霍恩说。

paras.en: At the end of 2018, Governor Charlie Baker of Massachusetts signed a bill to rein in those potential investor-buyers.
paras.zh: 2018年底，马萨诸塞州州长查理·贝克签署了一项法案，以约束那些潜在的投资型买家。

paras.en: The bill requires every rental host to register with the state, mandates they carry insurance, and opens the potential for local taxes on top of a new state levy.
paras.zh: 该法案要求每一位出租房屋的房东都向州政府登记，强制要求他们购买保险，还为在新开征的州税之外加征地方税创造了可能。

paras.en: Boston took things even further, requiring hosts to register with the city’s Inspectional Services Department.
paras.zh: 波士顿的做法还要更进一步，要求房东向该市的检查服务局登记。

paras.en: Horn said similar registration requirements could benefit struggling cities and towns, but “if we want to make a change in the housing market, the main one is we have to build a lot more.”
paras.zh: 霍恩说，类似的登记要求可能会让处境艰难的城镇受益，但“如果我们想让住房市场有所改变，最主要的一点就是必须建造多得多的住房”。

w.m: adj. 处境艰难的；苦苦挣扎的

passages.name: 2023年考研英语一 Text 3
passages.title: 出版商与书店僵持背后的隐忧
passages.genre: 说明文 · 出版与商业
passages.summary: 英国最大的图书零售商水石书店与企鹅兰登书屋陷入僵局：企鹅兰登书屋对水石书店实行了信用额度限制，据报道，水石书店各分店经理接到指示，把该社图书从显眼位置撤下。文章指出，吃亏的是企鹅兰登书屋的作者，尤其是销量中等、要靠书店员工热心推介的作者。与此同时，企鹅兰登书屋和西蒙与舒斯特拟议中的合并也令作者们担忧；文学经纪人洛尼认为，这一切都是权力走向集中这一更大范围转变的一部分，而出版业需要多元的途径来传递内容。

paras.en: If you’re heading for your nearest branch of Waterstones, the biggest book retailer in the UK, in search of the Duchess of Sussex’s new children’s book The Bench, you might have to be prepared to hunt around a bit; the same may be true of The President’s Daughter, the new thriller by Bill Clinton and James Patterson.
paras.zh: 如果你要去离你最近的水石书店分店（水石书店是英国最大的图书零售商），寻找萨塞克斯公爵夫人的新童书《长椅》，你可能得做好四处翻找一番的准备；比尔·克林顿与詹姆斯·帕特森合著的新惊悚小说《总统之女》或许也是如此。

paras.en: Both of these books are published next week by Penguin Random House (PRH), a company currently involved in a stand-off with Waterstones.
paras.zh: 这两本书都将于下周由企鹅兰登书屋（PRH）出版，这家公司目前正与水石书店陷入僵局。

paras.en: The problem began late last year, when PRH confirmed that it had introduced a credit limit with Waterstones “at a very significant level”.
paras.zh: 问题始于去年年底，当时企鹅兰登书屋证实，已对水石书店实行信用额度限制，额度定在“非常可观的水平”。

paras.en: The trade magazine The Bookseller reported that Waterstones branch managers were being told to remove PRH books from prominent areas such as tables, display spaces and windows, and were “quietly retiring them to their relevant sections”.
paras.zh: 据行业杂志《书商》报道，水石书店各分店经理接到指示，要把企鹅兰登书屋的图书从书台、展示区、橱窗等显眼位置撤下，并且正在“悄悄地把这些书撤回相应的分类区”。

paras.en: PRH declined to comment on the issue, but a spokesperson for Waterstones told me: “Waterstones are currently operating with reduced credit terms from PRH, the only publisher in the UK to place any limitations on our ability to trade.
paras.zh: 企鹅兰登书屋拒绝就此事发表评论，但水石书店的一位发言人告诉我：“水石书店目前从企鹅兰登书屋获得的信用条件有所收紧，在英国，只有这一家出版商对我们的正常经营施加了限制。

paras.en: We are not boycotting PRH titles but we are doing our utmost to ensure that availability for customers remains good despite the lower overall levels of stock.
paras.zh: 我们并没有抵制企鹅兰登书屋的图书，而是在竭尽全力确保：尽管整体库存水平降低了，顾客仍能顺利买到这些书。

w.m: n. 可获得性；供应情况

paras.en: We are hopeful with our shops now open again that normality will return and that we will be allowed to buy appropriately.
paras.zh: 现在我们的门店已重新开业，我们希望一切能恢复正常，也希望能获准适当地进货。

paras.en: Certainly, our shops are exceptionally busy.
paras.zh: 确实，我们的门店都格外繁忙。

paras.en: The sales for our May Books of the Month surpassed those of any other month since 2018.”
paras.zh: 我们5月‘每月好书’的销量超过了2018年以来其他任何一个月。”

paras.en: In the meantime, PRH authors have been the losers.
paras.zh: 与此同时，企鹅兰登书屋的作者一直是吃亏的一方。

paras.en: Big-name PRH authors may suffer a bit, but it’s those mid-list authors, who normally rely on Waterstones staff’s passion for promoting books by lesser-known writers, who will be praying for an end to the dispute.
paras.zh: 企鹅兰登书屋的大牌作者或许会吃点亏，但会祈盼这场纠纷结束的，是那些销量中等的作者——他们通常要靠水石书店员工满怀热情地推介不太知名作家的作品。

w.m: adj. 销量中等的（作家、书）

paras.en: It comes at a time when authors are already worried about the consequences of the proposed merger between PRH and another big publisher, Simon & Schuster—the reduction in the number of unaligned UK publishers is likely to lead to fewer bidding wars, lower advances, and more conformity in terms of what is published.
paras.zh: 这场纠纷发生之际，作者们本就在担心企鹅兰登书屋和另一家大型出版商西蒙与舒斯特拟议中的合并会带来什么后果——英国独立出版商数量减少，很可能导致竞价战变少、预付稿酬降低，出版的内容也更加趋同。

paras.en: “This is all part of a wider change towards concentration of power,” says literary agent Andrew Lownie.
paras.zh: 文学经纪人安德鲁·洛尼说：“这一切都是权力走向集中这一更大范围转变的一部分。”

paras.en: “The publishing industry talks about diversity in terms of authors and staff but it also needs a plurality of ways of delivering intellectual content, choice and different voices.
paras.zh: “出版业谈论作者和员工方面的多元化，但也需要多元的途径来传递思想内容、提供选择、发出不同的声音。

paras.en: After all, many of the most interesting books in recent years have come from small publishers.”
paras.zh: 毕竟，近年来最有意思的书当中，有许多都出自小出版商。”

paras.en: We shall see whether that plurality is a casualty of the current need among publishers to be big enough to take on all-comers.
paras.zh: 出版商眼下都需要做大，大到足以迎战一切对手；这种多元性是否会因此成为牺牲品，我们拭目以待。

w.m: 迎战一切对手；与所有挑战者较量

passages.name: 2023年考研英语一 Text 4
passages.title: 警惕学术论文中的引用操纵
passages.genre: 说明文 · 科研与学术
passages.summary: 科学界通过期刊的影响因子、论文的被引次数等方式衡量论文质量，科学家的职业生涯和所在机构的声誉都取决于论文及其所获引用。期刊、作者和机构合谋抬高被引次数的引用卡特尔由来已久；近来，一些支持服务咨询公司有时会建议投稿人在文章中添加引用，掠夺性期刊也可能让一篇文章在发表当年就获得大量引用。文章指出，Scopus本身掌握着发现这种不当行为所需的全部数据，并建议作者遇到添加不恰当参考文献的要求时不要照办，而要向期刊举报。

paras.en: Scientific papers are the recordkeepers of progress in research.
paras.zh: 科学论文是科研进展的记录者。

w.m: n. 记录者；记录保管者

paras.en: Each year researchers publish millions of papers in more than 30,000 journals.
paras.zh: 研究人员每年在3万多种期刊上发表数百万篇论文。

paras.en: The scientific community measures the quality of those papers in a number of ways, including the perceived quality of the journal (as reflected by the title’s impact factor) and the number of citations a specific paper accumulates.
paras.zh: 科学界通过多种方式衡量这些论文的质量，包括期刊在人们心目中的质量（反映在该刊的影响因子上），以及某篇论文累计获得的被引次数。

w.m: adj. 人们心目中的；感知到的
n. 刊物；（出版物的）名称

paras.en: The careers of scientists and the reputation of their institutions depend on the number and prestige of the papers they produce, but even more so on the citations attracted by these papers.
paras.zh: 科学家的职业生涯及其所在机构的声誉，取决于他们所发表论文的数量和声望，但在更大程度上取决于这些论文吸引到的引用。

paras.en: Citation cartels, where journals, authors, and institutions conspire to inflate citation numbers, have existed for a long time.
paras.zh: 期刊、作者和机构合谋抬高被引次数的引用卡特尔由来已久。

w.m: 引用卡特尔（相互抬高引用数的利益团伙）

paras.en: In 2016, researchers developed an algorithm to recognize suspicious citation patterns, including groups of authors that disproportionately cite one another and groups of journals that cite each other frequently to increase the impact factors of their publications.
paras.zh: 2016年，研究人员开发出一种算法，用来识别可疑的引用模式，其中包括相互引用次数多得不成比例的作者群体，以及为提高各自刊物的影响因子而频繁互引的期刊群体。

w.m: adv. 不成比例地；过多地

paras.en: Recently, another expression of this predatory behavior has emerged: so-called support service consultancies that provide language and other editorial support to individual authors and to journals sometimes advise contributors to add a number of citations to their articles.
paras.zh: 最近，这种掠夺性行为又出现了另一种表现形式：一些所谓的支持服务咨询公司向作者个人和期刊提供语言及其他编辑方面的支持，它们有时会建议投稿人在文章中添加若干引用。

paras.en: The advent of electronic publishing and authors’ need to find outlets for their papers resulted in thousands of new journals.
paras.zh: 电子出版的出现，加上作者需要为论文寻找发表渠道，催生了数以千计的新期刊。

w.m: 数以千计的；成千上万的

paras.en: The birth of predatory journals wasn’t far behind.
paras.zh: 没过多久，掠夺性期刊就诞生了。

w.m: 掠夺性期刊（只顾收费、几乎不审稿的期刊）
紧随其后；随后不久就出现

paras.en: These journals can act as milk cows where every single article in an issue may cite a specific paper or a series of papers.
paras.zh: 这些期刊可以充当“奶牛”：同一期中的每一篇文章都可能引用某一篇论文或某一系列论文。

w.m: 奶牛；（喻）可不断索取利益的来源

paras.en: In some instances, there is absolutely no relationship between the content of the article and the citations.
paras.zh: 在某些情况下，文章内容与所列引用之间毫无关联。

paras.en: The peculiar part is that the journal that the editor is supposedly working for is not profiting at all—it is just providing citations to other journals.
paras.zh: 奇怪之处在于，编辑名义上为之工作的期刊根本没有从中获利——它只是在为其他期刊提供引用。

paras.en: Such practices can lead an article to accrue more than 150 citations in the same year that it was published.
paras.zh: 这类做法可能让一篇文章在发表当年就积累起超过150次引用。

paras.en: How insidious is this type of citation manipulation?
paras.zh: 这类引用操纵有多阴险？

w.m: adj. 阴险的；暗中为害的

paras.en: In one example, an individual—acting as author, editor, and consultant—was able to use at least 15 journals as citation providers to articles published by five scientists at three universities.
paras.zh: 举个例子，有一个人身兼作者、编辑和顾问，得以利用至少15种期刊，为三所大学的五位科学家发表的文章提供引用。

paras.en: The problem is rampant in Scopus, a citation database, which includes a high number of the new “international” journals.
paras.zh: 这一问题在引文数据库Scopus中十分泛滥，该数据库收录了大量新出现的“国际”期刊。

paras.en: In fact, a listing in Scopus seems to be a criterion to be targeted in this type of citation manipulation.
paras.zh: 事实上，在这类引用操纵中，被Scopus收录似乎是挑选目标的一个标准。

paras.en: Scopus itself has all the data necessary to detect this malpractice.
paras.zh: Scopus本身就掌握着发现这种不当行为所需的全部数据。

w.m: n. 不当行为；违规行为

paras.en: Red flags include a large number of citations to an article within the first year.
paras.zh: 危险信号包括一篇文章在第一年内获得大量引用。

paras.en: And for authors who wish to steer clear of citation cartel activities: when an editor, a reviewer, or a support service asks you to add inappropriate references, do not oblige and do report the request to the journal.
paras.zh: 还有，希望远离引用卡特尔活动的作者请注意：如果编辑、审稿人或支持服务机构要求你添加不恰当的参考文献，不要照办，而且一定要向期刊举报这一要求。

w.m: adj. 不恰当的；不合适的

passages.name: 2023年考研英语二 Text 1
passages.title: 人造草坪引发环保争议
passages.genre: 说明文 · 环境与社会
passages.summary: 为了追求完美的草坪，房主们纷纷走捷径铺设人造草坪，环境却在为此付出代价。切尔西花展已禁止今年的展会使用人造草坪，主办方英国皇家园艺学会称，原因是塑料草坪会损害环境和生物多样性；一个Twitter账号也在鼓励人们签署两份请愿书，分别呼吁禁售塑料草坪和对其征税。人造草坪的支持者则指出，天然草坪同样会影响环境。政府表示没有禁止使用人造草坪的计划，更愿意帮助个人和组织作出正确的选择，而不是就此立法。

paras.en: In the quest for the perfect lawn, homeowners across the country are taking a shortcut—and it is the environment that is paying the price.
paras.zh: 为了追求完美的草坪，全国各地的房主正在走捷径，而为此付出代价的是环境。

w.m: 为了追求；在寻求……的过程中

paras.en: About eight million square metres of plastic grass is sold each year but opposition has now spread to the highest gardening circles.
paras.zh: 塑料草坪每年的销量约为800万平方米，但如今，反对之声已经蔓延到园艺界的最高层。

paras.en: The Chelsea Flower Show has banned fake grass from this year’s event, declaring it to be not part of its ethos.
paras.zh: 切尔西花展已禁止今年的展会使用人造草坪，并宣称人造草坪不符合花展的理念。

w.m: 禁止……出现在（某场合）；不准……用于

paras.en: The Royal Horticultural Society (RHS), which runs the annual show in west London, says it has introduced the ban because of the damage plastic grass does to the environment and biodiversity.
paras.zh: 英国皇家园艺学会（RHS）每年在伦敦西部主办这一花展，学会表示，之所以推出这项禁令，是因为塑料草坪会对环境和生物多样性造成损害。

paras.en: Ed Horne, of the RHS, said: “We launched our sustainability strategy last year and fake grass is just not in line with our ethos and views on plastic.
paras.zh: 皇家园艺学会的埃德·霍恩说：“我们去年推出了可持续发展战略，而人造草坪根本不符合我们的理念，也不符合我们对塑料的看法。

w.m: n. 可持续性；可持续发展

paras.en: We recommend using real grass because of its environmental benefits, which include supporting wildlife, alleviating flooding and cooling the environment.”
paras.zh: 我们建议使用天然草坪，因为它能带来种种环境效益，包括有助于野生动物生存、缓解洪涝和为环境降温。”

w.m: v. 维持（生命）；有助于……生存

paras.en: The RHS’s decision comes as campaigners try to raise awareness of the problems fake grass causes.
paras.zh: 皇家园艺学会作出这一决定之际，活动人士正努力让人们更加认识到人造草坪造成的问题。

paras.en: A Twitter account, which claims to “cut through the greenwash” of artificial grass, already has more than 20,000 followers.
paras.zh: 一个Twitter账号声称要揭穿人造草坪的“漂绿”说辞，已经有2万多名关注者。

w.m: n. 漂绿（虚假的环保宣传）
n. （社交媒体的）关注者；粉丝

paras.en: It is trying to encourage people to sign two petitions, one calling for a ban on the sale of plastic grass and another calling for an “ecological damage” tax on such lawns.
paras.zh: 该账号正努力鼓励人们签署两份请愿书：一份呼吁禁止销售塑料草坪，另一份呼吁对这类草坪征收“生态破坏”税。

paras.en: They have gathered 7,276 and 11,282 signatures.
paras.zh: 这两份请愿书已分别征集到7276个和11282个签名。

paras.en: However, supporters of fake grass point out that there is also an environmental impact with natural lawns, which need mowing and therefore usually consume electricity or petrol.
paras.zh: 不过，人造草坪的支持者指出，天然草坪同样会对环境造成影响：它需要修剪，因此通常要消耗电力或汽油。

paras.en: The industry also points out that real grass requires considerable amounts of water, weed killer or other treatments and that people who lay fake grass tend to use their garden more.
paras.zh: 人造草坪行业还指出，天然草坪需要大量的水、除草剂或其他养护药剂，而且铺设人造草坪的人往往会更多地使用自家花园。

paras.en: The industry also claims that people who lay fake grass spend an average of £500 on trees or shrubs for their garden, which provides habitat for insects.
paras.zh: 人造草坪行业还称，铺设人造草坪的人平均会花500英镑为自家花园购置树木或灌木，这能为昆虫提供栖息地。

paras.en: In response to another petition last year about banning fake lawns, which gathered 30,000 signatures, the government responded that it has “no plans to ban the use of artificial grass.”
paras.zh: 去年另有一份关于禁用人造草坪的请愿书征集到了3万个签名，对此，政府回应称“没有禁止使用人造草坪的计划”。

paras.en: It added: “We prefer to help people and organizations make the right choice rather than legislating on such matters.
paras.zh: 政府还补充说：“我们更愿意帮助个人和组织作出正确的选择，而不是就此类事务立法。

w.m: 宁愿……而不……；更愿意……而不是

paras.en: However, the use of artificial grass must comply with the legal and policy safeguards in place to protect biodiversity and ensure sustainable drainage, while measures such as the strengthened biodiversity duty should serve to encourage public authorities to consider sustainable alternatives.”
paras.zh: 不过，使用人造草坪必须遵守现行的法律和政策保障措施，这些措施旨在保护生物多样性、确保可持续排水；同时，经过强化的生物多样性义务等措施应当有助于鼓励公共机构考虑可持续的替代方案。”

w.m: adj. 经过强化的；加强了的
n. 替代方案；可供选择的事物

passages.name: 2023年考研英语二 Text 2
passages.title: 美国国家公园的资金困境
passages.genre: 议论文 · 公共政策与环境
passages.summary: 联邦政府为填补国家公园长期存在的资金缺口出了一些主意，作者认为这些主意很容易被斥为荒唐，但也承认美国国家公园确实陷入了危机：维护欠账超过120亿美元。作者指出，把露营地私有化、商业化并不能包治百病，扩大私有化还肯定会削弱国家公园的一大吸引力：让人享受大自然，暂时摆脱商业喧嚣。作者认为真正的问题在于国家公园长期严重缺乏资金。作者的调查显示，美国人非常看重国家公园，约81%的受访者愿意在今后10年额外缴税，以免国家公园的经费遭到任何削减。国家公园创造了多方面的价值，靠的却是极少的经费：国会每年只拨款30亿美元，这一数额（按通胀调整后的美元计算）除2009年有过一次性增加外，自2001年以来一直持平，而年游客量自1980年以来已增长50%以上。

paras.en: It’s easy to dismiss as absurd the federal government’s ideas for plugging the chronic funding gap of our national parks.
paras.zh: 联邦政府为填补美国国家公园长期存在的资金缺口出了一些主意，人们很容易斥之为荒唐，不予理会。

w.m: 斥为；认为……是（而不予理会）

paras.en: Can anyone really think it’s a good idea to allow Amazon deliveries to your tent in Yosemite or food trucks to line up under the redwood trees at Sequoia National Park?
paras.zh: 真会有人认为，允许亚马逊送货到你在优胜美地的帐篷，或者允许餐车在红杉国家公园的红杉树下一字排开，是个好主意吗？

paras.en: But the government is right about one thing: U.S. national parks are in crisis.
paras.zh: 不过，政府有一点说对了：美国的国家公园正陷入危机。

paras.en: Collectively, they have a maintenance backlog of more than $12 billion.
paras.zh: 这些国家公园的维护欠账合计超过120亿美元。

paras.en: Roads, trails, restrooms, visitor centers and other infrastructure are crumbling.
paras.zh: 道路、步道、卫生间、游客中心以及其他基础设施正日渐破败。

paras.en: But privatizing and commercializing the campgrounds would not be a cure-all.
paras.zh: 但把露营地私有化、商业化，并不能包治百病。

w.m: n. 万灵药；包治百病的办法

paras.en: Campgrounds are a tiny portion of the overall infrastructure backlog, and businesses in the parks hand over, on average, only about 5% of their revenues to the National Park Service.
paras.zh: 在全部基础设施欠账中，露营地只占很小一部分；而且国家公园里的商家平均只把约5%的收入上交给国家公园管理局。

paras.en: Moreover, increased privatization would certainly undercut one of the major reasons why 300 million visitors come to the parks each year: to enjoy nature and get a break from the commercial drumbeat that overwhelms daily life.
paras.zh: 此外，每年有3亿游客来到国家公园，一个主要原因就是享受大自然，暂时摆脱淹没日常生活的商业喧嚣；而扩大私有化肯定会让这种体验打折扣。

w.m: 暂时摆脱；从……中解脱出来

paras.en: The real problem is that the parks have been chronically starved of funding.
paras.zh: 真正的问题在于，国家公园长期以来一直严重缺乏资金。

w.m: 极度缺乏；得不到足够的

paras.en: We conducted a comprehensive survey examining how U.S. residents view their national parks, and we found that Americans place a very high value on them—whether or not they actually visit them.
paras.zh: 我们开展了一项全面调查，考察美国居民如何看待本国的国家公园，结果发现，不论是否真的去游览，美国人都非常看重国家公园。

paras.en: The peer-reviewed economic survey of 700 U.S. taxpayers, conducted by mail and internet, also found that people would be willing to pay a significant amount of money to make sure the parks and their programs are kept intact.
paras.zh: 这项经同行评审的经济调查以邮寄和网络方式进行，对象是700名美国纳税人；调查还发现，人们愿意拿出相当大的一笔钱，确保国家公园及其项目完整地保留下来。

paras.en: Some 81% of respondents said they would be willing to pay additional taxes for the next 10 years to avoid any cuts to the national parks.
paras.zh: 约81%的受访者表示，他们愿意在今后10年额外缴税，以免国家公园的经费遭到任何削减。

paras.en: The national parks provide great value to U.S. residents both as places to escape and as symbols of nature.
paras.zh: 国家公园既是逃离尘嚣的去处，也是大自然的象征，为美国居民带来巨大的价值。

paras.en: On top of this, they produce value from their extensive educational programs, their positive impact on the climate through carbon sequestration, their contribution to our cultural and artistic life, and of course from tourism.
paras.zh: 除此之外，国家公园创造的价值还来自以下几个方面：丰富的教育项目、通过固碳对气候产生的积极影响、对美国文化艺术生活的贡献，当然还有旅游业。

w.m: adj. 大量的；广泛的；丰富的

paras.en: The parks also help keep America’s past alive, working with thousands of local jurisdictions around the country to protect historical sites—including Ellis Island and Gettysburg—and to bring the stories of these places to life.
paras.zh: 国家公园还有助于让美国的历史保持鲜活：它们与全国各地数千个地方辖区合作，保护埃利斯岛、葛底斯堡等历史遗址，并让这些地方的故事生动再现。

w.m: 使……保持鲜活；使……延续下去
使……生动再现；使……鲜活起来

paras.en: The parks do all this on a shoestring.
paras.zh: 国家公园用极少的经费做到了这一切。

w.m: 以极少的钱；用很少的经费

paras.en: Congress allocates only $3 billion a year to the national park system—an amount that has been flat since 2001 (in inflation-adjusted dollars) with the exception of a onetime boost in 2009 as part of the Obama stimulus package.
paras.zh: 国会每年只给国家公园系统拨款30亿美元，这一数额（按通胀调整后的美元计算）自2001年以来一直持平，唯一的例外是2009年：作为奥巴马经济刺激方案的一部分，拨款有过一次性的增加。

w.m: adj. 持平的；没有变化的
（经济）刺激方案；一揽子刺激计划

paras.en: Meanwhile, the number of annual visitors has increased by more than 50% since 1980, and now stands at 330 million visitors per year.
paras.zh: 与此同时，自1980年以来，年游客量增长了50%以上，目前达到每年3.3亿人次。

passages.name: 2023年考研英语二 Text 3
passages.title: 互联网时代的记忆：衰退还是适应
passages.genre: 说明文 · 科技与心理
passages.summary: 哥伦比亚大学心理学教授斯帕罗认为，互联网或许只是在改变我们记住的内容，而不是改变我们的记忆能力：她的研究发现，参与者知道信息会保存在电脑上，就不费力去回忆；还有一组参与者没有记住信息，却记住了如何找到存放信息的文件夹。她认为人类的记忆并没有在衰退，而是在适应新的通信技术，这一趋势或许会让学习方法转向强调更具概念性的思维。也有专家认为，现在要弄清互联网如何影响大脑还为时过早；心理学教授斯托姆认为总体上好处会超过代价，但记忆是否在朝好的方向变化，目前还不得而知。

paras.en: The Internet may be changing merely what we remember, not our capacity to do so, suggests Columbia University psychology professor Betsy Sparrow.
paras.zh: 哥伦比亚大学心理学教授贝特西·斯帕罗提出，互联网或许只是在改变我们记住的内容，而不是改变我们的记忆能力。

w.m: 这样做（代指前面的动作）

paras.en: In 2011, Sparrow led a study in which participants were asked to record 40 factoids in a computer (“an ostrich’s eye is bigger than its brain,” for example).
paras.zh: 2011年，斯帕罗主持了一项研究，要求参与者在电脑里记下40条小知识（例如“鸵鸟的眼睛比它的大脑还大”）。

w.m: n. 小知识；琐碎的信息

paras.en: Half of the participants were told the information would be erased, while the other half were told it would be saved.
paras.zh: 其中一半参与者被告知这些信息会被删除，另一半则被告知信息会保存下来。

paras.en: Guess what?
paras.zh: 你猜怎么着？

w.m: 你猜怎么着（引出出人意料的事）

paras.en: The latter group made no effort to recall the information when quizzed on it later, because they knew they could find it on their computers.
paras.zh: 后来就这些信息接受测验时，后一组参与者并没有费力去回忆，因为他们知道可以在自己的电脑上找到这些信息。

paras.en: In the same study, a group was asked to remember both the information and the folders it was stored in.
paras.zh: 在同一项研究中，有一组参与者被要求既要记住信息，又要记住存放信息的文件夹。

paras.en: They didn’t remember the information, but they remembered how to find the folders.
paras.zh: 他们没有记住信息，却记住了如何找到那些文件夹。

paras.en: In other words, human memory is not deteriorating but “adapting to new communications technology,” Sparrow says.
paras.zh: 斯帕罗表示，换句话说，人类的记忆并没有在衰退，而是在“适应新的通信技术”。

paras.en: In a very practical way, the Internet is becoming an external hard drive for our memories, a process known as “cognitive offloading.”
paras.zh: 从非常实际的层面上讲，互联网正在成为我们记忆的外置硬盘，这一过程称为“认知卸载”。

paras.en: Traditionally, this role was fulfilled by data banks, libraries, and other humans.
paras.zh: 传统上，充当这一角色的是数据库、图书馆和其他人。

w.m: v. 充当（角色）；履行（职责）

paras.en: Your father may never remember birthdays because your mother does, for instance.
paras.zh: 比如，你父亲可能从来不记生日，因为有你母亲记着。

paras.en: Some worry that this is having a destructive effect on society, but Sparrow sees an upside.
paras.zh: 有些人担心这正在对社会产生破坏性影响，但斯帕罗看到了好的一面。

paras.en: Perhaps, she suggests, the trend will change our approach to learning from a focus on individual facts and memorization to an emphasis on more conceptual thinking—something that is not available on the Internet.
paras.zh: 她提出，这一趋势或许会改变我们的学习方法：从侧重一个个具体事实和记忆背诵，转向强调更具概念性的思维——这是互联网上所没有的。

paras.en: “I personally have never seen all that much intellectual value in memorizing things,” Sparrow says, adding that we haven’t lost our ability to do it.
paras.zh: 斯帕罗说：“我个人从来都不觉得背东西有多大的智力价值。”她还补充说，我们并没有丧失背东西的能力。

paras.en: Still other experts say it’s too soon to understand how the Internet affects our brains.
paras.zh: 还有一些专家说，现在要弄清互联网如何影响我们的大脑还为时过早。

paras.en: There is no experimental evidence showing that it interferes with our ability to focus, for instance, wrote psychologists Christopher Chabris and Daniel J. Simons.
paras.zh: 比如，心理学家克里斯托弗·查布里斯和丹尼尔·J.西蒙斯就写道，没有实验证据表明互联网会干扰我们集中注意力的能力。

paras.en: And surfing the web exercised the brain more than reading did among computer-savvy older adults in a 2008 study involving 24 participants at the Semel Institute for Neuroscience and Human Behavior at the University of California, Los Angeles.
paras.zh: 而且，2008年，加州大学洛杉矶分校塞梅尔神经科学与人类行为研究所开展了一项有24名参与者的研究，结果显示，在精通电脑的老年人当中，上网比阅读更能锻炼大脑。

paras.en: “There may be costs associated with our increased reliance on the Internet, but I’d have to imagine that overall the benefits are going to outweigh those costs,” observes psychology professor Benjamin Storm.
paras.zh: 心理学教授本杰明·斯托姆指出：“我们对互联网的依赖日益加深，这可能会带来一些代价，但我想，总体而言，好处会超过这些代价。”

paras.en: “It seems pretty clear that memory is changing, but is it changing for the better?
paras.zh: “记忆正在发生变化，这一点似乎相当清楚，但它是在朝好的方向变化吗？

paras.en: At this point, we don’t know.”
paras.zh: 目前，我们还不知道。”

passages.name: 2023年考研英语二 Text 4
passages.title: 青少年的亲社会行为与叛逆行为相伴而生
passages.genre: 说明文 · 心理与成长
passages.summary: 一项新研究表明，青少年的积极面和消极面相伴而生：与年龄更小的儿童或成年人相比，青少年更有可能称自己做过无私帮助朋友之类的事，而且更叛逆的青少年也更有可能帮助他人。一种观点认为，青少年的行为与“奖赏敏感性”有关：青少年对社会性奖赏尤其敏感，而奖赏敏感性似乎在青春期上升，随着年龄增长又会下降。

paras.en: Teenagers are paradoxical.
paras.zh: 青少年是一个矛盾体。

w.m: adj. 矛盾的；似是而非的

paras.en: That’s a mild and detached way of saying something that parents often express with considerably stronger language.
paras.zh: 这是一种温和而冷静客观的说法，同样的意思，父母们常常会用激烈得多的言辞来表达。

w.m: adj. 超然的；冷静客观的

paras.en: But the paradox is scientific as well as personal.
paras.zh: 但这一矛盾不只是个人层面的，也是科学层面的。

w.m: （A as well as B）不仅B，而且A

paras.en: In adolescence, helpless and dependent children who have relied on grown-ups for just about everything become independent people who can take care of themselves and help each other.
paras.zh: 到了青春期，原本无助、依赖性强、几乎凡事都靠大人的孩子，变成了独立的人，能够照顾自己，也能互相帮助。

w.m: adj. 无助的；无依无靠的

paras.en: At the same time, once cheerful and compliant children become rebellious teenage risk-takers.
paras.zh: 与此同时，曾经开朗、顺从的孩子变成了叛逆、爱冒险的青少年。

w.m: adj. 青少年的；十几岁的
n. 爱冒险的人；冒险者

paras.en: A new study published in the journal Child Development, by Eveline Crone of the University of Leiden and colleagues, suggests that the positive and negative sides of teenagers go hand in hand.
paras.zh: 莱顿大学的伊芙琳·克罗内与同事在《儿童发展》期刊上发表的一项新研究表明，青少年的积极面和消极面是相伴而生的。

paras.en: The study is part of a new wave of thinking about adolescence.
paras.zh: 围绕青春期出现了新一波思潮，这项研究就是其中的一部分。

paras.en: For a long time, scientists and policy makers concentrated on the idea that teenagers were a problem that needed to be solved.
paras.zh: 长期以来，科学家和政策制定者一直把注意力集中在这样一种观念上：青少年是一个需要解决的问题。

paras.en: The new work emphasizes that adolescence is a time of opportunity as well as risk.
paras.zh: 新的研究强调，青春期不仅是一个有风险的时期，也是一个充满机遇的时期。

w.m: n. 研究（成果）；研究工作
（A as well as B）不仅B，而且A

paras.en: The researchers studied “prosocial” and rebellious traits in more than 200 children and young adults, ranging from 11 to 28 years old.
paras.zh: 研究人员考察了200多名11岁至28岁的儿童和青年身上的“亲社会”特质和叛逆特质。

paras.en: The participants filled out questionnaires about how often they did things that were altruistic and positive, like sacrificing their own interests to help a friend, or rebellious and negative, like getting drunk or staying out late.
paras.zh: 参与者填写了问卷，说明自己做以下两类事情的频率：一类是利他的、积极的事，比如牺牲自己的利益去帮助朋友；另一类是叛逆的、消极的事，比如喝醉酒或在外面待到很晚。

w.m: 在外面待到很晚；很晚不回家

paras.en: Other studies have shown that rebellious behavior increases as you become a teenager and then fades away as you grow older.
paras.zh: 其他研究已经表明，叛逆行为会在人步入青春期时增加，然后随着年龄增长逐渐消退。

paras.en: But the new study shows that, interestingly, the same pattern holds for prosocial behavior.
paras.zh: 但有趣的是，这项新研究表明，同样的模式也适用于亲社会行为。

paras.en: Teenagers were more likely than younger children or adults to report that they did things like unselfishly help a friend.
paras.zh: 与年龄更小的儿童或成年人相比，青少年更有可能称自己做过无私地帮助朋友这类事情。

paras.en: Most significantly, there was a positive correlation between prosociality and rebelliousness.
paras.zh: 最重要的是，亲社会性与叛逆性之间存在正相关。

w.m: adv. （修饰全句）重要的是；值得注意的是

paras.en: The teenagers who were more rebellious were also more likely to help others.
paras.zh: 更叛逆的青少年也更有可能帮助他人。

paras.en: The good and bad sides of adolescence seem to develop together.
paras.zh: 青春期好的一面和坏的一面似乎是同步发展的。

paras.en: Is there some common factor that underlies these apparently contradictory developments?
paras.zh: 是否有某种共同的因素潜藏在这些看似矛盾的发展背后？

w.m: v. 潜藏在……背后；构成……的基础

paras.en: One idea is that teenage behavior is related to what researchers call “reward sensitivity.”
paras.zh: 一种观点认为，青少年的行为与研究人员所说的“奖赏敏感性”有关。

paras.en: Decision-making always involves balancing rewards and risks, benefits and costs.
paras.zh: 做决策总是要权衡奖赏与风险、收益与代价。

paras.en: “Reward sensitivity” measures how much reward it takes to outweigh risk.
paras.zh: “奖赏敏感性”衡量的是需要多大的奖赏才能压过风险。

w.m: v. 压过；超过（分量、价值）

paras.en: Teenagers are particularly sensitive to social rewards—winning the game, impressing a new friend, getting that boy to notice you.
paras.zh: 青少年对社会性奖赏尤其敏感——赢得比赛、给新朋友留下好印象、让心仪的那个男孩注意到你。

paras.en: Reward sensitivity, like prosocial behavior and risk-taking, seems to go up in adolescence and then down again as we age.
paras.zh: 和亲社会行为及冒险行为一样，奖赏敏感性似乎也会在青春期上升，然后随着年龄增长再次下降。

paras.en: Somehow, when you hit 30, the chance that something exciting and new will happen at that party just doesn’t seem to outweigh the effort of getting up off the couch.
paras.zh: 不知怎么的，人一到30岁，那场派对上兴许会发生点新鲜刺激的事，这种可能性似乎就是压不过从沙发上爬起来要费的那份力气。

w.m: adj. 令人兴奋的；刺激的
v. 压过；超过（分量、价值）

passages.name: 2022年考研英语一 Text 1
passages.title: 塑料文物的保存难题
passages.genre: 说明文 · 材料与文物保护
passages.summary: 人们常抱怨塑料太耐用，但有些塑料材料会随时间推移而变化：开裂、渗出添加剂、熔成烂泥，这给博物馆等力图保存重要文化物品的机构带来了令人头疼的大难题。聚合物化学家范奥斯滕指出，塑料艺术的一些先驱并不总是清楚该如何正确调配原料；意大利艺术家吉拉尔迪所用的聚氨酯泡沫本身就不稳定，到20世纪90年代中期，其作品中的南瓜、玫瑰等造型已在开裂、碎裂；范奥斯滕和同事给其中一些作品注入化学品加以保护，已有几件雕塑再次展出。但老旧物品仍在不断变质，可生物降解塑料又越来越普遍，塑料的保存很可能会变得更难；而且正如费雷拉所说，我们今天决定收藏和保存什么，将对未来的人如何看待我们产生重大影响。

paras.en: People often complain that plastics are too durable.
paras.zh: 人们常常抱怨塑料太耐用。

paras.en: Water bottles, shopping bags, and other trash litter the planet, from Mount Everest to the Mariana Trench, because plastics are everywhere and don’t break down easily.
paras.zh: 从珠穆朗玛峰到马里亚纳海沟，水瓶、购物袋和其他垃圾散落在地球各处，这是因为塑料无处不在，而且不易分解。

w.m: v. 散落在（某处）；使凌乱

paras.en: But some plastic materials change over time.
paras.zh: 但有些塑料材料会随着时间推移而发生变化。

paras.en: They crack and frizzle.
paras.zh: 它们会开裂、卷曲。

paras.en: They “weep” out additives.
paras.zh: 它们会“渗出”添加剂。

paras.en: They melt into sludge.
paras.zh: 它们会熔成一摊烂泥。

paras.en: All of which creates huge headaches for institutions, such as museums, trying to preserve culturally important objects.
paras.zh: 这一切都给博物馆等力图保存重要文化物品的机构带来了令人头疼的大难题。

w.m: n. 令人头疼的事；难题

paras.en: The variety of plastic objects at risk is dizzying: early radios, avant-garde sculptures, celluloid animation stills from Disney films, the first artificial heart.
paras.zh: 面临损毁风险的塑料物品种类之多，令人眼花缭乱：早期的收音机、先锋派雕塑、迪士尼电影的赛璐珞动画静帧，还有第一颗人工心脏。

w.m: n. 赛璐珞（一种早期塑料）

paras.en: Certain artifacts are especially vulnerable because some pioneers in plastic art didn’t always know how to mix ingredients properly, says Thea van Oosten, a polymer chemist who, until retiring a few years ago, worked for decades at the Cultural Heritage Agency of the Netherlands.
paras.zh: 聚合物化学家西娅·范奥斯滕说，某些文物之所以格外容易受损，是因为塑料艺术的一些先驱并不总是清楚该如何正确调配原料；她在荷兰文化遗产署工作了几十年，直到几年前退休。

paras.en: “It’s like baking a cake: If you don’t have exact amounts, it goes wrong,” she says.
paras.zh: “这就像烤蛋糕：如果用量不精确，就会出问题。”她说。

paras.en: “The object you make is already a time bomb.”
paras.zh: “你做出来的东西已经是一颗定时炸弹了。”

paras.en: And sometimes, it’s not the artist’s fault.
paras.zh: 而有时候，这并不是艺术家的错。

paras.en: In the 1960s, the Italian artist Piero Gilardi began to create hundreds of bright, colorful foam pieces.
paras.zh: 20世纪60年代，意大利艺术家皮耶罗·吉拉尔迪开始创作数百件鲜亮多彩的泡沫作品。

w.m: adj. 多彩的；色彩缤纷的

paras.en: Those pieces included small beds of roses and other items as well as a few dozen “nature carpets”—large rectangles decorated with foam pumpkins, cabbages, and watermelons.
paras.zh: 这些作品包括一些小型玫瑰花坛和其他物件，还有几十块“自然地毯”——大块的长方形，上面装饰着泡沫做的南瓜、卷心菜和西瓜。

paras.en: He wanted viewers to walk around on the carpets—which meant they had to be durable.
paras.zh: 他希望观众能在地毯上走来走去——这就意味着地毯必须经久耐用。

paras.en: Unfortunately, the polyurethane foam he used is inherently unstable.
paras.zh: 遗憾的是，他所用的聚氨酯泡沫本身就不稳定。

w.m: adv. 遗憾的是；不幸的是

paras.en: It’s especially vulnerable to light damage, and by the mid-1990s, Gilardi’s pumpkins, roses, and other figures were splitting and crumbling.
paras.zh: 这种泡沫尤其容易受到光照损害，到20世纪90年代中期，吉拉尔迪的南瓜、玫瑰和其他造型都在开裂、碎裂。

paras.en: Museums locked some of them away in the dark.
paras.zh: 博物馆把其中一些作品锁了起来，存放在暗处。

paras.en: So van Oosten and her colleagues worked to preserve Gilardi’s sculptures.
paras.zh: 于是，范奥斯滕和同事们努力保存吉拉尔迪的雕塑。

paras.en: They infused some with stabilizing and consolidating chemicals.
paras.zh: 他们给其中一些雕塑注入了起稳定和加固作用的化学品。

paras.en: Van Oosten calls those chemicals “sunscreens” because their goal was to prevent further light damage and rebuild worn polymer fibers.
paras.zh: 范奥斯滕把这些化学品称为“防晒霜”，因为使用它们的目的是防止光照造成进一步的损害，并修复已经磨损的聚合物纤维。

paras.en: She is proud that several sculptures have even gone on display again, albeit sometimes beneath protective cases.
paras.zh: 令她自豪的是，有几件雕塑甚至已再次展出，尽管有时是放在防护罩下面。

paras.en: Despite success stories like van Oosten’s, preservation of plastics will likely get harder.
paras.zh: 尽管有范奥斯滕这样的成功案例，塑料的保存工作很可能会变得更难。

paras.en: Old objects continue to deteriorate.
paras.zh: 老旧物品仍在不断变质。

paras.en: Worse, biodegradable plastics, designed to disintegrate, are increasingly common.
paras.zh: 更糟的是，可生物降解塑料越来越普遍，而这类塑料的设计初衷就是要分解。

paras.en: And more is at stake here than individual objects.
paras.zh: 而且，在这件事上，利害攸关的不只是单个物品。

paras.en: Joana Lia Ferreira, an assistant professor of conservation and restoration at the NOVA School of Science and Technology, notes that archaeologists first defined the great material ages of human history—Stone Age, Iron Age, and so on—after examining artifacts in museums.
paras.zh: NOVA科学技术学院文物保护与修复专业助理教授若阿娜·莉娅·费雷拉指出，考古学家最初是在研究了博物馆中的文物之后，才界定出人类历史上的几大材料时代——石器时代、铁器时代等等。

w.m: 若阿娜·莉娅·费雷拉（人名）

paras.en: We now live in an age of plastic, she says, “and what we decide to collect today, what we decide to preserve…will have a strong impact on how in the future we’ll be seen.”
paras.zh: 她说，我们如今生活在一个塑料时代，“而我们今天决定收藏什么、决定保存什么……将对未来的人如何看待我们产生重大影响。”

passages.name: 2022年考研英语一 Text 2
passages.title: 学位价值之变与Z世代的选择
passages.genre: 议论文 · 教育与就业
passages.summary: 随着学位普及，学位已经贬值，教育不再是实现社会阶层流动的可靠途径；如今英国有28%的大学毕业生从事着不需要大学学历的工作。作者强调，学位并非适合所有人，从中学教室到大学讲堂也不是必然的转变，而且还有其他选择；雇主们早就看到了雇用中学毕业生的好处，许多雇主也逐渐看到对某些岗位取消学位要求的好处。对想走学位这条路的人来说，这个学位很可能只是众多学位中的第一个；Z世代需要在整个职业生涯中不断提升技能，教育将成为其职业轨迹的核心组成部分；老一辈常以学位来定义自己，而他们的子女似乎已明白，学位不会再以同样的方式定义他们。

paras.en: As the latest crop of students pen their undergraduate application form and weigh up their options, it may be worth considering just how the point, purpose and value of a degree have changed and what Generation Z need to consider as they start the third stage of their educational journey.
paras.zh: 在新一批学生填写本科申请表、权衡各种选择之际，或许值得思考一下：学位的意义、目的和价值究竟发生了怎样的变化，Z世代在开启求学之路的第三阶段时又需要考虑些什么。

w.m: n. 一批（同时出现的人或物）
adj. 本科的；大学本科生的

paras.en: Millennials were told that if you did well in school and got a decent degree, you would be set up for life.
paras.zh: 千禧一代听到的说法是：只要在学校表现出色、拿到一个像样的学位，这辈子就有了保障。

w.m: 一辈子有保障；终身无忧

paras.en: But that promise has been found wanting.
paras.zh: 但事实证明，这一承诺靠不住。

w.m: 被证明有欠缺；被证明靠不住

paras.en: As degrees became universal, they became devalued.
paras.zh: 学位普及了，也就贬值了。

paras.en: Education was no longer a secure route to social mobility.
paras.zh: 教育不再是实现社会阶层流动的可靠途径。

w.m: 社会流动；社会阶层流动

paras.en: Today, 28 percent of graduates in the UK are in non-graduate roles, a percentage which is double the average among OECD countries.
paras.zh: 如今，英国有28%的大学毕业生在不需要大学学历的岗位上工作，这一比例是经合组织国家平均水平的两倍。

w.m: adj. 不需要大学学历的
n. 经济合作与发展组织（简称经合组织）

paras.en: This is not to say that there is no point in getting a degree, but rather to stress that a degree is not for everyone, that the switch from classroom to lecture hall is not an inevitable one and that other options are available.
paras.zh: 这并不是说读学位毫无意义，而是要强调：学位并非适合所有人，从中学教室到大学讲堂的转变并非必然，而且还有其他选择。

w.h: there is no point in doing

w.m: adj. 必然的；不可避免的
adj. 可获得的；可供选择的

paras.en: Thankfully, there are signs that this is already happening, with Generation Z seeking to learn from their millennial predecessors, even if parents and teachers tend to be still set in the degree mindset.
paras.zh: 值得庆幸的是，有迹象表明这种情况已经在发生：Z世代正设法从前辈千禧一代身上汲取经验，即便家长和老师往往仍固守着看重学位的思维定式。

w.m: adv. 值得庆幸的是；幸好

paras.en: Employers have long seen the advantages of hiring school leavers who often prove themselves to be more committed and loyal employees than graduates.
paras.zh: 雇主们早就看到了雇用中学毕业生的好处：事实往往证明，他们比大学毕业生更敬业、更忠诚。

w.m: adj. 尽心尽力的；敬业的

paras.en: Many too are seeing the advantages of scrapping a degree requirement for certain roles.
paras.zh: 许多雇主也逐渐看到了对某些岗位取消学位要求的好处。

paras.en: For those for whom a degree is the desired route, consider that this may well be the first of many.
paras.zh: 对于那些想走学位这条路的人来说，要考虑到：这个学位很可能是众多学位中的第一个。

paras.en: In this age of generalists, it pays to have specific knowledge or skills.
paras.zh: 在这个通才遍地的时代，拥有专门的知识或技能会带来回报。

w.m: 做……会有回报；做……是值得的

paras.en: Postgraduates now earn 40 percent more than graduates.
paras.zh: 如今，研究生的收入比本科毕业生高40%。

w.m: n. 大学毕业生；本科毕业生

paras.en: When more and more of us have a degree, it makes sense to have two.
paras.zh: 我们当中有学位的人越来越多，拥有两个学位也就合情合理了。

paras.en: It is unlikely that Generation Z will be done with education at 18 or 21: they will need to be constantly upskilling throughout their career to stay employable.
paras.zh: Z世代不太可能在18岁或21岁就与教育告别：为了保持就业能力，他们需要在整个职业生涯中不断提升技能。

w.m: v. 提升技能；学习新技能
adj. 具备就业能力的；可受雇的

paras.en: It has been estimated that this generation, due to the pressures of technology, the wish for personal fulfillment and desire for diversity, will work for 17 different employers over the course of their working life and have five different careers.
paras.zh: 据估计，由于技术带来的压力、对个人成就感的向往以及对多样化的渴望，这一代人在整个工作生涯中将为17个不同的雇主工作，并从事五种不同的职业。

paras.en: Education, and not just knowledge gained on campus, will be a core part of Generation Z’s career trajectory.
paras.zh: 教育——而不仅仅是在校园里获得的知识——将成为Z世代职业轨迹的核心组成部分。

paras.en: Older generations often talk about their degree in the present and personal tense: ‘I am a geographer’ or ‘I am a classicist’.
paras.zh: 老一辈人谈起自己的学位时，常常用现在时、以第一人称来表述：“我是地理学家”或“我是古典学者”。

paras.en: Their sons or daughters would never say such a thing; it’s as if they already know that their degree won’t define them in the same way.
paras.zh: 他们的子女绝不会说这种话，就好像早已明白，自己的学位不会以同样的方式来定义自己。

passages.name: 2022年考研英语一 Text 3
passages.title: 艺术与科学的合作应是双向的
passages.genre: 议论文 · 科学与艺术
passages.summary: 《自然》杂志的调查显示，近40%的受访者曾与艺术家合作，几乎所有人都表示今后会考虑这样做；科学家正越来越多地寻找视觉艺术家，借助他们向新的受众传播研究成果。文章认为，真正的合作必须是双向的：艺术家并不只是帮助科学家满足传播需求，科学家和艺术家如果在项目中利益与共、能共同设计项目并相互评析各自的工作，这类合作就最有价值。要让合作取得成效，双方都需要投入时间，欣然接受意外和挑战，合作的影响范围也需要超越科研传播这一必要目的。

paras.en: Enlightening, challenging, stimulating, fun.
paras.zh: 富有启发、充满挑战、令人振奋、乐趣十足。

w.m: adj. 富有启发性的；使人增长见识的
adj. 令人振奋的；激发兴趣的

paras.en: These were some of the words that Nature readers used to describe their experience of art-science collaborations in a series of articles on partnerships between artists and researchers.
paras.zh: 在《自然》杂志一系列关于艺术家与研究人员合作的文章中，读者描述自己参与艺术与科学合作的经历时，用到的就有上面这些词语。

w.m: adj. 艺术与科学（结合）的

paras.en: Nearly 40% of the roughly 350 people who responded to an accompanying poll said they had collaborated with artists; and almost all said they would consider doing so in future.
paras.zh: 在与这一系列文章配套的一项调查中，约350人作答，其中近40%表示曾与艺术家合作过；几乎所有人都表示今后会考虑这样做。

paras.en: Such an encouraging result is not surprising.
paras.zh: 如此鼓舞人心的结果并不令人意外。

w.m: adj. 鼓舞人心的；令人鼓舞的
adj. 令人意外的；令人惊讶的

paras.en: Scientists are increasingly seeking out visual artists to help them to communicate their work to new audiences.
paras.zh: 科学家正越来越多地寻找视觉艺术家，请他们帮助自己向新的受众传播研究成果。

paras.en: “Artists help scientists reach a broader audience and make emotional connections that enhance learning,” one respondent said.
paras.zh: 一位受访者说：“艺术家帮助科学家接触到更广泛的受众，并建立起能促进学习的情感联系。”

w.m: n. 受访者；（调查的）答卷人

paras.en: One example of how artists and scientists have together rocked the senses came last month when the Sydney Symphony Orchestra performed a reworked version of Antonio Vivaldi’s The Four Seasons.
paras.zh: 上个月就有一个艺术家和科学家携手震撼人们感官的例子：悉尼交响乐团演奏了安东尼奥·维瓦尔第《四季》的改编版。

w.m: adj. 改编的；重新加工的

paras.en: They reimagined the 300-year-old score by injecting the latest climate prediction data for each season—provided by Monash University’s Climate Change Communication Research Hub.
paras.zh: 他们将每个季节最新的气候预测数据注入这部有300年历史的乐谱，重新诠释了这部作品；这些数据由莫纳什大学气候变化传播研究中心提供。

w.m: v. 重新诠释；重新构想

paras.en: The performance was a creative call to action ahead of November’s United Nations Climate Change Conference in Glasgow, UK.
paras.zh: 这场演出赶在11月于英国格拉斯哥召开的联合国气候变化大会之前，以富有创意的方式发出了行动号召。

w.m: adj. 有创意的；创造性的

paras.en: But a genuine partnership must be a two-way street.
paras.zh: 但真正的合作必须是双向的。

w.m: 双向的事；有来有往的关系

paras.en: Fewer artists than scientists responded to the Nature poll; however, several respondents noted that artists do not simply assist scientists with their communication requirements.
