paras.zh: 在《自然》这项调查中作答的艺术家比科学家少；不过，有几位受访者指出，艺术家并不只是帮助科学家满足传播需求。

w.m: n. 受访者；（调查的）答卷人
在某事上帮助某人；帮助某人处理某事

paras.en: Nor should their work be considered only as an object of study.
paras.zh: 也不应仅仅把艺术家的作品看作研究对象。

w.m: conj. （置于句首，后接倒装）也不

paras.en: The alliances are most valuable when scientists and artists have a shared stake in a project, are able to jointly design it and can critique each other’s work.
paras.zh: 如果科学家和艺术家在项目中利益与共，能够共同设计项目，还能相互评析各自的工作，这类联盟就最有价值。

paras.en: Such an approach can both prompt new research and result in powerful art.
paras.zh: 这种方式既能激发新的研究，又能催生有感染力的艺术。

w.m: adj. 有感染力的；强有力的

paras.en: More than half a century ago, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology opened its Center for Advanced Visual Studies (CAVS) to explore the role of technology in culture.
paras.zh: 半个多世纪前，麻省理工学院成立了高级视觉研究中心（CAVS），以探索技术在文化中的作用。

paras.en: The founders deliberately focused their projects around light—hence the “visual studies” in the name.
paras.zh: 创办者有意让项目聚焦于光，中心名称中的“视觉研究”便由此而来。

paras.en: Light was something that both artists and scientists had an interest in, and therefore could form the basis of collaboration.
paras.zh: 艺术家和科学家都对光感兴趣，因此光可以构成合作的基础。

paras.en: As science and technology progressed, and divided into more sub-disciplines, the centre was simultaneously looking to a time when leading researchers could also be artists, writers and poets, and vice versa.
paras.zh: 随着科学技术不断进步、分化出更多的分支学科，该中心同时也在展望这样一个时代：顶尖研究人员也可以是艺术家、作家和诗人，反之亦然。

paras.en: Nature’s poll findings suggest that this trend is as strong as ever, but, to make a collaboration work, both sides need to invest time and embrace surprise and challenge.
paras.zh: 《自然》的调查结果表明，这一趋势一如既往地强劲；但要让合作取得成效，双方都需要投入时间，并欣然接受意外和挑战。

w.m: 和以往一样……；一如既往地……
使某事取得成效；使……奏效
n. 意外；出人意料的事

paras.en: The reach of art-science tie-ups needs to go beyond the necessary purpose of research communication, and participants must not fall into the trap of stereotyping each other.
paras.zh: 艺术与科学合作的影响范围需要超越科研传播这一必要目的，参与者也不能落入以刻板印象看待彼此的陷阱。

w.m: n. 影响范围；所及范围
adj. 艺术与科学（结合）的
v. 以刻板印象看待；给……贴标签

paras.en: Artists and scientists alike are immersed in discovery and invention, and challenge and critique are core to both, too.
paras.zh: 艺术家和科学家都沉浸在发现与发明之中，挑战与评析也都是二者的核心所在。

passages.name: 2022年考研英语一 Text 4
passages.title: 新西兰解雇保护规定的悖论
passages.genre: 议论文 · 经济与法律
passages.summary: 新西兰《2000年雇佣关系法》中的个人申诉条款禁止雇主无正当理由解雇雇员。作者认为，这些条款适用于高薪经理和高管时会给企业带来困难：限制企业解雇表现不佳的经理，可能反而危及普通工人的工作，即便不危及，也会制约企业生产率，进而制约工人工资；高薪经理自身和整个社会也会受到损害。澳大利亚把收入高于规定门槛的雇员排除在不公平解雇法的保护之外；新西兰2016年一项议员个人法案曾试图允许企业与高收入雇员通过合同约定不适用无正当理由解雇制度，但其提出的机制繁琐难行，法案也在2017年政府更迭后被否决。

paras.en: The personal grievance provisions of New Zealand’s Employment Relations Act 2000 (ERA) prevent an employer from firing an employee without good cause.
paras.zh: 新西兰《2000年雇佣关系法》（ERA）中的个人申诉条款禁止雇主无正当理由解雇雇员。

w.m: 个人申诉（雇员就雇主的不当对待提出的申诉）

paras.en: Instead, dismissals must be justified.
paras.zh: 相反，解雇必须有正当理由。

w.m: adj. 有正当理由的；合理的

paras.en: Employers must both show cause and act in a procedurally fair way.
paras.zh: 雇主既要拿出正当理由，又要在程序上公正行事。

paras.en: Personal grievance procedures were designed to guard the jobs of ordinary workers from “unjustified dismissals”.
paras.zh: 个人申诉程序的设计初衷，是保护普通工人的工作，使他们免遭“无正当理由的解雇”。

w.m: adj. 无正当理由的；不合理的

paras.en: The premise was that the common law of contract lacked sufficient safeguards for workers against arbitrary conduct by management.
paras.zh: 其前提是：普通法中的合同法缺乏足够的保障，无法保护工人免受管理层专断行为的侵害。

paras.en: Long gone are the days when a boss could simply give an employee contractual notice.
paras.zh: 老板只需按合同规定向雇员发出解雇通知就行，这样的日子早已一去不复返了。

w.h: long gone are the days when

w.m: adj. 合同规定的；契约的

paras.en: But these provisions create difficulties for businesses when applied to highly paid managers and executives.
paras.zh: 但这些条款适用于高薪经理和高管时，会给企业带来困难。

paras.en: As countless boards and business owners will attest, constraining firms from firing poorly performing, high-earning managers is a handbrake on boosting productivity and overall performance.
paras.zh: 正如无数董事会和企业主都会证实的那样，限制企业解雇表现不佳的高收入经理，就是给提升生产率和整体业绩拉上了手刹。

paras.en: The difference between C-grade and A-grade managers may very well be the difference between business success and failure.
paras.zh: C级经理和A级经理之间的差别，很可能就是企业成功与失败之间的差别。

w.m: adj. C级的；（喻）表现平平的

paras.en: Between preserving the jobs of ordinary workers and losing them.
paras.zh: 也就是保住普通工人的工作与丢掉这些工作之间的差别。

paras.en: Yet mediocrity is no longer enough to justify a dismissal.
paras.zh: 然而，平庸已不再足以成为解雇的正当理由。

w.m: v. 成为……的正当理由；证明……正当

paras.en: Consequently—and paradoxically—laws introduced to protect the jobs of ordinary workers may be placing those jobs at risk.
paras.zh: 因此，矛盾的是，为保护普通工人的工作而出台的法律，可能正在让这些工作面临风险。

w.m: adv. 矛盾的是；自相矛盾地

paras.en: If not placing jobs at risk, to the extent employment protection laws constrain business owners from dismissing under-performing managers, those laws act as a constraint on firm productivity and therefore on workers’ wages.
paras.zh: 就算没有让工作面临风险，只要就业保护法限制了企业主解雇表现不佳的经理，这些法律也会制约企业生产率，进而制约工人工资。

paras.en: Indeed, in “An International Perspective on the New Zealand Productivity Paradox” (2014), the Productivity Commission singled out the low quality of managerial capabilities as a cause of the country’s poor productivity growth record.
paras.zh: 事实上，生产力委员会在《从国际视角看新西兰生产率悖论》（2014年）中特别指出，管理能力水平低下是该国生产率增长一直表现不佳的原因之一。

w.m: 特别指出……是；把……挑出来作为

paras.en: Nor are highly paid managers themselves immune from the harm caused by the ERA’s unjustified dismissal procedures.
paras.zh: 《雇佣关系法》中针对无正当理由解雇的程序会造成伤害，高薪经理自身也无法免受其害。

w.m: conj. （置于句首，后接倒装）也不

paras.en: Because employment protection laws make it costlier to fire an employee, employers are more cautious about hiring new staff.
paras.zh: 由于就业保护法使解雇雇员的代价更高，雇主在招聘新员工时会更加谨慎。

w.m: 使做某事变得……（it为形式宾语）

paras.en: This makes it harder for the marginal manager to gain employment.
paras.zh: 这使得处于录用边缘的经理更难找到工作。

w.m: adj. 处于边缘的；勉强够格的

paras.en: And firms pay staff less because firms carry the burden of the employment arrangement going wrong.
paras.zh: 而且，雇佣安排一旦出问题，负担要由企业承担，因此企业付给员工的工资会更低。

paras.en: Society also suffers from excessive employment protections.
paras.zh: 社会也会因过度的就业保护而蒙受损害。

paras.en: Stringent job dismissal regulations adversely affect productivity growth and hamper both prosperity and overall well-being.
paras.zh: 严格的解雇规定会对生产率增长产生不利影响，既妨碍繁荣，又妨碍整体福祉。

paras.en: Across the Tasman, Australia deals with the unjustified dismissal paradox by excluding employees earning above a specified “high-income threshold” from the protection of its unfair dismissal laws.
paras.zh: 在塔斯曼海对岸，澳大利亚应对这一无正当理由解雇悖论的办法，是把收入高于规定“高收入门槛”的雇员排除在其不公平解雇法的保护之外。

paras.en: In New Zealand, a 2016 private members’ Bill tried to permit firms and high-income employees to contract out of the unjustified dismissal regime.
paras.zh: 在新西兰，2016年的一项议员个人法案曾试图允许企业和高收入雇员通过合同约定不适用无正当理由解雇制度。

w.m: 通过合同约定不受……约束；选择退出

paras.en: However, the mechanisms proposed were unwieldy and the Bill was voted down following the change in government in 2017.
paras.zh: 然而，法案提出的机制繁琐难行，2017年政府更迭后，该法案被投票否决。

w.m: adj. 繁琐难行的；难以操作的

passages.name: 2022年考研英语二 Text 1
passages.title: 美国蛋业押注气候友好型鸡蛋
passages.genre: 说明文 · 农业与环境
passages.summary: 美国蛋业正押注气候友好型鸡蛋：这类鸡蛋来自采用再生农业的农场，现已首次上架，每打售价高达8美元，在营销时可以宣称有助于对抗气候变化。蛋业的这番推广，是对再生农场的动物产品能否成为下一种高端产品的首次重大考验。不过，再生产品的概念难以三言两语界定清楚，因而可能难以推销，这种农业方式对食品的改善也微乎其微。业界则押注，那些为高端特性多花钱的消费者同样会欣然接受可持续理念，而调查也显示，较年轻的几代人更关心气候变化。

paras.en: On a recent sunny day, 13,000 chickens roam over Larry Brown’s 40 windswept acres in Shiner, Texas.
paras.zh: 最近的一个晴天，在得克萨斯州希纳，拉里·布朗那40英亩饱受风吹的土地上，13,000只鸡在四处走动。

w.m: adj. 晴朗的；阳光充足的
adj. 受强风吹的；风大的

paras.en: Some rest in the shade of a parked car.
paras.zh: 有的在一辆停着的汽车投下的阴凉里休息。

paras.en: Others drink water with the cows.
paras.zh: 还有的和牛一起喝水。

paras.en: This all seems random, but it’s by design, part of what the $6.1 billion U.S. egg industry bets will be its next big thing: climate-friendly eggs.
paras.zh: 这一切看似随意，实则是有意为之，是生产气候友好型鸡蛋的一环——规模达61亿美元的美国蛋业押注，这种鸡蛋将成为行业的下一个大热门。

paras.en: These eggs, which are making their debut now on shelves for as much as $8 a dozen, are still labeled organic and animal-friendly, but they’re also from birds that live on farms using regenerative agriculture—special techniques to cultivate rich soils that can trap greenhouse gases.
paras.zh: 这些鸡蛋眼下正首次登上货架，每打售价高达8美元；它们仍然标注为有机、善待动物的产品，但下蛋的鸡还生活在采用再生农业的农场上——再生农业是指用特殊技术培育肥沃的土壤，这种土壤能锁住温室气体。

w.m: v. 把……标注为；给……贴标签
adj. 善待动物的；对动物友好的

paras.en: Such eggs could be marketed as helping to fight climate change.
paras.zh: 这类鸡蛋在营销时可以宣称有助于对抗气候变化。

w.m: 把……宣传为；以……为卖点推销

paras.en: “I’m excited about our progress,” says Brown, who harvests eggs for Denver-based NestFresh Eggs and is adding more cover crops that draw worms and crickets for the chickens to eat.
paras.zh: “我们取得的进展让我很兴奋。”布朗说。他为总部位于丹佛的NestFresh Eggs公司养鸡产蛋，目前正在种植更多覆盖作物，这些作物能招来蠕虫和蟋蟀，供鸡食用。

paras.en: The birds’ waste then fertilizes fields.
paras.zh: 鸡粪随后又成了田地的肥料。

paras.en: Such improvements “allow our hens to forage for higher-quality natural feed that will be good for the land, the hens, and the eggs that we supply to our customers.”
paras.zh: 这些改进“让我们的母鸡能够寻觅质量更高的天然饲料，这些饲料对土地、对母鸡、对我们供应给顾客的鸡蛋都会有好处”。

paras.en: The egg industry’s push is the first major test of whether animal products from regenerative farms can become the next premium offering.
paras.zh: 蛋业的这番推广，是对再生农场的动物产品能否成为下一种高端产品的首次重大考验。

w.m: adj. 高端的；优质高价的

paras.en: In barely more than a decade, organic eggs went from being dismissed as a niche product in natural foods stores to being sold at Walmart.
paras.zh: 短短十年出头，有机鸡蛋就从被视为天然食品店里不值一提的小众产品，变成了在沃尔玛上架销售的商品。

paras.en: More recently there were similar doubts about probiotics and plant-based meats, but both have exploded into major supermarket categories.
paras.zh: 近些年，人们对益生菌和植物肉也有过类似的怀疑，但两者都已爆发式增长，成为超市里的主要品类。

w.m: 爆发式增长为；迅速发展成

paras.en: If the sustainable-egg rollout is successful, it could open the floodgates for regenerative beef, broccoli, and beyond.
paras.zh: 如果可持续鸡蛋推广成功，就可能为再生农业出产的牛肉、西兰花乃至更多产品打开闸门。

w.m: 为……打开闸门；使……大量涌现

paras.en: Regenerative products could be a hard sell, because the concept is tough to define quickly, says Julie Stanton, associate professor of agricultural economics at Pennsylvania State University Brandywine.
paras.zh: 宾夕法尼亚州立大学布兰迪万校区农业经济学副教授朱莉·斯坦顿说，再生产品可能难以推销，因为这个概念很难三言两语界定清楚。

w.m: 难以推销的东西；难以让人接受的事

paras.en: Such farming also brings minimal, if any, improvement to the food products (though some producers say their eggs have more protein).
paras.zh: 此外，这种农业方式即使能给食品带来什么改善，也微乎其微（不过有些生产商说，他们的鸡蛋蛋白质含量更高）。

w.m: adj. 极少的；微乎其微的

paras.en: The industry is betting that the same consumers paying more for premium attributes such as free-range, non-GMO, and pasture-raised eggs will embrace sustainability.
paras.zh: 业界正押注：那些为散养、非转基因、牧场饲养等高端特性多花钱买鸡蛋的消费者，同样会欣然接受可持续理念。

w.m: adj. 高端的；优质高价的

paras.en: Surveys show that younger generations are more concerned about climate change, and some of the success of plant-based meat can be chalked up to shoppers wanting to signal their desire to protect the environment.
paras.zh: 调查显示，较年轻的几代人更关心气候变化；植物肉取得的成功，有一部分可以归因于购物者想表明自己有保护环境的意愿。

paras.en: Young adults “really care about the planet,” says John Brunnquell, president of Egg Innovations.
paras.zh: Egg Innovations公司总裁约翰·布伦奎尔说，年轻人“真的很关心地球”。

paras.en: “They are absolutely altering the food chain beyond what I think even they understand.”
paras.zh: “他们绝对是在改变食品产业链，我觉得改变的程度甚至超出了他们自己的认识。”

w.m: （从生产到消费的）食品产业链；食物链

passages.name: 2022年考研英语二 Text 2
passages.title: 越来越多美国人退休后继续工作
passages.genre: 说明文 · 社会与经济
passages.summary: 越来越多的美国人选择在退休后继续工作很长时间，这一日益明显的趋势有可能颠覆旧的劳动力模式。哈里斯民调公司为德美利证券开展的调查显示，40岁及以上的美国人中有三分之一已经或计划在退休后工作，超过半数的“退而不休者”表示即使钱够用也会在晚年工作；除了经济需要，保持头脑灵活、防止无聊、避免抑郁等个人满足感也是原因。美国人越来越长寿，这是退休模式发生变化的原因之一，他们也因此在增加储蓄。一家财务规划公司的联合创始人指出，许多人准备退休后工作，是因为担心晚年难以维持生计；他建议即将退休的人与财务顾问商谈，制定长期财务目标。

paras.en: More Americans are opting to work well into retirement, a growing trend that threatens to upend the old workforce model.
paras.zh: 越来越多的美国人选择在退休后继续工作很长时间，这一趋势日益明显，有可能颠覆旧的劳动力模式。

w.m: 直到……很久；深入（某段时期）
adj. 日益增长的；日益明显的

paras.en: One in three Americans who are at least 40 have or plan to have a job in retirement to prepare for a longer life, according to a survey conducted by Harris Poll for TD Ameritrade.
paras.zh: 哈里斯民调公司为德美利证券开展的一项调查显示，40岁及以上的美国人中，有三分之一退休后已在工作或打算工作，为更长的寿命做准备。

paras.en: Even more surprising is that more than half of “unretirees”—those who plan to work in retirement or went back to work after retiring—said they would be employed in their later years even if they had enough money to settle down, the survey showed.
paras.zh: 更令人惊讶的是，调查显示，超过半数的“退而不休者”——即计划在退休后工作或退休后又重返职场的人——表示，即使有足够的钱安稳度日，他们也会在晚年工作。

w.m: 更令人惊讶的是（表语前置的倒装）
n. 退而不休者（退休后继续或重新工作的人）

paras.en: Financial needs aren’t the only culprit for the “unretirement” trend.
paras.zh: 经济上的需要并不是导致“退而不休”趋势的唯一原因。

w.m: n. 退而不休（退休后继续或重新工作）

paras.en: Other reasons, according to the study, include personal fulfillment such as staying mentally fit, preventing boredom or avoiding depression.
paras.zh: 研究显示，其他原因包括个人满足感，比如保持头脑灵活、防止无聊或避免抑郁。

w.m: adj. 健康的；状态良好的

paras.en: About 72% of “unretiree” respondents said that they would return to work once retired to keep mentally fit, while 59% said it would be tied to making ends meet.
paras.zh: 在受访的“退而不休者”中，约72%表示，退休后他们会为了保持头脑灵活而重返工作岗位；59%则表示，重返工作与维持生计有关。

w.m: adj. 健康的；状态良好的

paras.en: “The concept of retirement is evolving,” said Christine Russell, senior manager of retirement at TD Ameritrade.
paras.zh: 德美利证券退休业务高级经理克里斯蒂娜·拉塞尔说：“退休的概念正在演变。”

paras.en: “It’s not just about finances.
paras.zh: “这不仅仅是财务问题。

w.m: 不仅仅关乎；不只是……的问题

paras.en: The value of work is also driving folks to continue working past retirement.”
paras.zh: 工作的价值也在促使人们过了退休年龄仍继续工作。”

paras.en: One reason for the change in retirement patterns: Americans are living longer.
paras.zh: 退休模式发生变化的一个原因是：美国人越来越长寿了。

paras.en: The share of the population 65 and older was 16% in 2018, up 3.2% from the prior year, according to the U.S. Census Bureau.
paras.zh: 美国人口普查局的数据显示，2018年，65岁及以上人口占总人口的16%，比上一年上升了3.2%。

paras.en: That’s also up 30.2% since 2010.
paras.zh: 自2010年以来，这一比例也上升了30.2%。

paras.en: Older Americans are also the fastest-growing segment of the U.S. workforce, and boomers are expected to live longer than previous generations.
paras.zh: 老年人也是美国劳动力中增长最快的群体，而且预计婴儿潮一代会比前几代人更长寿。

paras.en: The percentage of retirement-age people in the labor force has doubled over the past three decades.
paras.zh: 过去三十年间，达到退休年龄的人当中属于劳动力人口的比例翻了一番。

paras.en: About 20% of people 65 and older were in the workforce in February, up from an all-time low of 10% in January 1985, according to money manager United Income.
paras.zh: 资产管理公司United Income的数据显示，2月份，65岁及以上的人中约有20%属于劳动力人口，高于1985年1月创下的10%这一历史最低点。

w.m: 资产管理公司；理财经理

paras.en: Because of longer life spans, Americans are also boosting their savings to preserve their nest eggs, according to the TD Ameritrade study, which surveyed 2,000 adults between 40 and 79.
paras.zh: 德美利证券的这项研究调查了2,000名40至79岁的成年人，结果显示，由于寿命延长，美国人也在增加储蓄，以守住自己的养老钱。

paras.en: Six in 10 “unretirees” are increasing their savings in anticipation of a longer life, according to the survey.
paras.zh: 调查显示，每10个“退而不休者”中就有6个正在增加储蓄，因为他们预计自己会活得更久。

paras.en: Among the most popular ways they are doing this, the company said, is by reducing their overall expenses, securing life insurance or maximizing their contributions to retirement accounts.
paras.zh: 该公司称，他们为此最常采用的做法包括：削减总体开支、购买人寿保险，或者把退休账户的缴款额提到最高。

paras.en: Seniors are living longer, but planning for the extended years is key.
paras.zh: 老年人的寿命越来越长，但关键是要为多出来的这些年做好规划。

w.m: adj. 关键的；至关重要的

paras.en: Unfortunately, many people who are opting to work in retirement are preparing to do so because they are worried about making ends meet in their later years, said Brent Weiss, a co-founder at Baltimore-based financial-planning firm Facet Wealth.
paras.zh: 总部位于巴尔的摩的财务规划公司Facet Wealth的联合创始人布伦特·韦斯说，遗憾的是，许多选择在退休后工作的人之所以准备这样做，是因为担心自己晚年难以维持生计。

w.m: adj. 总部位于巴尔的摩的

paras.en: He suggested that preretirees should speak with a financial adviser to set long-term financial goals.
paras.zh: 他建议，即将退休的人应该与财务顾问谈一谈，制定长期财务目标。

paras.en: “The most challenging moments in life are getting married, starting a family and ultimately retiring,” Weiss said.
paras.zh: 韦斯说：“人生中最具挑战性的时刻是结婚、生儿育女，以及最终退休。”

paras.en: “It’s not just a financial decision, but an emotional one.
paras.zh: “这不只是一个财务决定，也是一个情感上的决定。

paras.en: Many people believe they can’t retire.”
paras.zh: 很多人认为自己无法退休。”

passages.name: 2022年考研英语二 Text 3
passages.title: 正视暗黑模式：从监管到行业自律
passages.genre: 议论文 · 商业与科技
passages.summary: “暗黑模式”泛指操纵用户界面、以影响用户决策能力的各种手法，比如让会员或订阅服务注册顺畅、取消却很难；2019年的一项研究发现，约每10个受调查的产品页面和网站中就有1个采用这类手法，但人们对这一概念仍然认识不足。作者认为，企业和非营利组织的领导者应该了解暗黑模式、避开其造成的灰色地带，企业还应与IT、合规、风控和法务团队一起审查隐私政策，并让设计、编程、营销和广告人员参与讨论。立法者和监管机构正慢慢着手处理这一问题，商界也需要从内部加强问责；暗黑模式也可以通过自我监管来解决，但前提是各组织不仅对照法律要求，还对照行业最佳实践和标准自我问责。

paras.en: We have all encountered them, in both our personal and professional lives.
paras.zh: 我们每个人都遇到过它们，无论是在个人生活中还是在工作中。

paras.en: Think about the times you felt tricked or frustrated by a membership or subscription that had a seamless sign-up process but was later difficult to cancel.
paras.zh: 想想那些时候：某项会员或订阅服务的注册流程顺畅无阻，后来却很难取消，让你觉得上当受骗或恼火。

w.m: n. 会员资格；会员身份
adj. 顺畅无阻的；无缝的

paras.en: Something that should be simple and transparent can be complicated, intentionally or unintentionally, in ways that impair consumer choice.
paras.zh: 本应简单透明的事情，可能会被有意或无意地复杂化，以致损害消费者的选择权。

w.m: adj. 透明的；清晰易懂的

paras.en: These are examples of dark patterns.
paras.zh: 这些都是暗黑模式的例子。

w.m: 暗黑模式（诱导用户违背本意做决定的界面设计）

paras.en: First coined in 2010 by user experience expert Harry Brignull, “dark patterns” is a catch-all term for practices that manipulate user interfaces to influence the decision-making ability of users.
paras.zh: “暗黑模式”一词由用户体验专家哈里·布里格努尔于2010年首创，是一个统称，泛指操纵用户界面、以影响用户决策能力的各种手法。

paras.en: Brignull identifies 12 types of common dark patterns, ranging from misdirection and hidden costs to “roach motel,” where a user experience seems easy and intuitive at the start, but turns difficult when the user tries to get out.
paras.zh: 布里格努尔归纳出12种常见的暗黑模式，从误导、隐藏费用到“蟑螂旅馆”，不一而足。在“蟑螂旅馆”模式中，用户体验一开始看似简单直观，可等到用户想要脱身时，却变得困难起来。

w.m: 蟑螂旅馆（一种捕蟑盒，进得去出不来）
adj. 直观的；易懂好用的

paras.en: In a 2019 study of 53,000 product pages and 11,000 websites, researchers found that about one in 10 employs these design practices.
paras.zh: 在2019年一项针对53,000个产品页面和11,000个网站的研究中，研究人员发现，约每10个中就有1个采用了这些设计手法。

paras.en: Though widely prevalent, the concept of dark patterns is still not well understood.
paras.zh: 暗黑模式虽然广泛存在，但人们对这一概念仍然认识不足。

w.m: adj. 普遍存在的；盛行的

paras.en: Business and nonprofit leaders should be aware of dark patterns and try to avoid the gray areas they engender.
paras.zh: 企业和非营利组织的领导者应该了解暗黑模式，并努力避开它们造成的灰色地带。

paras.en: Where is the line between ethical, persuasive design and dark patterns?
paras.zh: 合乎道德的说服式设计与暗黑模式之间的界限在哪里？

w.m: adj. 合乎道德的；伦理的
adj. 劝导性的；有说服力的

paras.en: Businesses should engage in conversations with IT, compliance, risk, and legal teams to review their privacy policy, and include in the discussion the customer/user experience designers and coders responsible for the company’s user interface, as well as the marketers and advertisers responsible for sign-ups, checkout baskets, pricing, and promotions.
paras.zh: 企业应与IT、合规、风控和法务团队展开对话，审查自身的隐私政策，并让负责公司用户界面的客户/用户体验设计师和程序员，以及负责注册、结账购物车、定价和促销的营销人员和广告人员也参与讨论。

paras.en: Any or all of these teams can play a role in creating or avoiding “digital deception.”
paras.zh: 这些团队中任何一个乃至全部，都可能在制造或避免“数字欺骗”方面发挥作用。

paras.en: Lawmakers and regulators are slowly starting to address the ambiguity around dark patterns, most recently at the state level.
paras.zh: 立法者和监管机构正慢慢着手处理暗黑模式问题上的模糊之处，最近的举措来自州一级。

w.m: n. 模糊之处；含糊不清

paras.en: In March, the California Attorney General announced the approval of additional regulations under the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) that “ensure that consumers will not be confused or misled when seeking to exercise their data privacy rights.”
paras.zh: 3月，加州总检察长宣布，根据《加州消费者隐私法案》（CCPA）制定的补充法规已获批准，这些法规“确保消费者在寻求行使自身数据隐私权时不会感到困惑或受到误导”。

paras.en: The regulations aim to ban dark patterns—this means prohibiting companies from burdening consumers with “confusing language or unnecessary steps such as forcing them to click through multiple screens or listen to reasons why they shouldn’t opt out.”
paras.zh: 这些法规旨在禁止暗黑模式，这意味着禁止企业让消费者承受“令人困惑的措辞或不必要的步骤，比如强迫他们点击浏览多个页面，或者听取他们不应选择退出的理由”所带来的负担。

paras.en: As more states consider promulgating additional regulations, there is a need for greater accountability from within the business community.
paras.zh: 随着越来越多的州考虑颁布更多法规，商界需要从内部加强问责。

paras.en: Dark patterns also can be addressed on a self-regulatory basis, but only if organizations hold themselves accountable, not just to legal requirements but also to industry best practices and standards.
paras.zh: 暗黑模式也可以通过自我监管来解决，但前提是各组织要自我问责，不仅要对照法律要求，还要对照行业最佳实践和标准。

w.m: adj. 自我监管的；自律的
只有在……的情况下；前提是
自我问责；要求自己负责

passages.name: 2022年考研英语二 Text 4
passages.title: 一堂伦理课或能让学生少吃肉
passages.genre: 说明文 · 教育与伦理
passages.summary: 伦理课在世界各地都很常见，但科学家们并不确定这些课程能否真正改变人的行为。发表在《认知》期刊上的一项新研究发现，讨论过肉类伦理问题的学生，所购餐食中含肉的比例从52%降到了45%，并在为期数周的研究期间保持稳定，而另一组学生的这一比例仍为52%。未参与研究的心理学家斯特罗明格表示，不能排除某个未知混杂变量的影响，而且如果效果属实，它可能会被另一次助推逆转；研究合著者施维茨格贝尔则猜测，作用最大的是社会影响，研究人员正在进一步探究各项因素的具体影响。

paras.en: Although ethics classes are common around the world, scientists are unsure if their lessons can actually change behavior; evidence either way is weak, relying on contrived laboratory tests or sometimes unreliable self-reports.
paras.zh: 尽管伦理课在世界各地都很常见，但科学家们并不确定课上所讲的内容能否真正改变人的行为；正反两方面的证据都很薄弱，依靠的是人为设计的实验室测试，或者有时并不可靠的自我报告。

w.m: adj. 不确定的；没把握的
无论哪一方面；正反两方面
adj. 人为设计的；不自然的

paras.en: But a new study published in Cognition found that, in at least one real-world situation, a single ethics lesson may have had lasting effects.
paras.zh: 但发表在《认知》期刊上的一项新研究发现，至少在一种现实情境中，仅仅一堂伦理课也许就产生了持久的效果。

w.m: adj. 现实世界的；真实的
adj. 仅仅一个的；单个的

paras.en: The researchers investigated one class session’s impact on eating meat.
paras.zh: 研究人员考察了一节课对吃肉行为的影响。

paras.en: They chose this particular behavior for three reasons, according to study co-author Eric Schwitzgebel, a philosopher at the University of California, Riverside: students’ attitudes on the topic are variable and unstable, behavior is easily measurable, and ethics literature largely agrees that eating less meat is good because it reduces environmental harm and animal suffering.
paras.zh: 据该研究的合著者、加州大学河滨分校的哲学家埃里克·施维茨格贝尔介绍，他们之所以选择这一特定行为，有三个原因：学生在这个问题上的态度多变且不稳定；这种行为容易测量；而且伦理学文献大体上一致认为，少吃肉是好事，因为这样能减少对环境的危害和动物的痛苦。

w.m: adv. 大体上；在很大程度上

paras.en: Half of the students in four large philosophy classes read an article on the ethics of factory-farmed meat, optionally watched an 11-minute video on the topic and joined a 50-minute discussion.
paras.zh: 四门大型哲学课的学生中，有一半阅读了一篇探讨工厂化养殖肉类伦理问题的文章，还可以选择观看一段关于这一话题的11分钟视频，并参加了一场50分钟的讨论。

w.m: adv. 可选择地；非强制地

paras.en: The other half focused on charitable giving instead.
paras.zh: 另一半学生则把学习重点放在了慈善捐赠上。

paras.en: Then, unknown to the students, the researchers studied their anonymized meal-card purchases for that semester—nearly 14,000 receipts for almost 500 students.
paras.zh: 随后，研究人员在学生不知情的情况下，研究了他们那个学期经过匿名处理的饭卡消费记录——近500名学生的近14,000张收据。

w.m: 在……不知情的情况下；不为……所知
n. 购买（记录）；所购之物

paras.en: “It’s an awesome data set,” says Nina Strohminger, a psychologist who teaches business ethics at the University of Pennsylvania and was not involved in the study.
paras.zh: “这个数据集太棒了。”宾夕法尼亚大学的心理学家尼娜·斯特罗明格说。她在该校讲授商业伦理学，并未参与这项研究。

paras.en: Schwitzgebel predicted the intervention would have no effect; he had previously found that ethics professors do not differ from other professors on a range of behaviors, including voting rates, blood donation and returning library books.
paras.zh: 施维茨格贝尔原本预计这次干预不会产生任何效果；他此前曾发现，在包括投票率、献血和归还图书馆图书在内的一系列行为上，伦理学教授与其他教授并无差别。

paras.en: But among student subjects who discussed meat ethics, meal purchases containing meat decreased from 52 to 45 percent—and this effect held steady for the study’s duration of several weeks.
paras.zh: 但在讨论过肉类伦理问题的学生受试者中，所购餐食中含肉的比例从52%降到了45%——而且这一效果在为期数周的研究期间始终保持稳定。

paras.en: Purchases from the other group remained at 52 percent.
paras.zh: 另一组学生所购餐食中含肉的比例仍保持在52%。

paras.en: “That’s actually a pretty large effect for a pretty small intervention,” Schwitzgebel says.
paras.zh: “对于一次相当小的干预来说，这个效果其实相当大。”施维茨格贝尔说。

paras.en: Strohminger says she wants the effect to be real but cannot rule out some unknown confounding variable.
paras.zh: 斯特罗明格说，她希望这一效果是真实的，但无法排除某个未知混杂变量的影响。

paras.en: And if real, she notes, it might be reversible by another nudge: “Easy come, easy go.”
paras.zh: 她还指出，如果这一效果确实存在，它可能会被另一次助推逆转：“来得容易，去得也快。”

w.m: adj. 可逆转的；可撤销的

paras.en: Schwitzgebel suspects the greatest impact came from social influence—classmates or teaching assistants leading the discussions may have shared their own vegetarianism, showing it as achievable or more common.
paras.zh: 施维茨格贝尔猜测，作用最大的是社会影响——同学或主持讨论的助教可能说过自己吃素，让人看到吃素是做得到的，或是更为普遍的。

w.m: v. 猜测；怀疑（某事属实）
adj. 可实现的；做得到的

paras.en: Second, the video may have had an emotional impact.
paras.zh: 其次，那段视频可能带来了情感上的冲击。

paras.en: Least rousing, he thinks, was rational argument, although his co-authors say reason might play a bigger role.
paras.zh: 他认为，最不能打动人的是理性论证，不过他的合著者们说，理性可能会发挥更大的作用。

w.m: adj. 激发情感的；鼓舞人心的

paras.en: Now the researchers are probing the specific effects of teaching style, teaching assistants’ eating habits and students’ video exposure.
paras.zh: 现在，研究人员正在探究教学风格、助教的饮食习惯以及学生观看视频的情况各自产生的具体影响。

paras.en: Meanwhile Schwitzgebel—who had predicted no effect—will be eating his words.
paras.zh: 与此同时，曾预言不会有任何效果的施维茨格贝尔，将不得不收回自己说过的话了。

w.m: 收回前言；承认说错（此处又暗指吃肉，一语双关）

passages.name: 2021年考研英语一 Text 1
passages.title: 英国铁路票价年年涨，服务理应有保障
passages.genre: 议论文 · 交通与公共政策
passages.summary: 英国铁路票价每年一月照例上涨，今年平均涨幅为2.7%，仍远高于官方以消费者价格指数衡量的通胀率。历届政府允许涨价，理由是铁路的投资和运营成本应由使用者而非普通纳税人承担。作者认为，乘客付出大笔费用，理应得到基本水准的服务，受罢工影响最严重的人应当获得赔偿；政府承诺的最低服务要求应当成为解决铁路长期问题的一揽子措施的一部分。如果乘客的愤怒得不到迅速回应，国有化的威胁将卷土重来。

paras.en: How can Britain’s train operators possibly justify yet another increase to rail passenger fares?
paras.zh: 英国的火车运营商又一次上调铁路客运票价，究竟有什么正当理由？

w.m: adv. （用于疑问句，加强语气）究竟；怎么可能
v. 证明……正当；为……找到正当理由

paras.en: It has become a grimly reliable annual ritual: every January the cost of travelling by train rises, imposing a significant extra burden on those who have no option but to use the rail network to get to work or otherwise.
paras.zh: 说来令人沮丧，这已成为一年一度、雷打不动的惯例：每到一月，乘火车出行的费用都会上涨，给那些别无选择、只能依靠铁路网上班或出于其他目的出行的人带来相当大的额外负担。

w.m: adv. 令人沮丧地；令人不快地
adj. （每次都）必然出现的；可以预料的
adj. 一年一度的；每年的
或出于其他目的；或其他

paras.en: This year’s rise, an average of 2.7 percent, may be a fraction lower than last year’s, but it is still well above the official Consumer Price Index (CPI) measure of inflation.
paras.zh: 今年的涨幅平均为2.7%，或许比去年略低一点，但仍远高于官方以消费者价格指数（CPI）衡量的通胀率。

paras.en: Successive governments have permitted such increases on the grounds that the cost of investing in and running the rail network should be borne by those who use it, rather than the general taxpayer.
paras.zh: 历届政府都允许这样涨价，理由是投资和运营铁路网的成本应当由使用铁路网的人承担，而不是由普通纳税人承担。

paras.en: Why, the argument goes, should a car-driving pensioner from Lincolnshire have to subsidise the daily commute of a stockbroker from Surrey?
paras.zh: 持这种观点的人会问：凭什么要让林肯郡一位开车出行的退休老人，去补贴萨里郡一位股票经纪人每天的通勤呢？

w.m: 按照这种说法；有观点认为
n. 领养老金的人；退休老人

paras.en: Equally, there is a sense that the travails of commuters in the South East, many of whom will face among the biggest rises, have received too much attention compared to those who must endure the relatively poor infrastructure of the Midlands and the North.
paras.zh: 同样，人们也觉得，与那些不得不忍受中部和北部地区基础设施相对落后的人相比，东南部的通勤者（其中许多人将面临数一数二的涨幅）所经历的艰辛受到了过多关注。

w.m: 数一数二的；最大的……之列

paras.en: However, over the past 12 months, those commuters have also experienced some of the worst rail strikes in years.
paras.zh: 然而，在过去12个月里，这些通勤者还经历了多年来最严重的几次铁路罢工。

paras.en: It is all very well train operators trumpeting the improvements they are making to the network, but passengers should be able to expect a basic level of service for the substantial sums they are now paying to travel.
paras.zh: 火车运营商大肆宣扬自己正在改进铁路网，这固然好，但乘客如今为出行付出了大笔费用，理应可以期待基本水准的服务。

paras.en: The responsibility for the latest wave of strikes rests on the unions.
paras.zh: 最近这一波罢工的责任在于工会。

paras.en: However, there is a strong case that those who have been worst affected by industrial action should receive compensation for the disruption they have suffered.
paras.zh: 不过，有充分的理由认为，受罢工等劳工行动影响最严重的人，应当就自己出行受阻获得赔偿。

w.h: there is a strong case that

paras.en: The Government has pledged to change the law to introduce a minimum service requirement so that, even when strikes occur, services can continue to operate.
paras.zh: 政府已承诺修改法律，引入最低服务要求，这样即使发生罢工，列车也能继续运行。

paras.en: This should form part of a wider package of measures to address the long-running problems on Britain’s railways.
paras.zh: 这应当成为更全面的一揽子措施的一部分，用以解决英国铁路长期存在的问题。

w.m: adj. 长期存在的；持续已久的

paras.en: Yes, more investment is needed, but passengers will not be willing to pay more indefinitely if they must also endure cramped, unreliable services, interrupted by regular chaos when timetables are changed, or planned maintenance is managed incompetently.
paras.zh: 没错，是需要更多投资，但如果乘客还得忍受列车拥挤、服务不可靠，而且每逢时刻表调整或计划内的检修工作管理无方，服务就会因时常出现的混乱而中断，那么他们不会愿意无休止地多付钱。

w.m: adv. 无限期地；无休止地
n. （火车等公共交通的）班次；客运服务
adj. 计划内的；预先安排的

paras.en: The threat of nationalisation may have been seen off for now, but it will return with a vengeance if the justified anger of passengers is not addressed in short order.
paras.zh: 国有化的威胁眼下或许已经化解，但如果乘客合情合理的怒火得不到迅速回应，这一威胁就会卷土重来，而且来势更猛。

passages.name: 2021年考研英语一 Text 2
passages.title: 印尼扶贫项目与毁林减少
passages.genre: 说明文 · 环境与经济
passages.summary: 去年，印度尼西亚的毁林速度连续第三年放缓，原因之一可能是该国推行的有条件现金转移支付扶贫项目。扶贫与环境保护常被视为相互冲突的目标，但经济学家费拉罗分析卫星数据后发现，该项目与毁林减少30%相关，很可能是因为农村穷人把领到的现金当作应对恶劣天气的临时保险。这一结论能否推广到别处尚不确定，但研究表明，对人有益的事物也可能对环境有益。

paras.en: Last year marked the third year in a row that Indonesia’s bleak rate of deforestation has slowed in pace.
paras.zh: 去年，印度尼西亚令人忧心的毁林速度连续第三年放缓。

w.m: v. 标志着；是（某一时刻）
adj. 令人忧心的；暗淡的

paras.en: One reason for the turnaround may be the country’s antipoverty program.
paras.zh: 这一好转的原因之一，可能在于该国的扶贫项目。

paras.en: In 2007, Indonesia started phasing in a program that gives money to its poorest residents under certain conditions, such as requiring people to keep kids in school or get regular medical care.
paras.zh: 2007年，印度尼西亚开始逐步推行一个项目，在一定条件下向最贫困的居民发放钱款，比如要求人们不让孩子辍学，或定期接受医疗服务。

paras.en: Called conditional cash transfers, or CCTs, these social assistance programs are designed to reduce inequality and break the cycle of poverty.
paras.zh: 这类社会救助项目名为有条件现金转移支付（简称CCT），旨在减少不平等，打破贫困的循环。

paras.en: They’re already used in dozens of countries worldwide.
paras.zh: 这类项目已在全球数十个国家实施。

paras.en: In Indonesia, the program has provided enough food and medicine to substantially reduce severe growth problems among children.
paras.zh: 在印度尼西亚，该项目提供的食物和药品已足以大幅减少儿童严重的生长发育问题。

paras.en: But CCT programs don’t generally consider effects on the environment.
paras.zh: 但CCT项目一般不考虑对环境的影响。

paras.en: In fact, poverty alleviation and environmental protection are often viewed as conflicting goals, says Paul Ferraro, an economist at Johns Hopkins University.
paras.zh: 约翰斯·霍普金斯大学的经济学家保罗·费拉罗说，事实上，扶贫和环境保护常被视为相互冲突的目标。

w.m: adj. 相互冲突的；矛盾的

paras.en: That’s because economic growth can be correlated with environmental degradation, while protecting the environment is sometimes correlated with greater poverty.
paras.zh: 这是因为经济增长可能与环境退化相关，而保护环境有时又与更严重的贫困相关。

paras.en: However, those correlations don’t prove cause and effect.
paras.zh: 然而，这些相关性并不能证明因果关系。

paras.en: The only previous study analyzing causality, based on an area in Mexico that had instituted CCTs, supported the traditional view.
paras.zh: 此前唯一一项分析因果关系的研究以墨西哥一个已实行CCT项目的地区为对象，结果支持了传统观点。

paras.en: There, as people got more money, some of them may have cleared more land for cattle to raise for meat, Ferraro says.
paras.zh: 费拉罗说，在那里，随着人们手头的钱多了起来，其中一些人可能开辟了更多土地来饲养肉牛。

paras.en: Such programs do not have to negatively affect the environment, though.
paras.zh: 不过，这类项目并不一定会对环境产生负面影响。

paras.en: Ferraro wanted to see if Indonesia’s poverty-alleviation program was affecting deforestation.
paras.zh: 费拉罗想弄清楚，印度尼西亚的扶贫项目是否正对毁林产生影响。

paras.en: Indonesia has the third-largest area of tropical forest in the world and one of the highest deforestation rates.
paras.zh: 印度尼西亚是世界上热带森林面积第三大的国家，也是毁林率最高的国家之一。

paras.en: Ferraro analyzed satellite data showing annual forest loss from 2008 to 2012—including during Indonesia’s phase-in of the antipoverty program—in 7,468 forested villages across 15 provinces.
paras.zh: 费拉罗分析了卫星数据，这些数据显示了15个省份7468个有森林覆盖的村庄在2008年至2012年间每年的森林损失，这段时间包括了印度尼西亚逐步推行扶贫项目的时期。

w.m: n. 逐步推行；分阶段实施

paras.en: “We see that the program is associated with a 30 percent reduction in deforestation,” Ferraro says.
paras.zh: 费拉罗说：“我们看到，这个项目与毁林减少30%相关。”

paras.en: That’s likely because the rural poor are using the money as makeshift insurance policies against inclement weather, Ferraro says.
paras.zh: 费拉罗说，这很可能是因为农村穷人正把这笔钱当作应对恶劣天气的临时保险。

w.m: adj. 临时凑合的；权宜的

paras.en: Typically, if rains are delayed, people may clear land to plant more rice to supplement their harvests.
paras.zh: 通常情况下，如果降雨推迟，人们可能会开垦土地，多种水稻，以补充收成。

paras.en: With the CCTs, individuals instead can use the money to supplement their harvests.
paras.zh: 有了CCT项目，人们就可以改用这笔钱来补充收成。

paras.en: Whether this research translates elsewhere is anybody’s guess.
paras.zh: 这项研究的结果能否适用于其他地方，谁也说不准。

paras.en: Ferraro suggests the results may transfer to other parts of Asia, due to commonalities such as the importance of growing rice and market access.
paras.zh: 费拉罗认为，由于存在一些共同点，比如种植水稻的重要性和进入市场的便利程度，这些结果或许也能推广到亚洲其他地区。

w.m: 进入市场的机会；进入市场的便利程度

paras.en: And regardless of transferability, the study shows that what’s good for people may also be good for the environment.
paras.zh: 而且，无论能否推广到别处，这项研究都表明，对人有益的事物也可能对环境有益。

w.m: n. 可推广性；可转移性

paras.en: Even if this program didn’t reduce poverty, Ferraro says, “the value of the avoided deforestation just for carbon dioxide emissions alone is more than the program costs.”
paras.zh: 费拉罗说，即使这个项目没能减少贫困，“仅就二氧化碳排放一项而言，避免毁林所带来的价值就已经超过了项目的花费”。

passages.name: 2021年考研英语一 Text 3
passages.title: 维多利亚时代的人拍照为何少有笑容
passages.genre: 说明文 · 历史与文化
passages.summary: 作者在Twitter上发布维多利亚时代的人面带微笑的照片，引起不小的轰动，但这类照片只占当时人像摄影作品极小的比例，大多数照片里的人神情愁苦、姿势僵硬，或目光茫然。摄影早期曝光时间很长，一直保持笑容让人吃不消；但到19世纪80年代曝光已快得多，90年代捕捉自然流露的笑容已相对容易，因此需要另找原因。一种可能的解释是，咧嘴笑会显得有失尊严：当时人们的口腔卫生常常很糟，露齿而笑显得没有格调，对有教养的人来说并不得体。

paras.en: As a historian who’s always searching for the text or the image that makes us re-evaluate the past, I’ve become preoccupied with looking for photographs that show our Victorian ancestors smiling (what better way to shatter the image of 19th-century prudery?).
paras.zh: 作为一名历史学家，我总在寻找能让我们重新评价过去的文字或图像；如今，我已一心扑在寻找我们维多利亚时代先辈的笑脸照片上（要打破19世纪拘谨古板的形象，还有什么比这更好的办法呢？）。

w.m: v. 重新评价；重新评估
一心扑在……上；全神贯注于
还有什么比这更好的办法来……

paras.en: I’ve found quite a few, and—since I started posting them on Twitter—they have been causing quite a stir.
paras.zh: 我已经找到了不少这样的照片，而且自从我开始把它们发到Twitter上，它们就一直引起不小的轰动。

paras.en: People have been surprised to see evidence that Victorians had fun and could, and did, laugh.
paras.zh: 人们惊讶地发现，有证据表明维多利亚时代的人也会找乐子，他们能笑，而且确实笑过。

w.m: n. 维多利亚时代的人

paras.en: They are noting that the Victorians suddenly seem to become more human as the hundred-or-so years that separate us fade away through our common experience of laughter.
paras.zh: 他们注意到，笑是我们与维多利亚时代的人共有的体验，隔开双方的一百来年时光由此渐渐淡去，那个时代的人似乎一下子变得更有血有肉了。

w.m: n. 维多利亚时代的人
adj. 有血有肉的；像常人一样（有喜怒哀乐）的
adj. 一百来（年）的；一百左右的

paras.en: Of course, I need to concede that my collection of “Smiling Victorians” makes up only a tiny percentage of the vast catalogue of photographic portraiture created between 1840 and 1900, the majority of which show sitters posing miserably and stiffly in front of painted backdrops, or staring absently into the middle distance.
paras.zh: 当然，我得承认，1840年至1900年间创作的人像摄影作品浩如烟海，我收集的“微笑的维多利亚人”只占其中极小的比例；这些作品大多呈现的是被拍摄者在彩绘背景布前愁眉苦脸、僵硬地摆着姿势，或者两眼放空、茫然地望着前方。

w.m: n. 收藏品；收集的东西
n. 人像（作品）；肖像艺术
n. （拍照或画像的）被拍摄者；模特
adj. 彩绘的；涂了颜料的
adv. 茫然地；心不在焉地
中景；（视野中）不远不近的地方

paras.en: How do we explain this trend?
paras.zh: 我们该如何解释这种倾向呢？

paras.en: During the 1840s and 1850s, in the early days of photography, exposure times were notoriously long: the daguerreotype photographic method (producing an image on a silvered copper plate) could take several minutes to complete, resulting in blurred images as sitters shifted position or adjusted their limbs.
paras.zh: 19世纪40年代和50年代正值摄影术发展早期，当时的曝光时间之长是出了名的：达盖尔银版摄影法（在镀银的铜板上成像）可能要好几分钟才能完成拍摄，结果被拍摄者一挪动位置或调整手脚，图像就模糊了。

w.m: adv. 出了名地；众所周知地
n. 达盖尔银版摄影法
n. （拍照或画像的）被拍摄者；模特

paras.en: The thought of holding a fixed grin as the camera performed its magical duties was too much to contemplate, and so a non-committal blank stare became the norm.
paras.zh: 相机施展神奇本领的时候，要一直咧着嘴保持笑容不变，光是想想就让人吃不消，于是，不流露任何情绪的木然凝视便成了常态。

w.m: adj. 不流露情绪的；不置可否的
adj. 木然的；没有表情的

paras.en: But exposure times were much quicker by the 1880s, and the introduction of the Box Brownie and other portable cameras meant that, though slow by today’s digital standards, the exposure was almost instantaneous.
paras.zh: 但到了19世纪80年代，曝光时间已经短得多了，而且随着布朗尼盒式相机和其他便携式相机问世，曝光几乎是一瞬间的事，尽管按今天的数码标准来看仍然算慢。

w.m: 布朗尼盒式相机（柯达公司推出的廉价相机）
adj. 便携式的；手提式的

paras.en: Spontaneous smiles were relatively easy to capture by the 1890s, so we must look elsewhere for an explanation of why Victorians still hesitated to smile.
paras.zh: 到了19世纪90年代，捕捉自然流露的笑容已经相对容易，所以，维多利亚时代的人为什么仍然迟迟不肯露出笑容，我们必须从别处寻找解释。

w.m: adj. 自然流露的；自发的
n. 维多利亚时代的人
迟迟不肯做；犹豫做某事

paras.en: One explanation might be the loss of dignity displayed through a cheesy grin.
paras.zh: 一种解释可能是：咧嘴傻笑会让人显得有失尊严。

paras.en: “Nature gave us lips to conceal our teeth,” ran one popular Victorian saying, alluding to the fact that before the birth of proper dentistry, mouths were often in a shocking state of hygiene.
paras.zh: 维多利亚时代有一句流行的俗语这样说：“大自然赐给我们嘴唇，是为了遮住牙齿。”这句话暗指这样一个事实：在正规的牙科医学诞生之前，人们的口腔卫生状况常常糟糕得惊人。

w.m: v. （文字、说法）写着；是这样说的
adj. 流行的；广为流传的
adj. 糟糕透顶的；骇人的

paras.en: A flashing set of healthy and clean, regular “pearly whites” was a rare sight in Victorian society, the preserve of the super-rich (and even then, dental hygiene was not guaranteed).
paras.zh: 在维多利亚时代的社会里，一口闪闪发亮、健康洁净又整齐的“珍珠白”牙齿难得一见，是超级富豪的专利（而且即便如此，牙齿卫生也未必有保障）。

paras.en: A toothy grin (especially when there were gaps or blackened teeth) lacked class: drunks, tramps, and music hall performers might gurn and grin with a smile as wide as Lewis Carroll’s gum-exposing Cheshire Cat, but it was not a becoming look for properly bred persons.
paras.zh: 露齿而笑（尤其是有豁牙或牙齿发黑时）显得没有格调：醉汉、流浪汉和歌舞杂耍剧场的艺人可能会做鬼脸、咧嘴笑，嘴咧得像刘易斯·卡罗尔笔下那只露出牙龈的柴郡猫一样宽，但对于有教养的人来说，这副模样并不得体。

w.m: 柴郡猫（童话《爱丽丝漫游奇境》里咧嘴笑的猫）

paras.en: Even Mark Twain, a man who enjoyed a hearty laugh, said that when it came to photographic portraits there could be “nothing more damning than a silly, foolish smile fixed forever”.
paras.zh: 马克·吐温是个爱开怀大笑的人，可就连他也说过，就人像照片而言，“没有什么比一张永远定格的傻乎乎、蠢兮兮的笑脸更要命的了”。

w.m: adj. 极其不利的；要命的

passages.name: 2021年考研英语一 Text 4
passages.title: 网络中立之争亟待国会出手
passages.genre: 议论文 · 科技与法律
passages.summary: 从宽带发展初期起，就有人担心宽带服务商有能力也有动机偏袒关联网站，因此一直有人强烈要求出台网络中立规则，但这一要求几乎无法得到满足。联邦通信委员会2017年的命令废除了严格的网络中立规则，并宣布州和地方政府也不得监管宽带服务商；上诉法院维持了这项命令，但驳回了委员会阻止所有州级网络中立规则的企图，同时保留了委员会的权力，使其仍可推翻有损其命令的个别州法律，争斗因此延续下去。作者认为，国会需要一劳永逸地赋予委员会明确的权力，禁止宽带服务商干预其网络上的流量，并制定保护网上开放与创新的清晰规则。

paras.en: From the early days of broadband, advocates for consumers and web-based companies worried that the cable and phone companies selling broadband connections had the power and incentive to favor affiliated websites over their rivals’.
paras.zh: 从宽带发展初期起，为消费者和网络公司代言的人士就担心，销售宽带接入服务的有线电视公司和电话公司既有能力也有动机偏袒自己的关联网站，而冷落竞争对手的网站。

w.m: adj. 基于网络的；网络的

paras.en: That’s why there has been such a strong demand for rules that would prevent broadband providers from picking winners and losers online, preserving the freedom and innovation that have been the lifeblood of the Internet.
paras.zh: 正因如此，人们才一直这么强烈地要求出台规则，阻止宽带服务商在网上决定谁胜谁负，从而维护自由与创新——这两者向来是互联网的命脉。

w.m: 这就是……的原因；正因如此
决定谁胜谁负；挑选赢家和输家

paras.en: Yet that demand has been almost impossible to fill—in part because of pushback from broadband providers, anti-regulatory conservatives and the courts.
paras.zh: 然而，这一要求至今几乎无法得到满足，部分原因在于宽带服务商、反对监管的保守派和法院的抵制。

w.m: n. 保守派；保守主义者

paras.en: A federal appeals court weighed in again Tuesday, but instead of providing a badly needed resolution, it only prolonged the fight.
paras.zh: 周二，一家联邦上诉法院再次介入此事，却没有给出急需的解决方案，只是让这场争斗拖得更久了。

paras.en: At issue before the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit was the latest take of the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) on net neutrality, adopted on a party-line vote in 2017.
paras.zh: 美国哥伦比亚特区巡回上诉法院审理的争议焦点，是联邦通信委员会（FCC）在网络中立问题上的最新方案，该方案于2017年在一次按党派划线的投票中获得通过。

w.m: n. （联邦法院的）巡回审判区
v. 通过（法规、决议）；采纳
按党派划线的投票（各成员完全按所属党派立场投票）

paras.en: The Republican-penned order not only eliminated the strict net neutrality rules the FCC had adopted when it had a Democratic majority in 2015, but rejected the commission’s authority to require broadband providers to do much of anything.
paras.zh: 这项由共和党人起草的命令不仅废除了联邦通信委员会2015年在民主党人占多数时通过的严格网络中立规则，还否定了该委员会的职权，认定它几乎无权要求宽带服务商做任何事。

w.m: adj. 由共和党人起草的
不仅（常与 but 连用：不仅……而且）
v. 通过（法规、决议）；采纳

paras.en: The order also declared that state and local governments couldn’t regulate broadband providers either.
paras.zh: 该命令还宣布，州和地方政府也不得监管宽带服务商。

paras.en: The commission argued that other agencies would protect against anti-competitive behavior, such as a broadband-providing conglomerate like AT&T favoring its own video-streaming service at the expense of Netflix and Apple TV.
paras.zh: 该委员会辩称，其他机构会防范反竞争行为，比如AT&T这类提供宽带服务的企业集团偏袒自家的视频流媒体服务，损害Netflix和Apple TV的利益。

paras.en: Yet the FCC also ended the investigations of broadband providers that imposed data caps on their rivals’ streaming services but not their own.
paras.zh: 然而，联邦通信委员会同时也终止了对一些宽带服务商的调查，这些服务商对竞争对手的流媒体服务设置了流量上限，对自家的却没有设。

paras.en: On Tuesday, the appeals court unanimously upheld the 2017 order deregulating broadband providers, citing a Supreme Court ruling from 2005 that upheld a similarly deregulatory move.
paras.zh: 周二，上诉法院一致裁定维持2017年那项放松宽带服务商监管的命令，并援引了最高法院2005年的一项裁决，该裁决维持了一项类似的放松监管举措。

w.m: adv. 一致地；全体一致地
v. 维持（原判、决定）；支持

paras.en: But Judge Patricia Millett rightly argued in a concurring opinion that “the result is unhinged from the realities of modern broadband service,” and said Congress or the Supreme Court could intervene to “avoid trapping Internet regulation in technological anachronism.”
paras.zh: 但帕特里夏·米利特法官在一份协同意见中正确地指出，“这一结果脱离了现代宽带服务的现实”，并表示国会或最高法院可以介入，以“避免让互联网监管困在技术上落后于时代的境地”。

w.m: 协同意见（赞同判决结果但理由不同的法官意见）
n. 时代错位；不合时宜的事物
v. 避免（后接动名词：avoid doing 避免做某事）

paras.en: In the meantime, the court threw out the FCC’s attempt to block all state rules on net neutrality, while preserving the commission’s power to preempt individual state laws that undermine its order.
paras.zh: 与此同时，法院驳回了联邦通信委员会阻止所有州级网络中立规则的企图，但保留了委员会的权力，使之仍可推翻有损其命令的个别州法律。

w.m: v. （以联邦法规）推翻，取代（州法）

paras.en: That means more battles like the one now going on between the Justice Department and California, which enacted a tough net neutrality law in the wake of the FCC’s abdication.
paras.zh: 这意味着还会有更多较量，就像司法部与加利福尼亚州之间正在进行的这场一样；在联邦通信委员会放弃职责之后，加州颁布了一部严格的网络中立法律。

paras.en: The endless legal battles and back-and-forth at the FCC cry out for Congress to act.
paras.zh: 面对无休止的法律较量和联邦通信委员会的反复摇摆，国会亟须采取行动。

w.m: adj. 无休止的；没完没了的
n. 反复摇摆；来回拉锯

paras.en: It needs to give the commission explicit authority once and for all to bar broadband providers from meddling in the traffic on their network and to create clear rules protecting openness and innovation online.
paras.zh: 国会需要一劳永逸地赋予该委员会明确的权力，使其得以禁止宽带服务商干预自家网络上的流量，并制定清晰的规则来保护网上的开放与创新。

passages.name: 2021年考研英语二 Text 1
passages.title: 再培训必不可少，费用该由谁出
passages.genre: 议论文 · 经济与就业
passages.summary: “再培训”听起来像个时髦词，实际上却是必要条件：有市场需求的工作岗位将迅速变化，留存岗位的要求也是如此。再培训该由谁出钱是个棘手的问题：单个企业总想辞退技能已不再有市场需求的员工、换上新人，但也有AT&T这样决定实施大规模再培训计划的企业；技能错配出现在整个经济层面时，人们通常把目光转向政府、指望政府来应对，而加拿大等地的努力可以说充其量只是有气无力。疫情之下失业率飙升，但并非所有用工短缺都已消失；再培训虽不能在几周内把失业的服务员培训成医生，却或许能填补其他缺口，在瑞典，北欧航空公司联合其他公司和当地一所大学，通过短期再培训让下岗员工协助医院工作人员，似乎就是这样的例子。

paras.en: “Reskilling” is something that sounds like a buzzword but is actually a requirement if we plan to have a future in which a lot of would-be workers do not get left behind.
paras.zh: “再培训”听起来像个时髦词，但如果我们打算迎来一个不让大批潜在劳动者掉队的未来，它实际上是一项必要条件。

w.m: n. 再培训；技能再培训
n. 必要条件；必需的事物
adj. 想要成为的；潜在的

paras.en: We know we are moving into a period where the jobs in demand will change rapidly, as will the requirements of the jobs that remain.
paras.zh: 我们知道，我们正步入这样一个时期：有市场需求的工作岗位将迅速变化，留存下来的岗位，其要求也会如此。

w.m: conj. 正如……一样（后接倒装：as will … ＝……也会如此）

paras.en: Research by the World Economic Forum finds that on average 42 percent of the “core skills” within job roles will change by 2022.
paras.zh: 世界经济论坛的研究发现，到2022年，各岗位的“核心技能”中平均将有42%发生变化。

paras.en: That is a very short timeline.
paras.zh: 这个时限非常短。

paras.en: The question of who should pay for reskilling is a thorny one.
paras.zh: 再培训应该由谁出钱，这个问题很棘手。

paras.en: For individual companies, the temptation is always to let go of workers whose skills are no longer in demand and replace them with those whose skills are.
paras.zh: 对单个企业来说，总会有这样一种诱惑：辞退技能已不再有市场需求的员工，换上技能有市场需求的人。

paras.en: That does not always happen.
paras.zh: 这种情况并不总会发生。

paras.en: AT&T is often given as the gold standard of a company that decided to do a massive reskilling program rather than go with a fire-and-hire strategy.
paras.zh: AT&T常被奉为标杆：这家公司决定实施大规模的再培训计划，而没有采用先解雇、再招聘的策略。

w.m: 把……作为（例子、典范）提出；举……为例

paras.en: Other companies have also pledged to create their own plans.
paras.zh: 其他公司也已承诺制定各自的计划。

paras.en: When the skills mismatch is in the broader economy, though, the focus usually turns to government to handle it.
paras.zh: 不过，技能错配一旦出现在整个经济层面，人们关注的焦点通常就会转向政府，由政府来应对。

w.m: 技能错配（技能供需不匹配）

paras.en: Efforts in Canada and elsewhere have been arguably languid at best, and have given us a situation where we frequently hear of employers begging for workers even at times and in regions where unemployment is high.
paras.zh: 加拿大和其他地方的努力，可以说充其量只是有气无力，还让我们陷入了这样一种局面：经常听说雇主苦求人手，即便在失业率高的时期和地区也是如此。

w.m: adv. 可以说；有理由认为
adj. 有气无力的；无精打采的

paras.en: With the pandemic, unemployment is very high indeed.
paras.zh: 疫情之下，失业率的确非常高。

paras.en: In February, at 3.5 percent and 5.5 percent respectively, unemployment rates in the U.S. and Canada were at generational lows and worker shortages were everywhere.
paras.zh: 2月份，美国和加拿大的失业率分别为3.5%和5.5%，处于一代人以来的低点，用工短缺随处可见。

paras.en: As of May, those rates had spiked up to 13.3 percent and 13.7 percent, and although many worker shortages had disappeared, not all had done so.
paras.zh: 截至5月，两国失业率已分别飙升至13.3%和13.7%；虽然许多用工短缺已经消失，但并非全都消失了。

paras.en: In the medical field, to take an obvious example, the pandemic meant that there were still clear shortages of doctors, nurses and other medical personnel.
paras.zh: 举一个明显的例子：在医疗领域，疫情使得医生、护士和其他医务人员依然明显短缺。

w.m: adj. 明显的；显而易见的

paras.en: Of course, it is not like you can take an unemployed waiter and train him to be a doctor in a few weeks.
paras.zh: 当然，又不是说你可以找来一个失业的服务员，用几周时间就把他培训成医生。

paras.en: But even if you cannot close the gap, maybe you can close others, and doing so would be to the benefit of all concerned.
paras.zh: 但即使填补不了这个缺口，或许也能填补别的缺口，而这样做会让所有相关方受益。

w.m: 所有相关的人；有关各方

paras.en: That seems to be the case in Sweden: When forced to furlough 90 percent of their cabin staff, Scandinavian Airlines decided to start up a short retraining program that reskilled the laid-off workers to support hospital staff.
paras.zh: 瑞典似乎就是这种情况：北欧航空公司在被迫让90%的客舱乘务人员停薪休假时，决定启动一项短期再培训计划，使这些下岗员工掌握新技能，去协助医院的工作人员。

w.m: v. 使停薪休假；让……暂时停职
v. 使掌握新技能；对……再培训
n. 工作人员；全体员工

paras.en: The effort was a collective one and involved other companies as well as a Swedish university.
paras.zh: 这是一次集体行动，参与者还包括其他公司以及瑞典的一所大学。

passages.name: 2021年考研英语二 Text 2
passages.title: 英国食物自给自足的设想难以实现
passages.genre: 议论文 · 农业与粮食安全
passages.summary: 全球人口预计到2050年将接近100亿，粮食安全日益成为新闻头条；在英国，脱欧也让这一话题备受关注，一些人认为脱欧是扭转英国越来越多地进口食物的趋势、回归自给自足的机会。但据利兹大学的报告，英国85%的国土与肉类和奶制品生产相关，这部分生产供应了国内肉类和奶制品消费量的80%；改为以植物性食物为主的饮食也无济于事，因为英国只有25%的土地适合种植农作物。即使采取最极端的措施，英国也只能满足30%的新鲜农产品需求，这还没考虑要为提供绝大部分热量的谷物、糖料、种子和油料作物寻找种植空间。

paras.en: With the global population predicted to hit close to 10 billion by 2050, and forecasts that agricultural production in some regions will need to nearly double to keep pace, food security is increasingly making headlines.
paras.zh: 全球人口预计到2050年将接近100亿，而且有预测称，一些地区的农业产量需要增长近一倍才能跟上人口增长的步伐；在这种情况下，粮食安全越来越多地登上新闻头条。

w.m: 登上头条新闻；成为新闻焦点

paras.en: In the UK, it has become a big talking point recently too, for a rather particular reason: Brexit.
paras.zh: 在英国，这一问题最近也成了热门话题，原因相当特别：脱欧。

paras.en: Brexit is seen by some as an opportunity to reverse a recent trend towards the UK importing food.
paras.zh: 一些人把脱欧视为一个机会，可以借此扭转近来英国越来越多地进口食物的趋势。

paras.en: The country produces only about 60 percent of the food it eats, down from almost three-quarters in the late 1980s.
paras.zh: 英国自己生产的食物只占其消费量的60%左右，而在20世纪80年代末，这一比例还接近四分之三。

paras.en: A move back to self-sufficiency, the argument goes, would boost the farming industry, political sovereignty and even the nation’s health.
paras.zh: 按照这种观点，回归自给自足会提振农业，增强政治主权，甚至改善国民健康。

w.m: n. 转变；转向（a move back to … 回归……）
按照这种观点；这种观点认为

paras.en: Sounds great—but how feasible is this vision?
paras.zh: 听起来很不错，但这一设想的可行性有多大呢？

paras.en: According to a report on UK food production from the University of Leeds, UK, 85 percent of the country’s total land area is associated with meat and dairy production.
paras.zh: 据英国利兹大学一份关于英国食物生产的报告，该国国土总面积的85%与肉类和奶制品生产相关。

paras.en: That supplies 80 percent of what is consumed, so even covering the whole country in livestock farms wouldn’t allow us to cover all our meat and dairy needs.
paras.zh: 这部分生产供应了国内肉类和奶制品消费量的80%，因此，即使让畜牧场遍布全国，也无法满足我们对肉类和奶制品的全部需求。

paras.en: There are many caveats to those figures, but they are still grave.
paras.zh: 这些数字虽然需要附加许多说明，但依然很严峻。

w.m: n. 附加说明；（需要注意的）限制条件

paras.en: To become much more self-sufficient, the UK would need to drastically reduce its consumption of animal foods, and probably also farm more intensively—meaning fewer green fields and more factory-style production.
paras.zh: 要大大提高自给程度，英国就需要大幅减少动物性食物的消费，而且可能还要更加集约化地经营农业——这意味着绿色田野会减少，工厂化生产会增加。

w.m: v. 从事农业生产；务农
adj. 工厂化的；工厂式的

paras.en: But switching to a mainly plant-based diet wouldn’t help.
paras.zh: 但改为以植物性食物为主的饮食不会有什么帮助。

w.m: adj. 以植物为主的；植物性的

paras.en: There is a good reason why the UK is dominated by animal husbandry: most of its terrain doesn’t have the right soil or climate to grow crops on a commercial basis.
paras.zh: 英国以畜牧业为主是有充分理由的：该国大部分地区都没有适合商业化种植农作物的土壤或气候。

w.m: 以商业化方式；在商业基础上

paras.en: Just 25 percent of the country’s land is suitable for crop-growing, most of which is already occupied by arable fields.
paras.zh: 英国只有25%的土地适合种植农作物，而其中大部分已经是耕地。

w.m: adj. 可耕种的；适于耕作的

paras.en: Even if we converted all the suitable land to fields of fruit and veg—which would involve taking out all the nature reserves and removing thousands of people from their homes—we would achieve only a 30 percent boost in crop production.
paras.zh: 即使我们把所有适合种植的土地都改造成果蔬田——这需要撤销所有自然保护区，让数以千计的人迁离家园——农作物产量也只能提高30%。

w.m: 成千上万的；数以千计的

paras.en: Just 23 percent of the fruit and vegetables consumed in the UK are currently home-grown, so even with the most extreme measures we could meet only 30 percent of our fresh produce needs.
paras.zh: 目前，英国消费的水果和蔬菜中只有23%是本土种植的，因此，即使采取最极端的措施，我们也只能满足30%的新鲜农产品需求。

w.m: adj. 本土种植的；自产的

paras.en: That is before we look for the space to grow the grains, sugars, seeds and oils that provide us with the vast bulk of our current calorie intake.
paras.zh: 这还没考虑要为种植谷物、糖料、种子和油料作物寻找空间，而目前我们摄入的热量绝大部分都来自这些作物。

passages.name: 2021年考研英语二 Text 3
passages.title: 科技巨头的小型收购引来监管关注
passages.genre: 说明文 · 商业与科技
passages.summary: 2015年，微软收购了两家在硅谷颇受热议的初创公司，后来弃用了这两家公司的应用，工程师团队则留了下来。批评者认为，大公司借这类交易，趁最具威胁的潜在竞争对手尚未壮大就将其买下，有时干脆关停。美国联邦贸易委员会已要求美国市值最高的五家科技公司提供过去十年间小型收购的信息；这目前还只是一个研究项目，但已让人想到一种可能：监管机构会介入早期科技市场。

paras.en: When Microsoft bought task management app Wunderlist and mobile calendar Sunrise in 2015, it picked up two newcomers that were attracting considerable buzz in Silicon Valley.
paras.zh: 2015年，微软收购了任务管理应用Wunderlist和移动日历Sunrise，将两家当时在硅谷颇受热议的新秀收入囊中。

paras.en: Microsoft’s own Office dominates the market for “productivity” software, but the start-ups represented a new wave of technology designed from the ground up for the smartphone world.
paras.zh: 微软自家的Office主导着“生产力”软件市场，而这两家初创公司代表的是专为智能手机时代从零设计的新一波技术。

paras.en: Both apps, however, were later scrapped after Microsoft said it had used their best features in its own products.
paras.zh: 然而，后来微软表示，已把这两款应用最好的功能用到了自家产品中，随后便将二者双双弃用。

paras.en: Their teams of engineers stayed on, making them two of the many “acqui-hires” that the biggest companies have used to feed their great hunger for tech talent.
paras.zh: 两家公司的工程师团队则留了下来，这样一来，这两笔收购就成了众多“人才收购”中的两例，而最大的几家公司一直靠这类收购来满足自己对科技人才的强烈渴求。

w.m: n. 人才收购（为招揽人才而收购公司）
n. 人才；（总称）有才能的人

paras.en: To Microsoft’s critics, the fates of Wunderlist and Sunrise are examples of a remorseless drive by Big Tech to chew up any innovative companies that lie in their path.
paras.zh: 在微软的批评者看来，Wunderlist和Sunrise的下场正是例证，说明科技巨头一心要无情地吞掉挡在自己路上的任何创新公司。

paras.en: “They bought the seedlings and closed them down,” complained Paul Arnold, a partner at San Francisco-based Switch Ventures, referring to deals that put an end to businesses that might one day turn into competitors.
paras.zh: “他们买下幼苗，然后就把它们关掉了。”总部位于旧金山的Switch Ventures公司合伙人保罗·阿诺德抱怨道。他所指的这些交易，让一些有朝一日可能成长为竞争对手的企业就此夭折。

paras.en: Microsoft declined to comment.
paras.zh: 微软拒绝置评。

paras.en: As with other start-up investors, Mr Arnold’s own business often depends on selling start-ups to larger tech companies, though he admits to mixed feelings about the result: “I think these things are good for me, if I put my selfish hat on.
paras.zh: 和其他初创公司投资人一样，阿诺德自己的生意也常常要靠把初创公司卖给更大的科技公司，不过他承认，自己对这种结果心情复杂：“要是从自私的角度考虑，我觉得这些事对我有好处。

paras.en: But are they good for the American economy?
paras.zh: 但它们对美国经济有好处吗？

paras.en: I don’t know.”
paras.zh: 我不知道。”

paras.en: The US Federal Trade Commission says it wants to find the answer to that question.
paras.zh: 美国联邦贸易委员会表示，希望找到这个问题的答案。

paras.en: This week, it asked the five most valuable US tech companies for information about their many small acquisitions over the past decade.
paras.zh: 本周，该委员会要求美国市值最高的五家科技公司提供各自过去十年间众多小规模收购的相关信息。

w.m: 要求某人提供某物；向某人索要某物
adj. 有价值的；（公司）市值高的

paras.en: Although only a research project at this stage, the request has raised the prospect of regulators wading into early-stage tech markets that until now have been beyond their reach.
paras.zh: 尽管现阶段这只是一个研究项目，但这一要求已让人想到一种可能：监管机构会介入早期科技市场，而迄今为止，它们对这些市场一直鞭长莫及。

w.m: 让人想到……的可能；带来……的前景
adj. 早期的；初期阶段的
超出……的能力（或权限）范围

paras.en: Given their combined market value of more than $5.5 trillion, rifling through such small deals—many of them much less prominent than Wunderlist and Sunrise—might seem beside the point.
paras.zh: 鉴于这五家公司的总市值超过5.5万亿美元，翻查这类小交易可能显得无关紧要——其中许多交易远不如Wunderlist和Sunrise那样引人注目。

w.m: adj. 引人注目的；著名的

paras.en: Between them, the five biggest tech companies have spent an average of only $3.4 billion a year on sub-$1 billion acquisitions over the past five years—a drop in the ocean compared with their massive financial reserves, and the more than $130 billion of venture capital that was invested in the US last year.
paras.zh: 过去五年间，最大的五家科技公司在金额低于10亿美元的收购上合计平均每年只花了34亿美元——与它们庞大的资金储备相比，与去年在美国投入的1300多亿美元风险资本相比，这都不过是沧海一粟。

paras.en: However, critics say the big companies use such deals to buy their most threatening potential competitors before their businesses have a chance to gain momentum, in some cases as part of a “buy and kill” tactic to simply close them down.
paras.zh: 然而，批评者说，大公司利用这类交易，趁最具威胁的潜在竞争对手的业务还没来得及发展壮大，就把它们买下来；有时这是“收购再扼杀”策略的一部分，目的就是干脆把它们关掉。

w.m: 获得发展势头；势头增强

passages.name: 2021年考研英语二 Text 4
passages.title: 有时直觉胜过深思熟虑
passages.genre: 说明文 · 心理与认知
passages.summary: 人们相当善于凭第一印象判断他人，而深思熟虑可能多余，甚至起干扰作用：在已故心理学家安巴迪的研究中，有一组参与者被要求先写下判断理由再评分，结果准确度大幅下降；其他研究也表明，人们依靠直觉而非反思时，更善于识破欺骗行为。想得太多还可能损害人们形成偏好的能力。不过，直觉的特殊威力只有在某些情况下才能释放出来：在一项研究中，依靠直觉使参与者在调动反思性思维的任务上表现变差，在调动直觉和创造力的任务上则表现更好。

paras.en: We’re fairly good at judging people based on first impressions, thin slices of experience ranging from a glimpse of a photo to a five-minute interaction, and deliberation can be not only extraneous but intrusive.
paras.zh: 我们相当善于凭第一印象判断他人，第一印象就是从经验中切下的薄片，短至瞥一眼照片，长至五分钟的互动；而深思熟虑不仅可能多余，还可能起干扰作用。

w.m: n. 深思熟虑；仔细考虑

paras.en: In one study of the ability she called “thin slicing,” the late psychologist Nalini Ambady asked participants to watch silent 10-second video clips of professors and to rate the instructor’s overall effectiveness.
paras.zh: 已故心理学家纳莉妮·安巴迪把这种能力称为“薄片撷取”，她在一项针对该能力的研究中，请参与者观看一些教授的10秒钟无声视频片段，并为授课者的整体教学效果打分。

w.m: 薄片撷取（凭零星片段迅速作出判断）

paras.en: Their ratings correlated strongly with students’ end-of-semester ratings.
paras.zh: 他们的评分与学生在学期末给出的评分高度相关。

paras.en: Another set of participants had to count backward from 1,000 by nines as they watched the clips, occupying their conscious working memory.
paras.zh: 另一组参与者在观看这些视频片段时，必须从1000开始每次减9倒着数，从而占用了他们有意识的工作记忆。

w.m: adj. 有意识的；意识到的

paras.en: Their ratings were just as accurate, demonstrating the intuitive nature of the social processing.
paras.zh: 他们的评分同样准确，这表明此类社会信息加工在本质上是凭直觉进行的。

paras.en: Critically, another group was asked to spend a minute writing down reasons for their judgment, before giving the rating.
paras.zh: 关键在于，还有一组参与者按要求先花一分钟写下自己作出判断的理由，然后再评分。

w.m: adv. 关键的是；至关重要地

paras.en: Accuracy dropped dramatically.
paras.zh: 准确度大幅下降。

paras.en: Ambady suspected that deliberation focused them on vivid but misleading cues, such as certain gestures or utterances, rather than letting the complex interplay of subtle signals form a holistic impression.
paras.zh: 安巴迪推测，深思熟虑使参与者把注意力集中在鲜明却具有误导性的线索上，比如特定的手势或话语，而不是让细微信号之间复杂的相互作用形成整体印象。

w.m: n. 深思熟虑；仔细考虑
adj. 误导性的；引入歧途的
n. 相互作用；相互影响

paras.en: She found similar interference when participants watched 15-second clips of pairs of people and judged whether they were strangers, friends, or dating partners.
paras.zh: 她发现，参与者观看一对对人物的15秒视频片段，并判断每对人是陌生人、朋友还是恋人时，也存在类似的干扰。

paras.en: Other research shows we’re better at detecting deception from thin slices when we rely on intuition instead of reflection.
paras.zh: 其他研究表明，我们依靠直觉而非反思时，更善于从零星片段（即“薄片”）中识破欺骗行为。

paras.en: “It’s as if you’re driving a stick shift,” says Judith Hall, a psychologist at Northeastern University, “and if you start thinking about it too much, you can’t remember what you’re doing.
paras.zh: 美国东北大学心理学家朱迪丝·霍尔说：“这就好比开手动挡的车，要是你开始在这上面想得太多，就会忘了自己在干什么。

paras.en: But if you go on automatic pilot, you’re fine.
paras.zh: 但要是你进入“自动驾驶”状态，就没问题。

w.m: 开启自动驾驶；（喻）不假思索地行事

paras.en: Much of our social life is like that.”
paras.zh: 我们的社交生活很大程度上就是这样。”

paras.en: Thinking too much can also harm our ability to form preferences.
paras.zh: 想得太多还可能损害我们形成偏好的能力。

paras.en: College students’ ratings of strawberry jams and college courses aligned better with experts’ opinions when the students weren’t asked to analyze their rationale.
paras.zh: 不要求大学生分析自己的评分理由时，他们对草莓酱和大学课程的评分与专家意见更为吻合。

paras.en: And people made car-buying decisions that were both objectively better and more personally satisfying when asked to focus on their feelings rather than on details, but only if the decision was complex—when they had a lot of information to process.
paras.zh: 另外，如果要求人们关注自己的感受而不是细节，他们做出的购车决定既在客观上更好，又让自己更满意，但前提是决定本身很复杂，即他们有大量信息需要处理。

w.m: adv. 对本人而言；就个人而言

paras.en: Intuition’s special powers are unleashed only in certain circumstances.
paras.zh: 直觉的特殊威力只有在某些情况下才能释放出来。

paras.en: In one study, participants completed a battery of eight tasks, including four that tapped reflective thinking (discerning rules, comprehending vocabulary) and four that tapped intuition and creativity (generating new products or figures of speech).
paras.zh: 在一项研究中，参与者完成了一组共八项任务，其中四项调动的是反思性思维（辨别规则、理解词汇），另外四项调动的是直觉和创造力（想出新产品或修辞表达）。

w.m: 修辞表达（如比喻）；修辞手法

paras.en: Then they rated the degree to which they had used intuition (“gut feelings,” “hunches,” “my heart”).
paras.zh: 随后，他们为自己运用直觉（“本能感觉”“预感”“我的内心”）的程度打分。

paras.en: Use of their gut hurt their performance on the first four tasks, as expected, and helped them on the rest.
paras.zh: 正如预期，依靠直觉拖累了他们在前四项任务上的表现，却让他们在其余任务上表现更好。

paras.en: Sometimes the heart is smarter than the head.
paras.zh: 有时候，心比头脑更聪明。

w.m: n. 心；内心（喻指感觉、直觉）
